caption: Fig. AC-1 Principle of air flow
description: Functional block diagram showing air driven by blower motor splitting through heater core and evaporator to supply cabin temperature control.
mechanic_notes: Illustrates how airflow splits between heating and cooling elements before entering the cabin distribution ducts.

caption: Fig. AC-2 Sectional view of air conditioner
description: Cutaway perspective view of the under-dash air conditioning package showing air intake housing, blower assembly, evaporator core, heater core, control doors, actuators, and air delivery ducting.
mechanic_notes: Shows structural relationship and mounting positions of under-dash HVAC housings: intake housing on passenger side, blower housing, and evaporator/heater housing.

caption: Fig. AC-3 Refrigeration cycle
description: Schematic layout of the closed-loop R-12 refrigeration cycle showing compressor, condenser, receiver drier, expansion valve, and evaporator with shading indicating pressure and state changes.

callouts.High pressure gas: Refrigerant vapor between compressor discharge and condenser
callouts.High pressure liquid: Condensed liquid refrigerant from condenser through receiver drier to expansion valve
callouts.Low pressure liquid: Atomized low-pressure liquid spray emerging from expansion valve into evaporator
callouts.Low pressure gas: Vaporized refrigerant leaving evaporator core returning to compressor suction port

mechanic_notes: Heat absorbed from cabin air at evaporator is pumped by compressor to condenser where it is transferred to outside airflow.

caption: Fig. AC-4 Receiver drier
description: Cross-sectional cutaway diagram of the receiver drier tank showing liquid pick-up tube, desiccant bed, strainer screens, sight glass, and top-mounted high-pressure safety switch.
wiring_and_connections: Electrical harness connector to pressure switch
mechanic_notes: Excess liquid refrigerant is held in tank while central pick-up tube draws clean, dehydrated liquid from bottom through strainer and desiccant.

caption: Fig. AC-5 Expansion valve
description: Cross-sectional cutaway illustration of the thermostatic expansion valve detailing valve housing, thermo bulb, diaphragm, valve ball, orifice, equalizer, and O-ring seal.
mechanic_notes: Sensing bulb pressure acts against diaphragm to modulate valve ball against calibrated orifice, regulating superheat entering evaporator.

caption: Fig. AC-6 Air flow - OFF position
description: Schematic of air ducting and vacuum control circuits in OFF position with blower motor unpowered and vacuum source magnet valve de-energized.

callouts.S: Vacuum supply port on selector valve

wiring_and_connections: Vacuum circuit vented through de-energized vacuum source magnet valve
mechanic_notes: When FAN lever is OFF, the vacuum source magnet valve vents the entire selector valve network to atmospheric pressure.

caption: Fig. AC-7 Air flow - A/C (Air Conditioner) position
description: Schematic routing of air flow and vacuum lines in A/C mode showing recirculated air cooling through evaporator, fast idle actuator energized, and vacuum cock shutting hot water off.
measurements_and_specs: FAN lever: In any position other than OFF
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum applied to vacuum cock and F.I.C.D. actuator; ports D1, D2, and I vented
mechanic_notes: Vacuum cock cuts hot coolant flow to heater core. Air intake door closes to outside air to maximize cabin recirculation cooling.

caption: Fig. AC-8 Air flow - VENT (Ventilation) position
description: Schematic routing of airflow and vacuum in VENT mode with fresh air intake door open, compressor unpowered, mode door closed, and air discharged through dashboard vents.
measurements_and_specs: FAN lever: In any position other than OFF
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum routed from port S to port I and vacuum cock
mechanic_notes: Directs fresh outside air through dashboard vents without heating or refrigeration.

caption: Fig. AC-9 Air flow - BI-LEVEL position
description: Schematic of airflow and vacuum in BI-LEVEL position where vacuum energizes stage D1 of mode door actuator, discharging cool fresh air to face vents and heated air to footwell.
measurements_and_specs: FAN lever: In any position other than OFF
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum applied to port I and port D1; port D2 vented
mechanic_notes: First stage of double-action actuator holds mode door halfway open to split airflow between dash vents and floor heater core.

caption: Fig. AC-10 Air flow - HEAT position
description: Schematic of airflow and vacuum in HEAT mode showing vacuum applied to both D1 and D2 ports, opening mode door fully to pass outside air through heater core to floor.
measurements_and_specs: FAN lever: In any position other than OFF
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum applied to ports I, D1, D2, and vacuum cock
mechanic_notes: Both D1 and D2 ports are energized, causing maximum travel of mode door so all incoming fresh air passes through heater core.

caption: Fig. AC-11 Air flow - REC HEAT position
description: Schematic routing of airflow and vacuum in REC HEAT mode with intake door closed to outside air, recirculating passenger cabin air through heater core for rapid warmup.
measurements_and_specs: AIR lever: In REC HEAT position
FAN lever: In any position other than OFF
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum applied to D1, D2, and vacuum cock; port I vented
mechanic_notes: Port I is vented to close intake door to outside air, recycling passenger compartment air across the heater core.

caption: Fig. AC-12 Air flow - DEF (Defrost) position
description: Schematic of airflow and vacuum in DEF mode with outside air admitted, mode door fully open, and heater door mechanically closed to footwell, directing all warm air to defroster nozzles.
measurements_and_specs: FAN lever: In any position other than OFF
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum applied to I, D1, D2, and vacuum cock
mechanic_notes: A mechanical control cable linked directly to the AIR lever forces the heater door shut, blocking floor distribution and directing heated air exclusively to windshield defroster nozzles.

caption: Fig. AC-13 Check valve
description: Cross-sectional cutaway drawing of vacuum check valve in open and closed positions, displaying rubber plate flapper and porous plastic filter.

callouts.Valve open: Negative pressure on engine side 20 mm Hg higher than vacuum tank
callouts.Valve closed: Manifold pressure higher than vacuum tank, preventing reverse flow

measurements_and_specs: Opening pressure differential: 20 mm Hg (4/5 in Hg)
mechanic_notes: Maintains stored vacuum inside reservoir during acceleration when manifold vacuum drops.

caption: Fig. AC-14 Magnet valve
description: Cross-sectional cutaway illustration of three-way solenoid magnet valve in energized (valve open to vacuum tank) and de-energized (valve closed, open to atmosphere) conditions.
measurements_and_specs: Actuation vacuum: 200 mm Hg (8 in Hg)
mechanic_notes: When energized, needle lifts connecting selector side to vacuum tank. When de-energized, spring pushes needle down, isolating tank and venting selector line to atmosphere.

caption: Fig. AC-15 Vacuum selector valve
description: Top perspective diagram of rotary faceplate vacuum selector valve showing port nipples S, D1, D2, and I.

callouts.S: Vacuum source line from magnet valve

wiring_and_connections: Hose S from vacuum source magnet valve
Hose D1 to mode door actuator stage 1
Hose D2 to mode door actuator stage 2
Hose I to air intake door actuator
mechanic_notes: Mechanically actuated by the AIR control lever; channels vacuum across grooved mating faceplates to drive HVAC mode doors.

caption: Fig. AC-16 Electrical circuit
description: Full electrical schematic showing circuit routing for OFF position, A/C position, and other HVAC positions (VENT, BI-LEVEL, HEAT, REC HEAT, DEF).

callouts.*1: When AIR lever is in A/C position, micro switch is ON.
callouts.*2: May be on or off by switching thermostat on or off

wiring_and_connections: Battery positive feed through ignition switch to ignition relay
Ignition relay power feed to blower motor and vacuum source magnet valve
Blower resistor tapped speeds grounded through blower control switch
Compressor relay coil circuit in series with micro switch, thermostat, pressure switch, and blower ground
Compressor relay output to compressor clutch and FICD magnet valve
mechanic_notes: Ground-controlled circuit architecture. Compressor clutch and FICD cannot engage unless blower fan is running, micro switch is closed in A/C position, thermostat calls for cooling, and high pressure switch is closed.

caption: Fig. AC-17 Manifold gauge
description: Cutaway diagram of dual-dial service manifold gauge block showing low-pressure compound gauge, high-pressure gauge, hand valves, back-seated vs front-seated seating, and port fittings.
components: To vacuum pump or refrigerant can fitting

callouts.Front-seated (Full clockwise): Valve seated, blocking passage between service port and center fitting

mechanic_notes: Turning hand valves clockwise (front-seated) isolates gauge ports from center charging line; turning counter-clockwise (back-seated) connects port to center line.

caption: Fig. AC-18 Service valve
description: Sectional cutaway of service Schrader-style check valve displaying cap, internal valve core, rubber packing, and charging hose flare connection in closed and open states.
mechanic_notes: Check valve opens automatically when charging hose is coupled. The metal cap provides primary leak sealing and prevents vacuum ingestion during high-speed driving; do not overtighten.

caption: Fig. AC-19 Can tap
description: Cross-sectional cutaway of refrigerant can tap clamp and puncturing needle mechanism showing clockwise piercing position and counterclockwise dispensing position.
wiring_and_connections: Charging hose connection to manifold gauge center fitting
mechanic_notes: Turning handle clockwise forces piercing needle through metal can seal; turning counterclockwise retracts needle to release pressurized refrigerant gas into charging hose.

caption: Fig. AC-20 Purging air
description: Procedure diagram demonstrating purging trapped atmospheric air from center charging hose by cracking flare nut at manifold gauge center fitting.
wiring_and_connections: Center hose connected between can tap and manifold gauge block
mechanic_notes: Crack center flare nut loose for 2-3 seconds until pure refrigerant vapor escapes, expelling all atmospheric air and moisture from hose before opening manifold valves.

caption: Fig. AC-21 Discharging system
description: Service hookup illustration showing manifold gauge set connected to compressor service valves with center hose venting refrigerant vapor slowly into atmosphere.
measurements_and_specs: Discharge rate: Slow controlled bleed to prevent oil loss
wiring_and_connections: Blue hose to low-pressure suction service valve
Red hose to high-pressure discharge service valve
Yellow center hose directed to waste exhaust
mechanic_notes: Open gauge hand wheels only slightly to prevent foaming refrigerant from carrying compressor lubricant out of system.

caption: Fig. AC-22 Evacuating system - First step
description: Initial evacuation step showing vacuum pump operating with only low-pressure valve open until compound gauge reaches 500 mm Hg (20 in Hg).
measurements_and_specs: Target vacuum: 500 mm Hg (20 in Hg)
wiring_and_connections: Low-pressure valve open, high-pressure valve closed, center hose to vacuum pump
mechanic_notes: Evacuate through low-pressure side first to avoid pulling liquid lubricant out of compressor.

caption: Fig. AC-23 Evacuating system - Second step
description: Second evacuation step showing high-pressure valve opened in addition to low-pressure valve, pulling deep vacuum down to 710 mm Hg (28 in Hg).
measurements_and_specs: Target vacuum: 710 mm Hg (28 in Hg)
wiring_and_connections: Both high- and low-pressure valves open to vacuum pump
mechanic_notes: Once 500 mm Hg is reached, open high-pressure valve to fully evacuate high side down to 710 mm Hg; hold for 5-10 min to check vacuum retention.

caption: Fig. AC-24 Charging refrigerant
description: Initial refrigerant charging procedure showing upright R-12 can connected to manifold gauge, feeding vapor into both high- and low-pressure service ports of evacuated system.
wiring_and_connections: Can tap center hose to manifold; both high and low hand valves open
mechanic_notes: Engine remains off. Deep vacuum in system draws refrigerant vapor into both sides.

caption: Fig. AC-25 Charging refrigerant
description: Illustration of refrigerant can immersed in warm water bath to elevate vapor pressure and maintain charging speed.
wiring_and_connections: Charging hose to manifold center port
mechanic_notes: WARNING: Never heat with an open flame, torch, or stove. Never exceed 52°C (126°F) to avoid container explosion.

caption: Fig. AC-26 Charging refrigerant
description: Liquid charging setup showing inverted R-12 can feeding liquid refrigerant strictly into high-pressure discharge service valve with engine off.
measurements_and_specs: Compressor rotation: Turn several times manually by hand after charging
wiring_and_connections: High-pressure manifold valve open, low-pressure manifold valve tightly closed
mechanic_notes: CRITICAL: Never charge liquid through low side. Never run engine while liquid charging. Rotate compressor clutch disc by hand several times after charging to expel liquid from cylinders.

caption: Fig. AC-27 Charging refrigerant
description: Gas charging method with engine running below 1,500 rpm, drawing refrigerant gas into compressor suction port while throttling low-pressure valve.
measurements_and_specs: Low-pressure gauge limit: 2.8 kg/cm² (40 psi) or less
wiring_and_connections: Low-pressure valve throttle-controlled, high-pressure valve strictly closed
mechanic_notes: DANGER: High-pressure valve MUST be closed. Opening high-pressure valve while compressor runs will pump extreme pressure into the can and cause it to explode.

caption: Fig. AC-28 Charging refrigerant
description: Weighing refrigerant can and tap on a mechanical scale during charging to meter exact factory charge weight.
measurements_and_specs: Specified total charge: 0.7 to 0.9 kg (1.5 to 2.0 lb)
mechanic_notes: Weigh can before and during charging to determine exact charge. Overcharging elevates discharge pressure and impairs cooling efficiency.

caption: Fig. AC-29 Checking for leaks
description: Halide leak detector torch assembly showing gas cylinder, burner chimney, flame adjuster, copper reaction plate, and flexible sampling wand.
mechanic_notes: Refrigerant gas is heavier than air; hold probe directly underneath fittings and joints. Color shift from greenish-blue to yellow/green indicates small leak; brilliant purple/vivid green indicates large leak. WARNING: Phosgene gas produced by burning refrigerant is toxic; ventilate work area well.

caption: Sight glass: Almost no refrigerant (bubbles flow continuously)
description: Sight glass view showing continuous streams of bubbles indicating almost no refrigerant in system.
mechanic_notes: Bubbles disappear and mist flows when refrigerant is nearly empty.

caption: Sight glass: Insufficient refrigerant (bubbles at 1-2 sec intervals)
description: Sight glass view with bubbles visible at intervals of 1 to 2 seconds, indicating insufficient charge.
mechanic_notes: Check for leakage, repair as required, replenish and charge system.

caption: Sight glass: Suitable / Too much refrigerant (clear/no bubbles)
description: Sight glass view showing transparent liquid stream with no bubbles, indicating either proper charge or overcharge.
mechanic_notes: Visual appearance is identical between suitable charge and overcharge; verify with pressure gauges.

caption: Fig. AC-30 Compressor
description: Exploded view of compressor mounting bracket and bolts attaching compressor assembly to engine block.

callouts.A: Tightening torque: 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Bracket bolt tightening torque: 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten mounting bolts to 4.5 - 5.5 kg-m (33 - 40 ft-lb). Hand crank compressor before running if tilted.

caption: Fig. AC-31 Idler pulley
description: Exploded view of A/C idler pulley assembly, bracket, tension adjusting screw, and locking nut.

callouts.A: 0.9 to 1.2 kg-m (6.5 to 8.7 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque A: 0.9 to 1.2 kg-m (6.5 to 8.7 ft-lb)
Tightening torque B: 2.2 to 3.0 kg-m (16 to 22 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten bracket bolt B to 2.2-3.0 kg-m and adjusting lock nut A to 0.9-1.2 kg-m.

caption: Fig. AC-32 Belt tension
description: Belt drive routing diagram showing deflection check points for compressor drive belt and alternator belt.
measurements_and_specs: Belt deflection: 8 to 12 mm (0.31 to 0.47 in) under moderate thumb pressure
mechanic_notes: Measure belt deflection midway between pulleys. Adjust by turning idler pulley bolt.

caption: Fig. AC-33 Removing condenser
description: Front radiator support and condenser mounting bolt locations during removal.
mechanic_notes: Add 28 g (1 oz) compressor oil if replacing with new condenser.

caption: Fig. AC-34 Pipe connection
description: Flare tube and seat surface connection showing oil coating requirement and two-wrench method.
mechanic_notes: Coat seat surfaces with compressor oil and tighten using two wrenches.

caption: Fig. AC-35 Refrigeration line
description: Complete vehicle refrigeration piping layout showing condenser, compressor, receiver drier, strainer, service valves, and line torques.

callouts.A: Tightening torque: 4.5 to 5.0 kg-m (33 to 36 ft-lb)
callouts.B: Tightening torque: 3.0 to 3.5 kg-m (22 to 25 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Torque A (flexible hose / compressor unions): 4.5 to 5.0 kg-m (33 to 36 ft-lb)
Torque B (receiver drier / strainer fittings): 3.0 to 3.5 kg-m (22 to 25 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Coat seating surfaces with compressor oil. Clamp lines securely to avoid vibration.

caption: Fig. AC-36 Fast idle actuator
description: F.I.C.D. vacuum actuator and adjustable linkage lever mounted on intake manifold throttle linkage.
measurements_and_specs: Engine idle speed with A/C ON: 800 rpm
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum hose to F.I.C.D. solenoid valve
mechanic_notes: Adjust lever stroke length until idle speed stabilizes at 800 rpm with A/C engaged.

caption: Fig. AC-37 Removing blower motor
description: Blower motor mounting screws and removal from underneath the passenger dashboard blower housing.
mechanic_notes: Three spacers are inserted between motor and housing. Do not lose them.

caption: Fig. AC-38 Air intake door actuator
description: Air intake door vacuum actuator installed on air intake duct housing with lever and snap ring.
mechanic_notes: Ensure air intake door shuts off outside air completely when actuated.

caption: Fig. AC-39 Removing blower housing
description: Blower housing mounting bolt locations under dashboard on passenger side.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect vacuum hose from air intake door actuator before dropping housing.

caption: Fig. AC-40 Removing heater door rod
description: Disconnection of heater door operating rod from heater core box.
mechanic_notes: Keep heater door open when removing or installing core to avoid damaging core fins.

caption: Fig. AC-41 Mode door actuator
description: Mode door vacuum actuator installed on heater housing showing dual vacuum ports and linkage arm.
mechanic_notes: Remove snap ring from tip of actuator lever before removing mounting screws.

caption: Fig. AC-42 Removing finisher
description: Removal of center console cluster finisher bezel and disconnect points for wire harness.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect finisher harness connectors before withdrawing finisher completely.

caption: Fig. AC-43 Removing control assembly
description: Control panel assembly mounting points showing upper screws and lower E-ring attachment.
mechanic_notes: Remove upper screws and E-ring to pull control assembly out from dash frame.

caption: Fig. AC-44 Exploded view of control assembly
description: Exploded view of the A/C control panel assembly detailing internal electrical switches, vacuum valve, and bracket components.
mechanic_notes: Route wiring carefully through harness clamp (5) upon reassembly.

caption: Fig. AC-45 Removing capillary tube
description: Capillary tube mounting bracket and routing across heater unit housing.
mechanic_notes: Ensure heater cock is fully open when bending capillary tube.

caption: Fig. AC-46 Thermostat
description: Thermostat switch body with sensing capillary tube inserted into evaporator case core.
measurements_and_specs: Capillary tube insertion depth: 50 to 70 mm (1.97 to 2.76 in)
mechanic_notes: Do not bend capillary tube too sharply; insert 50 to 70 mm into evaporator core.

caption: Fig. AC-47 Removing expansion valve
description: Expansion valve removal from evaporator case showing flare nut tube connection and mounting nuts.
mechanic_notes: Insert valve parallelly without twisting to avoid damaging O-rings.

caption: Fig. AC-48 O-ring
description: Expansion valve mounting flange and replacement O-rings with insertion orientation arrows.
mechanic_notes: Always replace O-rings with new ones and lubricate with clean compressor oil.

caption: Fig. AC-49 Removing finisher brackets
description: Removal of finisher support brackets and instrument panel reinforcement brace.
mechanic_notes: Remove brackets and brace to access 3-way air duct and evaporator casing.

caption: Fig. AC-50 Removing instrument panel center stays
description: Structural center stays of instrument panel supporting evaporator housing and center dash.
components: Instrument panel center stays (left and right)
mechanic_notes: Unbolt stays to free evaporator assembly.

caption: Fig. AC-51 Removing evaporator housing
description: Lower mounting bolts holding evaporator housing to the vehicle dashboard framing.
mechanic_notes: Remove two lower bolts to allow evaporator housing to drop down.

caption: Fig. AC-52 Exploded view of evaporator housing
description: Exploded view of evaporator housing assembly showing casing shells, core, expansion valve, and retaining clips.
measurements_and_specs: Compressor oil addition: 28 g (1 oz) for new evaporator core
mechanic_notes: Cut sealing packing with knife between cases. Clean nicotine and dirt to prevent odors.

caption: Fig. AC-53 Removing heater unit
description: Heater unit mounting bolts and bracket locations under center instrument panel.
mechanic_notes: Insert heater unit into dashboard opening with cock facing engine, then rotate 90 degrees.

caption: Fig. AC-54 Vacuum hose diagram
description: Comprehensive schematic of the air conditioning vacuum distribution system including vacuum tank, check valve, solenoid valves, selector valve, actuators, and hose stripe color codes.
mechanic_notes: Pay strict attention to hose stripe color markings (N, Y, W) when reconnecting vacuum lines.

caption: Fig. AC-55 Wiring harness diagram
description: Pictorial layout of A/C wiring harnesses in engine compartment and dashboard showing connectors, switches, relays, and resistor.
wiring_and_connections: Blue single lead wire to compressor magnetic clutch
mechanic_notes: Verify connector latching and ground connection at body ground points.

caption: Fig. AC-56 Circuit diagram for air conditioner
description: Complete electrical schematic diagram of the A/C control circuits including compressor clutch, pressure switch, vacuum magnet valves, blower switch, resistor, and relays.
measurements_and_specs: Fuses: 10A, 15A, 20A ratings as shown in fuse block
wiring_and_connections: B, BG, W, WR, Y, YR, L, LB, LW, LR, LY, LG, LB/W color coding
mechanic_notes: Trace power from battery through fusible link to starter motor and ignition relay before diagnosing individual components.

caption: Fig. AC-57 Circuit diagram for illumination lamp
description: Wiring diagram for the air conditioner control panel illumination lamp, dimmer rheostat, lighting switch, and fuse block.
wiring_and_connections: B (Black), W (White), WR (White/Red), RL (Red/Blue), GW (Green/White), GL (Green/Blue)
mechanic_notes: Rheostat regulates lamp ground/resistance for dash illumination dimming.

caption: Air Conditioner Diagnoses Chart
description: Comprehensive troubleshooting decision tree for air conditioner problems including insufficient cooling, noise, pressure abnormalities, and sight glass bubbles.
measurements_and_specs: Outside 70°F: Suction 20-28 psi, Head 138-168 psi, Temp diff 18-24°F
Outside 80°F: Suction 23-33 psi, Head 152-185 psi, Temp diff 19-26°F
Outside 90°F: Suction 28-38 psi, Head 175-209 psi, Temp diff 23-30°F
Outside 100°F: Suction 37-48 psi, Head 201-235 psi, Temp diff 27-35°F
mechanic_notes: Always check dash panel grommets and seals if discharge air temp is abnormal but pressures are within normal spec.

caption: Insufficient Refrigerant Charge Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for insufficient refrigerant charge: Low pressure ~ 10 psi (normal 28-38), High pressure ~ 115 psi (normal 175-209).
mechanic_notes: Both low and high pressures are lower than normal shaded area; bubbles visible in sight glass.

caption: Almost No Refrigerant Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for severe refrigerant loss: Low pressure in deep vacuum (~ -10 psi), High pressure ~ 35 psi.
mechanic_notes: Stop compressor immediately to avoid burning out compressor from oil starvation.

caption: Faulty Expansion Valve Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for restricted/stuck closed expansion valve: Low pressure in vacuum, High pressure low (~ 70 psi).
mechanic_notes: Expansion valve inlet sweats or frosts when restriction occurs.

caption: Expansion Valve Over-Discharge Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for over-metering expansion valve: Low pressure abnormally high (~ 45 psi), High pressure normal/high (~ 220 psi).
mechanic_notes: Suction line shows heavy sweating when expansion valve allows excess refrigerant.

caption: Faulty Expansion Valve O-Ring Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for leaking expansion valve O-ring: Low pressure high (~ 55 psi), High pressure elevated (~ 250 psi).
mechanic_notes: Frosting or sweating suction line indicates refrigerant bypass past O-ring seal.

caption: Air In System Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for air contamination: Low pressure elevated (~ 40 psi), High pressure very high (~ 260 psi).
mechanic_notes: Both pressures are abnormally high, and occasional bubbles appear in sight glass.

caption: Moisture In System Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for moisture freezing in expansion valve: Suction gauge fluctuates with 0.4 kg/cm² (6 psi) needle vibration before pulling into vacuum.
mechanic_notes: Perform 30-minute evacuation three consecutive times to boil out moisture after drier replacement.

caption: Faulty Condenser Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for insufficient condenser airflow/cooling: Both low pressure (~ 45 psi) and head pressure (~ 280 psi) excessively high.
mechanic_notes: Suction line is very hot and engine may overheat. Clean condenser fins with water.

caption: High Pressure Line Blocked Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for clogged receiver drier or line restriction: Suction drops into vacuum, Head pressure drops to ~ 70 psi.
mechanic_notes: High pressure liquid line frosts after the point of restriction.

caption: Faulty Compressor Gauge Reading
description: Manifold gauge readings for damaged compressor valves/gaskets: Suction pressure very high (~ 60 psi) while discharge pressure is very low (~ 100 psi).
mechanic_notes: Compressor fails to pump; high suction with low discharge indicates failed internal reed valves or gaskets.

caption: Blower Motor Diagnoses Flowchart
description: Logic flowchart for diagnosing an inoperative blower motor through fuse check, ground wire bypass, resistor check, and test light probing.
mechanic_notes: Ground blower speed switch leads sequentially to isolate open circuits or faulty switch contacts.

caption: Compressor Diagnoses Flowchart
description: Troubleshooting tree for compressor malfunctions covering clutch slipping, low voltage, seizure, oil leaks, high torque, and operating noise.
mechanic_notes: If clutch coil voltage is below 10.5V, check coil ground terminal connection before replacing clutch.

caption: Compressor Clutch Diagnoses Flowchart
description: Systematic electrical troubleshooting procedure for compressor clutch non-engagement using a 12V test light through fuse, switch, and thermostat stages.
mechanic_notes: Ensure AIR lever is set to A/C position when testing blower speed switch terminal.

caption: Pressure switch and compressor relay diagnostic procedure flowchart
description: Diagnostic logic tree for testing the pressure switch and compressor relay circuit using a 12-volt test light connected to the yellow wire.
wiring_and_connections: Yellow wire leading to pressure switch
Compressor relay electric power source wire
mechanic_notes: If the test light is OFF, check for open circuit on compressor relay power source wire, and inspect the relay and fuse. Blower motor also will not operate if the relay or fuse is faulty.

caption: Vacuum system diagnoses — A/C position flowchart
description: Diagnostic flowchart for troubleshooting vacuum circuits in A/C mode when air comes out of improper outlets or fails to discharge from A/C outlets.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum tester light keeps OFF unless normal vacuum level exists in each check point.
wiring_and_connections: Air intake door actuator vacuum hose
mechanic_notes: Tester light remains OFF unless specified vacuum level is reached. When removing actuator hose normalizes operation, inspect vacuum selector valve and hose connections. If not normalized, inspect return spring or actuator diaphragm.

caption: Fast Idle Control Device Diagnoses (FICD) flowchart
description: Diagnostic tree for investigating failure of the Fast Idle Control Device (FICD) to operate, isolating actuator, magnet valve electrical circuit, vacuum tank, check valve, and plumbing.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum tester light keeps OFF unless normal vacuum level exists in each check point.
wiring_and_connections: Blue wire leading to FICD magnet valve terminal
Vacuum hose at inlet side of FICD magnet valve
mechanic_notes: Connect 12V test light to blue wire terminal on FICD magnet valve. If light is OFF, refer to Compressor Clutch Diagnoses.

caption: Vacuum system diagnoses-VENT position flowchart
description: Troubleshooting tree for vacuum controls in VENT position, assessing ventilation discharge, mode door actuator D1 and D2, air intake door actuator, vacuum selector valve hose S, magnet valve, and vacuum storage.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum tester light keeps OFF unless normal vacuum level exists in each check point.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect hose S from vacuum selector valve and connect to vacuum tester. If light is ON, check hose for twist/leak; replace selector valve if hose is good.

caption: Vacuum system diagnoses - BI-LEVEL position flowchart
description: Troubleshooting tree for vacuum controls in BI-LEVEL position, determining whether air discharges only from heater outlets, only from A/C outlets, or fails to bring outside air in.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum tester light keeps OFF unless normal vacuum level exists in each check point.
mechanic_notes: When air discharges from heater outlets alone, disconnect hose D2 of mode door actuator. If normalized, check selector valve piping; if not, check return spring and actuator.

caption: Vacuum system diagnoses - HEAT position flowchart
description: Diagnostic flowchart for heating mode failures, including recirculating air door sticking, lack of hot air due to water cock/vacuum cock, and closed heater door or mode door malfunction.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum tester light keeps OFF unless normal vacuum level exists in each check point.
mechanic_notes: Inspect water cock mechanical control wire before replacing vacuum cock. If heater door is closed, check and replace heater door wire.

caption: Vacuum system diagnoses - REC HEAT position flowchart
description: Diagnostic tree for recirculating heat operation, covering air intake door opening, failure to supply hot air, closed heater door, and mode door actuator malfunctions.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum tester light keeps OFF unless normal vacuum level exists in each check point.
mechanic_notes: In REC HEAT, the air intake door should isolate outside air. If outside air is admitted, check actuator return spring and selector valve.

caption: Vacuum system diagnoses - DEFROST position flowchart
description: Diagnostic flowchart for DEFROST position, testing issues when air does not discharge from defroster nozzles, discharges partially, or fails to warm up.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum tester light keeps OFF unless normal vacuum level exists in each check point.
mechanic_notes: If air comes out only a little, check if mode door is only half operative by connecting vacuum tester to hose D2 of the double actuator.

caption: Fig. AC-58 Sectional view
description: Cross-sectional engineering view of Model SWP123 swash plate compressor detailing internal cylinder, swash plate, drive balls, shoe discs, oil pump, and electromagnetic clutch.
mechanic_notes: Reciprocating pistons driven by swash plate rotation provide high cooling capacity and mechanical balance.

caption: Fig. AC-59 Exploded view
description: Complete exploded diagram of Model SWP123 swash plate compressor and clutch assembly showing component arrangement and fastening order.
components: Rear end cover fixing bolt and washer

callouts.15: Rear end cover fixing bolt and washer

mechanic_notes: Discard all old gaskets, O-rings, and shaft seals upon disassembly.

caption: Fig. AC-60 Removing clutch hub nut
description: Holding clutch hub with Clutch Hub Wrench KV99412302 and removing clutch hub nut using Hub Nut Socket KV99412305.
mechanic_notes: Hold clutch hub firmly with tool KV99412302 while loosening nut with socket KV99412305.

caption: Fig. AC-61 Removing clutch hub
description: Using Clutch Hub Puller KV99412306 threaded into the hub bore to pull clutch hub from compressor shaft.
mechanic_notes: Thread tool into hub bore, hold tool body with a wrench, and thread in center bolt to draw off hub.

caption: Fig. AC-62 Flattening lock washer tab
description: Flattening the lock washer tab using a flat-blade screwdriver to permit removal of the pulley lock nut.
mechanic_notes: Be careful not to damage bearing cage when prying up washer tab.

caption: Fig. AC-63 Removing lock nut
description: Loosening and removing the bearing lock nut using Lock Nut Socket KV99412310.
mechanic_notes: Engage socket prongs fully into lock nut cutouts.

caption: Fig. AC-64 Removing pulley
description: Removing the clutch pulley and bearing assembly from the compressor neck by hand or with puller.
mechanic_notes: If pulley cannot be pulled by hand, use puller adapter KV99412313 and pilot KV99412312.

caption: Fig. AC-65 Loosening coil mounting screw
description: Loosening the six calked coil assembly mounting screws using a handheld manual impact screwdriver.
mechanic_notes: Use of impact screwdriver is recommended as screws are factory calked/staked.

caption: Fig. AC-66 Punch-locking
description: Staking/punch-locking each coil mounting screw at one location with a center punch and hammer to prevent loosening.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 0.28 to 0.35 kg-m (2.0 to 2.5 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: After tightening to 0.28-0.35 kg-m (2.0-2.5 ft-lb), punch-lock each screw at one point.

caption: Fig. AC-67 Checking clutch hub-to-pulley clearance
description: Measuring clearance between clutch hub and pulley using a feeler gauge at multiple peripheral locations.
mechanic_notes: If clearance is not within 0.5 to 0.8 mm (0.020 to 0.031 in), replace adjusting spacer shim and re-measure.

caption: Fig. AC-68 Removing retainer ring
description: Compressing and removing the shaft seal retainer snap ring from the front end cover using snap ring pliers.
mechanic_notes: Use snap ring pliers to compress and remove retainer ring without scratching shaft or bore.

caption: Fig. AC-69 Removing shaft seal seat
description: Applying refrigerant pressure from a charging cylinder through the low pressure port to pop the shaft seal seat out into a rag wrapped around the shaft.
mechanic_notes: Do NOT use compressed air to pop out seal seat, as air introduces moisture and dust into the system.

caption: Fig. AC-70 Inserting special tool
description: Inserting Shaft Seal Remover & Installer KV99412321 into the front end cover to engage the case projection of the shaft seal.
mechanic_notes: Depress carbon seal and hook tool at the case projection of shaft seal.

caption: Fig. AC-71 Removing shaft seal
description: Slowly pulling the hooked special tool KV99412321 out of the front end cover to extract the shaft seal assembly.
mechanic_notes: Pull tool straight outward slowly to remove shaft seal without scoring shaft.

caption: Fig. AC-72 Checking shaft seal
description: Inspection view of shaft seal showing carbon seal face and contact surface.
mechanic_notes: Check carbon seal surface for damage, cracks, or scoring.

caption: Fig. AC-73 Checking shaft seal seat
description: Inspection view of shaft seal seat highlighting O-ring groove, contact surface, and internal oil seal.
mechanic_notes: Check mating surfaces of O-ring and shaft seal seat for scratches. Ensure oil seal inside seat is lubricated with grease.

caption: Fig. AC-74 Inserting shaft seal
description: Installing the shaft seal over the shaft end using pilot KV99412322 and installer KV99412321, aligning case with shaft cutout.
mechanic_notes: Rotate seal slightly left and right to ensure it seats completely in shaft cutout.

caption: Fig. AC-75 Checking for gas leaks
description: Refrigerant pressure leak test setup connecting manifold gauge set and refrigerant can to compressor service valves while rotating shaft with tool KV99412329.
mechanic_notes: Purge air by loosening oil plug while charging refrigerant. Turn shaft 5-6 turns clockwise and verify pressure does not decrease on low pressure gauge.

caption: Fig. AC-76 Removing bolts
description: Removing two hex socket head bolts securing the discharge valve assembly to compressor shell using Allen Socket KV99412324.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.8 to 2.0 kg-m (13 to 14 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Discard old O-ring. Torque bolts to 1.8 to 2.0 kg-m (13 to 14 ft-lb) upon installation.

caption: Fig. AC-77 Loosening cover mounting bolt
description: Loosening and tightening pattern (1 through 8) for the eight side cover mounting bolts on compressor shell.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.8 to 2.0 kg-m (13 to 14 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Loosen and tighten bolts in numbered alternating pattern. Two internal silencer springs force the cover upward.

caption: Fig. AC-78 Exploded view of silencer spring, pieces and O-ring
description: Exploded view showing assembly relationship of silencer O-ring, silencer piece, silencer spring, and side cover.
mechanic_notes: Do not damage O-ring surface of silencer piece during removal. Discard used O-rings.

caption: Fig. AC-79 Loosening bolts
description: Loosening the five rear end cover Allen bolts in criss-cross order 1 through 5 using Allen Socket KV99412330.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 3.0 to 3.5 kg-m (22 to 25 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Loosen bolts one turn at a time in alternating sequence starting at top.

caption: Fig. AC-80 Removing rear end cover
description: Tapping flange of rear end cover lightly with a plastic mallet to separate cover from cylinder assembly.
mechanic_notes: Do not tap on the compressor shaft! Tap only on the cover flange.

caption: Fig. AC-81 Removing pump gear
description: Removing the trochoid oil pump gear assembly from the rear end cover cavity.
mechanic_notes: Do not allow pump gear to damage the machined end cover cavity surface.

caption: Fig. AC-82 Removing rear cylinder head
description: Using Cylinder Head Remover KV99412315 inserted into cylinder head hole to jack rear cylinder head loose.
mechanic_notes: Tighten the puller bolt slowly with the nut in firm contact with the cylinder head backside to pop head free.

caption: Fig. AC-83 Cutouts of cylinder and gasket
description: Alignment illustration showing match marks and cutouts between the cylinder block face, suction valve plate, and cylinder head gasket.
mechanic_notes: Make sure three valve reeds align perfectly with cylinder bores and gasket cutouts.

caption: Fig. AC-84 Installing gasket
description: Placing the oiled rear cylinder head gasket onto the dowel pins and valve plate on the cylinder assembly.
mechanic_notes: Coat gasket and O-ring with clean refrigeration oil before assembly.

caption: Fig. AC-85 Cylinder head and gasket
description: Plan view of cylinder head face and gasket matching ports and bolt holes.
mechanic_notes: Ensure port openings match exactly between head passages and gasket openings.

caption: Fig. AC-86 Installing rear end cover
description: Positioning the rear end cover over the pump gear and rear cylinder assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 3.0 to 3.5 kg-m (22 to 25 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Torque five bolts to 3.0-3.5 kg-m (22-25 ft-lb) in alternating criss-cross order with lock washers in place.

caption: Fig. AC-87 Pulling out oil pipe
description: Extracting internal oil delivery pipe from cylinder body using long-nose pliers.
mechanic_notes: CRITICAL: Oil pipe must be removed before attempting shell removal, or pipe will be bent/damaged.

caption: Fig. AC-88 Removing shell
description: Driving the outer compressor shell downward off the cylinder assembly by tapping rear shell flange with a plastic mallet.
mechanic_notes: Support cylinder assembly front face down, tap rear shell flange evenly straight downward.

caption: Fig. AC-89 Removing front end cover
description: Driving the front end cover upward off cylinder assembly using a plastic mallet.
mechanic_notes: Tap lightly upward with plastic mallet; avoid excessive force to prevent cover damage.

caption: Fig. AC-90 Installing suction valve plate
description: Placing gasket and front suction valve plate onto the cylinder face aligning with pins and cylinder ports.
mechanic_notes: Suction valve plates and gaskets are identical front and rear. Lubricate gasket with clean oil.

caption: Fig. AC-91 Installing cylinder head
description: Installing the front cylinder head over the locating pins and suction valve plate.
mechanic_notes: The cylinder head with fewer holes is the FRONT head; do not interchange with rear head.

caption: Fig. AC-92 Installing front end cover
description: Fitting front end cover over the front cylinder head showing silencer hole alignment.
mechanic_notes: Front and rear head gaskets differ. Adjust protruding gasket edges evenly by hand.

caption: Fig. AC-93 Installing shell
description: Lowering the compressor shell over the cylinder assembly, carefully aligning side cover holes with cylinder ports.
mechanic_notes: Carefully align the two side cover holes with the cylinder holes. Do not move shell up and down excessively to prevent dislodging gasket.

caption: Fig. AC-94 Installing oil pipe
description: Inserting the oiled oil delivery pipe and O-ring into the rear cylinder face.
mechanic_notes: Generously coat pipe and O-ring with oil before insertion; ensure hole lines match perfectly.

description: Special spanner wrench designed to engage holes in clutch hub to hold it during bolt removal.
mechanic_notes: Used on Fig. AC-60.

description: Grooved ring collar adapter used behind pulley to facilitate mechanical puller extraction.

mechanic_notes: Used on Fig. AC-76 and Page AC-62.

caption: Silencer piece installer (KV99412327)
description: T-handled driver tool for seating the silencer piece into the compressor side port.
mechanic_notes: Used on Page AC-63.

caption: Allen socket (KV99412330)
