mechanic_notes: Used on Fig. AC-79 and Page AC-64.

caption: O-ring installer (KV99412328)
description: T-handled pilot punch used to seat the silencer O-ring into the shell hole.
mechanic_notes: Used on Page AC-63.

caption: Cylinder head remover (KV99412315)
description: Screw jacking tool with nut used to separate stubborn cylinder heads from cylinder dowel pins.
mechanic_notes: Used on Fig. AC-82.

caption: Fig. AT-1 Identification number
description: Location of identification number plate attached to the right-hand side of the 3N71B transmission case.
mechanic_notes: The identification plate is attached to the right-hand side of the transmission case above the oil pan rail.

caption: Identification of number arrangements
description: Illustration of the Jatco identification plate and breakdown of model and serial number designations.
measurements_and_specs: Serial number breakdown: First digit = Last figure denoting year (A.D.); Second digit = Month of production (1-9, X: Oct., Y: Nov., Z: Dec.); Remaining digits = Serial production number for the month
mechanic_notes: Month codes: 1-9 for Jan-Sep, X for October, Y for November, Z for December.

caption: Fig. AT-2 Cross-sectional view of 3N71B automatic transmission
description: Comprehensive longitudinal cross-sectional cutaway diagram of the 3N71B automatic transmission showing all major internal components from drive plate to output shaft, with bolt tightening torque letter callouts A through I and component numbered callouts 1 through 19.

callouts.A: Converter housing to engine bolts: 4 to 5 kg-m (29 to 36 ft-lb)
callouts.B: Drive plate to crankshaft bolts: 14 to 16 kg-m (101 to 116 ft-lb)
callouts.C: Torque converter to drive plate bolts: 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)
callouts.D: Oil pump housing bolts: 0.6 to 0.8 kg-m (4.3 to 5.8 ft-lb)
callouts.E: Oil pan bolts: 0.5 to 0.7 kg-m (3.6 to 5.1 ft-lb)
callouts.F: Rear extension housing bolts: 2.0 to 2.5 kg-m (14 to 18 ft-lb)
callouts.G: Rear mounting crossmember bolts: 1.3 to 1.8 kg-m (9 to 13 ft-lb)
callouts.H: Oil pump to case bolts: 0.55 to 0.75 kg-m (4.0 to 5.4 ft-lb)
callouts.I: Control valve assembly bolts: 0.25 to 0.35 kg-m (1.8 to 2.5 ft-lb)

mechanic_notes: Ensure exact torque specifications A through I are observed during reassembly of the transmission casing, oil pump, valve body, and converter housing.

caption: Hydraulic control system block diagram
description: Block flow diagram illustrating functional relationships between Oil pump, Manual linkage, Vacuum diaphragm, Downshift solenoid, Governor valve, Control valve, Torque converter, Front clutch, Rear clutch, Low and reverse brake, Band brake, and Lubrication circuits.
mechanic_notes: Shows inputs (oil pump, manual linkage, vacuum diaphragm, downshift solenoid, governor valve) to control valve, and outputs from control valve to clutches, brakes, converter, and lubrication.

caption: Fig. AT-3 Oil pump
description: Exploded view of the internal involute gear oil pump showing the housing with crescent, cover, inner drive gear, and outer driven gear.
mechanic_notes: The inner gear is driven by the torque converter drive sleeve directly coupled with engine rotation.

caption: Fig. AT-4 Manual linkage
description: Assembly drawing of manual linkage on transmission case showing manual plate, inhibitor switch, parking rod, and manual shaft.
wiring_and_connections: Starter magnet circuit closed at P and N
Back-up lamp circuit closed at R
mechanic_notes: Inhibitor switch prevents starting in gear (allows start in P and N only) and switches reverse lamps in R.

caption: Fig. AT-5 Vacuum diaphragm
description: Cross section of vacuum diaphragm unit connected to intake manifold with central rubber partition, return spring, and throttle valve actuator rod.
mechanic_notes: Vacuum level modulates the throttle valve to adapt shift points and line pressure to engine load.

caption: Fig. AT-6 Downshift solenoid
description: Downshift solenoid and kickdown switch mechanism operated by accelerator linkage.
measurements_and_specs: Kickdown switch closes between 7/8 and 15/16 full throttle pedal stroke
mechanic_notes: Accelerator pedal must be adjusted properly to guarantee kickdown switch contact at 7/8 to 15/16 travel.

caption: Fig. AT-7 Cross-sectional view of governor
description: Cross-sectional drawing of primary and secondary governor valves mounted in the governor body on the output shaft oil distributor.
mechanic_notes: Primary valve operates as an ON/OFF threshold valve; secondary valve regulates governor pressure in proportion to vehicle speed.

caption: Fig. AT-8 Output shaft with oil distributor and governor
description: Perspective view of the output shaft assembly complete with oil distributor and governor valve body.
mechanic_notes: Located on the output shaft inside the transmission rear extension housing.

caption: Fig. AT-9 Exploded view of governor
description: Exploded view of the governor assembly showing oil distributor, governor valve body, primary governor valve, secondary governor valve, springs, retainers, and mounting bolts.
mechanic_notes: Valves and springs must move smoothly in their bores without sticking.

caption: Flow chart of control valve system
description: Flow diagram showing oil flow from pump through regulator valve to throttle valve, manual valve, auxiliary valve, speed change valve, governor valve, and final actuation of clutches and band brake.
mechanic_notes: Flow chart defines basic hydraulic logic of line pressure distribution.

caption: Fig. AT-10 Pressure regulator valve
description: Cross-sectional diagram of the Pressure Regulator Valve (PRV) showing ports 7 (line pressure), 8, 14 (torque converter), 16 (throttle pressure), 18 (throttle pressure from PMV), orifice 20, orifice 21, spools A and B, and spring.
measurements_and_specs: Circuit (20): Involute pump delivery damping orifice
mechanic_notes: Balances pump pressure against spring force modulated by throttle pressure (16, 18) and Reverse line pressure (6). Feeds torque converter circuit (14).

caption: Fig. AT-11 Manual valve
description: Cross section of the manual valve spool indicating selector positions P, R, N, D, 2, 1 and connected line pressure output circuits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 23.
mechanic_notes: Manually shifted spool selects port alignment for P, R, N, D, 2, and 1 ranges. Drains inactive circuits.

caption: Fig. AT-12 "1st-2nd" shift valve
description: Cross-sectional schematic of 1st-2nd shift valve (FSV) showing spool, spring, and hydraulic ports 1, 5, 8, 11, 12, 13, 15.
measurements_and_specs: Port 12: Low and reverse brake feed
mechanic_notes: Governor pressure on port 15 acts against line pressure and spring force to shift from 1st to 2nd.

caption: Fig. AT-13 "2nd-3rd" shift valve
description: Cross-sectional view of 2nd-3rd shift valve (SSV) showing spool, readjust plug, orifice checking valve 24, and hydraulic connections 3, 6, 10, 13, 15, 16, 19.
measurements_and_specs: Port 10: Front clutch / band servo release feed
Port 13: Kickdown line pressure from SDV
Port 19: Regulated throttle pressure to SSV/FSV
mechanic_notes: SSV connects port 3 to port 10 to engage front clutch and release band servo for 3rd gear.

caption: Fig. AT-14 Pressure modifier valve
description: Cross section of Pressure Modifier Valve (PMV) showing spool, ports 15, 16, 18, and drain ports.
measurements_and_specs: Port 18: Modified throttle pressure to PRV top
mechanic_notes: Governor pressure modulates PMV to direct throttle pressure (18) to PRV to reduce line pressure at cruising speeds.

caption: Fig. AT-15 Vacuum throttle valve
description: Cross section of vacuum throttle valve (VTV) connected to vacuum diaphragm actuator, showing ports 7 (line pressure), 16 (throttle pressure), and 17 (drain / back-up pressure).
mechanic_notes: Modulates line pressure to throttle pressure (16) proportional to engine manifold depression.

caption: Fig. AT-16 Throttle back-up valve
description: Cross-sectional view of Throttle Back-Up Valve (TBV) showing ports 4, 12, 17, and drain.
measurements_and_specs: Port 4: Line pressure in ranges 2 and 1
Port 12: Line pressure in range 1 low
Port 17: Back-up pressure output to VTV
mechanic_notes: Supplies back-up pressure to VTV in manual ranges 2 and 1 to boost line pressure.

caption: Fig. AT-17 Solenoid downshift valve
description: Cross-sectional schematic of solenoid downshift valve (SDV) showing electromagnetic solenoid, plunger, spring, and ports 4, 7, 13.
measurements_and_specs: Port 13: Kickdown pressure circuit to FSV and SSV
mechanic_notes: Electromagnetic plunger forces valve downward when kickdown switch closes, routing line pressure (7) to circuit (13).

caption: Fig. AT-18 Second lock valve
description: Cross-sectional diagram of second lock valve (SLV) showing ports 2, 3, 8, 9, and spring.
measurements_and_specs: Port 3: Line pressure in D range
mechanic_notes: In range 2, line pressure (2) locks valve downward to keep band servo engaged regardless of FSV position.

caption: Fig. AT-19 "2nd-3rd" timing valve
description: Cross section of 2nd-3rd timing valve (TMV) showing ports 10, 11, 15, 16, bypass passage, orifice 22, and spring.
mechanic_notes: Under low throttle / high vehicle speed, TMV routes line pressure through orifice 22 to soften front clutch engagement.

caption: Fig. AT-20 Control valve
description: Plan view layout of the complete control valve body assembly showing relative physical locations and bore orientations of all 10 hydraulic control and shift valves.
mechanic_notes: Reference this layout when disassembling and assembling the valve body to verify spool and spring orientation in each bore.

caption: Fig. AT-21 Identification of oil channels in oil pump
description: Port diagram on the rear face of the oil pump housing showing oil pump discharge hole (7), torque converter pressure (14), rear clutch pressure (1), front clutch pressure (11), and oil pump suction hole.
mechanic_notes: Identify matching oil passages between oil pump rear face and transmission case front face during assembly.

caption: Fig. AT-22 Identification of oil channels in case front face
description: Oil passage layout on the transmission case front face mating with oil pump housing, showing ports 1, 7, 11, 14, air breather, and suction hole.
mechanic_notes: Ensure air breather is clear and oil pump gasket correctly aligns with all indicated holes.

caption: Fig. AT-23 Identification of oil channels in case face
description: Oil passage identification on the lower transmission case face mating with the control valve assembly.
components: Transmission case valve body mating surface
mechanic_notes: Crucial passage reference for diagnosis and valve body gasket positioning.

caption: Fig. AT-24 Parking mechanism
description: Mechanical engagement views of the parking pawl with the oil distributor park gear showing 'Free' and 'Lock' states and operating rod cam linkage.
mechanic_notes: In 'Lock', the parking rod cam drives pawl into oil distributor teeth to mechanically lock output shaft.

caption: Fig. AT-25 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "P" range (Park)
description: Full hydraulic circuit diagram in 'P' (Park) range showing line pressure (7) applied to manual valve, routed via line 4 to SDV and TBV, and line 5 to FSV, line 12 to Low & Reverse brake, and torque converter supply (14) while other clutches and band servo are drained.
measurements_and_specs: Active hydraulic circuits: Line 7 (pump delivery), Line 4 (SDV/TBV), Line 5 & 12 (Low & reverse brake), Line 14 (converter/lube), Line 16 (throttle pressure)
mechanic_notes: In Park range, Low & Reverse brake is hydraulically applied along with mechanical locking pawl engagement. Red = Line pressure, Blue = Throttle pressure, Pink = Torque converter pressure, Light blue = Governor pressure, X = Drain.

caption: Fig. AT-26 Power transmission during "R" range
description: Cutaway perspective diagram illustrating torque and power flow through input shaft, front clutch, sun gear, rear planetary gears, connecting drum, rear internal gear, and output shaft during Reverse range operation.
mechanic_notes: Input shaft rotates clockwise; front clutch and low & reverse brake engaged; output shaft rotates counterclockwise.

caption: Fig. AT-27 Operation of each mechanism during "R" range
description: Schematic representation of engaged friction elements in Reverse range showing front clutch applied, band brake released (release side pressurized), and low & reverse brake applied.
mechanic_notes: Front clutch: ON; Rear clutch: OFF; Band brake: RELEASE (ON); Low & reverse brake: ON; One-way clutch: INACTIVE.

caption: Fig. AT-28 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "R" range (Reverse)
description: Full hydraulic schematic in Reverse range showing line pressure (7) directed through manual valve (2) into circuits (5) and (6), pressurizing circuit (12) for Low & Reverse brake and circuit (10) for Front clutch and band servo release side.
measurements_and_specs: Active hydraulic circuits: Line 7, Line 5, Line 6, Line 10 (Front clutch & band release), Line 12 (Low & reverse brake), Line 14 (torque converter)
mechanic_notes: Line pressure (6) assists spring on PRV to boost line pressure to maximum for heavy reverse torque transmission.

caption: Fig. AT-29 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "N" range (Neutral)
description: Full hydraulic schematic in 'N' (Neutral) range showing line pressure (7) regulated by PRV (1), delivered to manual valve (2) with all output circuits (1 through 6) blocked/drained, while circuit (14) supplies torque converter and lubrication.
measurements_and_specs: Active hydraulic circuits: Line 7 (regulated line pressure), Line 14 (converter feed and lubrication), Line 16 (throttle pressure)
mechanic_notes: All friction elements (clutches, band brake, low & reverse brake) are unpressurized and drained in Neutral.

caption: Fig. AT-30 Power transmission during "D₁" range
description: Cutaway perspective diagram illustrating torque and power transmission through input shaft, rear clutch, front internal gear, front planetary gears, sun gear, rear planetary gears, one-way clutch, rear internal gear, and output shaft during D1 low gear operation.
mechanic_notes: One-way clutch prevents rear planetary carrier counterclockwise rotation, enabling low gear torque multiplication.

caption: Fig. AT-31 Operation of each mechanism during "D₁" range
description: Schematic representation of engaged friction elements in D1 low gear showing rear clutch applied and one-way clutch holding, with front clutch, band brake, and low & reverse brake released.
mechanic_notes: Rear clutch: ON; One-way clutch: ON (holding); Front clutch: OFF; Band brake: OFF; Low & reverse brake: OFF.

caption: Fig. AT-32 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "D₁" range (Low gear)
description: Full hydraulic schematic in D1 (Low gear) range showing line pressure (7) routed through manual valve (2) into circuits (1), (2), and (3), applying Rear clutch and feeding governor valve, while 1st-2nd shift valve remains in low position.
measurements_and_specs: Active hydraulic circuits: Line 7, Line 1 (Rear clutch and governor feed), Line 2 (to SLV), Line 3 (to SSV and SLV), Line 14 (converter and lubrication), Line 15 (governor pressure build-up), Line 16 (throttle pressure)
mechanic_notes: Rear clutch is engaged by circuit 1; governor valve begins generating speed-dependent pressure in line 15 to oppose FSV return spring.

caption: Fig. AT-33 Power transmission during "D₂" range
description: Cutaway diagram showing the power flow path through the transmission during D2 range (2nd gear).

callouts.D2: Applied band brake and power flow path

mechanic_notes: Rear clutch is applied; band brake holds front clutch drum, connecting shell, and sun gear from rotating.

caption: Fig. AT-34 Operation of each mechanism during "D₂" range
description: Cross-sectional schematic illustration of engaged components during D2 range (2nd gear).
mechanic_notes: Rear clutch and band brake are engaged; one-way clutch freewheels clockwise.

caption: Fig. AT-35 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "D₂" range (2nd gear)
description: Complete schematic oil pressure circuit diagram during D2 range (2nd gear). Line pressure is directed through manual valve at D position to rear clutch and through shifted 1st-2nd shift valve and second lock valve to band servo apply side.
mechanic_notes: 1st-2nd shift valve moves to introduce line pressure (1) to line pressure (8), then via second lock valve to line pressure (9) locking the band servo apply side.

caption: Fig. AT-36 Power transmission during "D₃" range
description: Cutaway diagram showing power transmission in D3 range (top gear). Both front and rear clutches are engaged, locking the planetary gearset together for 1:1 direct drive.
mechanic_notes: Both front and rear clutches engaged; planetary gearing rotates as a solid unit to provide direct 1:1 ratio.

caption: Fig. AT-37 Operation of each mechanism "D₃" range
description: Cross-sectional schematic illustration of engaged components in D3 range (top gear).
mechanic_notes: Front clutch and rear clutch engaged; band servo release side pressurized to release the band brake.

caption: Fig. AT-38 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "D₃" range (Top gear)
description: Complete schematic oil pressure circuit diagram during D3 range (top gear). Governor pressure shifts 2nd-3rd shift valve, directing line pressure (10) to engage front clutch and to the release side of band servo.
mechanic_notes: Line pressure (10) pressurizes front clutch and release side of band servo, overcoming apply pressure and releasing band brake.

caption: Fig. AT-39 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "D" range kickdown (shift valves in 2nd gear position)
description: Oil pressure circuit diagram showing D range kickdown operation with shift valves shifted to the 2nd gear position. Solenoid downshift valve is actuated, delivering kickdown pressure (13) to assist the 2nd-3rd shift valve spring against governor pressure.
mechanic_notes: Downshift solenoid pushes downshift valve downward to open line pressure (7) to circuit (13), overcoming governor pressure (15) to achieve immediate downshift.

caption: Fig. AT-40 Power transmission during "2" range
description: Cutaway diagram showing power flow in 2 range (locked 2nd gear). Front clutch drum and sun gear held stationary by band brake; rear clutch engaged.

callouts.2: Applied band brake and power flow path

mechanic_notes: Gear ratio is locked in 2nd forward speed regardless of vehicle speed.

caption: Fig. AT-41 Operation of each mechanism during "2" range
description: Cross-sectional schematic illustration of engaged components in 2 range (2nd gear locked).
mechanic_notes: Rear clutch engaged, band brake applied.

caption: Fig. AT-42 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "2" range (2nd gear)
description: Oil pressure circuit diagram for 2 range (2nd gear). Manual valve in '2' position directs line pressure (2) to lock the second lock valve and feed the apply side of the band servo, keeping 2nd gear locked regardless of speed.
mechanic_notes: Line pressure (2) hydraulically locks the second lock valve, fixing the transmission in 2nd gear.

caption: Fig. AT-43 Power transmission during "1₁" range
description: Cutaway diagram showing power transmission in 1_1 range (low gear). Rear clutch is engaged and low & reverse brake is applied to hold the connecting drum and rear planet carrier stationary.
mechanic_notes: Rear clutch engaged, low and reverse brake applied to hold rear planet carrier.

caption: Fig. AT-44 Operation of each mechanism during "1₁" range
description: Cross-sectional schematic illustration of engaged components in 1_1 range (low gear).
mechanic_notes: Rear clutch engaged, low & reverse brake applied; front clutch and band brake disengaged.

caption: Fig. AT-45 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "1₁" range (Low gear)
description: Oil pressure circuit diagram for 1_1 range (low gear). Manual valve in '1' position directs line pressure (5) through 1st-2nd shift valve into circuit (12) to actuate the low and reverse brake.
mechanic_notes: Line pressure (12) assists the 1st-2nd shift valve spring to prevent upshift until governor pressure reaches very high speeds.

caption: Fig. AT-46 Oil pressure circuit diagram — "1₂" range (2nd gear)
description: Oil pressure circuit diagram for 1_2 range (2nd gear overspeed protection). When vehicle speed exceeds safety limit in 1 range, high governor pressure overcomes line pressure (12) and shifts the 1st-2nd shift valve to release low & reverse brake and apply band servo.
mechanic_notes: Automatic upshift to 2nd gear occurs at high speed in 1 range to prevent engine over-revolution.

caption: Fig. AT-47 Removing torque converter attaching bolts
description: Technician using a wrench through the lower converter housing access opening to remove the torque converter-to-drive plate attaching bolts.
mechanic_notes: Scribe match marks on torque converter and drive plate before removal so they can be replaced in original orientation.

caption: Fig. AT-48 Measuring drive plate runout
description: Dial gauge setup positioned against drive plate while turning crankshaft one full turn to measure drive plate runout.
measurements_and_specs: Replace drive plate limit: > 0.5 mm (0.020 in)
mechanic_notes: Rotate crankshaft one full turn to measure runout. Replace drive plate if runout exceeds 0.5 mm (0.020 in).

caption: Fig. AT-49 Torque converter aligning cut
description: Detail view of the torque converter drive hub notch/aligning cut that engages the oil pump drive gear lugs.
mechanic_notes: Notch in torque converter hub must engage drive flats of oil pump drive gear without force.

caption: Fig. AT-50 Installing torque converter
description: Sectional diagram showing measurement of distance 'A' from converter housing front face to converter mounting bolt boss face.

callouts.A: Distance from housing front face to converter bolt boss

mechanic_notes: Distance 'A' must exceed 21.5 mm (0.846 in) to confirm the torque converter is fully seated into the oil pump.

caption: Fig. AT-51 Control linkage system
description: Complete assembly diagram of the automatic transmission control linkage mechanism with shift gate patterns and tightening torque specifications for each connection point.

callouts.A: Bolt and nut T: 3.0 to 4.0 kg-m (22 to 29 ft-lb)
callouts.B: Adjust nuts T: 0.8 to 1.1 kg-m (5.8 to 8.0 ft-lb)
callouts.C: Knob screws T: 0.2 to 0.25 kg-m (1.4 to 1.8 ft-lb)
callouts.D: Bracket nut T: 0.8 to 1.1 kg-m (5.8 to 8.0 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Bolt and nut A: 3.0 to 4.0 kg-m (22 to 29 ft-lb)
Adjust nuts B: 0.8 to 1.1 kg-m (5.8 to 8.0 ft-lb)
Knob screws C: 0.2 to 0.25 kg-m (1.4 to 1.8 ft-lb)
Bracket nut D: 0.8 to 1.1 kg-m (5.8 to 8.0 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Set both control lever and selector range lever at N position when adjusting selector rod trunnion nuts.

caption: Fig. AT-52 Removing oil pan
description: Removing oil pan bolts while transmission is mounted on Transmission Case Stand ST07860000.
mechanic_notes: Mount transmission on Transmission Case Stand ST07870000 or ST07860000 before removing oil pan.

caption: Fig. AT-53 Downshift solenoid and vacuum diaphragm
description: External view of transmission case showing location and removal of downshift solenoid and vacuum diaphragm.
mechanic_notes: Do not leave diaphragm rod inside transmission case; rod is assembled in top of vacuum diaphragm.

caption: Fig. AT-54 Removing valve body
description: Underside view of transmission case with oil pan removed showing removal of bolts holding control valve body.
mechanic_notes: Remove bolts holding control valve body to transmission case.

caption: Fig. AT-55 Loosening band servo
description: Technician using wrench to loosen lock nut and adjust piston stem on band servo.
mechanic_notes: Tighten piston stem to hold front clutch drum before withdrawing oil pump; then loosen to remove band strut.

caption: Fig. AT-56 Removing oil pump
description: Withdrawing oil pump from front of transmission case using Sliding Hammer ST25850000.
mechanic_notes: Do not allow front clutch to slip out of position and drop onto floor when oil pump is withdrawn.

caption: Fig. AT-57 Removing band strut
description: Front view of transmission case interior showing removal of band strut after loosening band servo stem.
mechanic_notes: Remove band strut by loosening piston stem further.

caption: Fig. AT-58 Removing connecting shell
description: Removing connecting shell, rear clutch hub, and front planetary carrier as an assembled unit.
mechanic_notes: Remove connecting shell, rear clutch hub, and front planetary carrier as a unit.

caption: Fig. AT-59 Removing snap ring
description: Prying snap ring off the output shaft using Snap Ring Remover HT69860000.
mechanic_notes: Use Snap Ring Remover HT69860000 to pry snap ring off output shaft.

caption: Fig. AT-60 Removing connecting drum
description: Withdrawing connecting drum and internal gear of rear planetary carrier as an assembly.
mechanic_notes: Remove connecting drum and inner gear of rear planetary carrier as an assembly.

caption: Fig. AT-61 Removing rear extension
description: Removing rear extension housing from transmission case by loosening securing bolts.
mechanic_notes: Loosen securing bolts and withdraw rear extension housing.

caption: Fig. AT-62 Removing governor and oil distributor
description: Pulling out output shaft and removing oil distributor together with governor valve assembly.
mechanic_notes: Pull out output shaft; remove oil distributor ② together with governor valve ①.

caption: Fig. AT-63 Removing drive and driven plates
description: Removing low and reverse brake retaining plate, drive plate, driven plate, and dish plate from transmission case after prying off snap ring.
mechanic_notes: Pry off snap ring using pliers. Remove retaining plate, drive plate, driven plate and dish plate in that order.

caption: Fig. AT-64 Removing hex-head slotted bolt
description: Using Hex-head Extension ST25570001 to reach through back side of transmission case and remove hex-head slotted bolts.
mechanic_notes: Reach through back side of transmission case with special extension ST25570001 to remove slotted bolts.

caption: Fig. AT-65 Removing piston
description: Applying compressed air into hole in cylinder to blow out low and reverse brake piston.
mechanic_notes: Blow out low and reverse brake piston by directing a jet of air into hole in cylinder.

caption: Fig. AT-66 Removing band servo
description: Directing a jet of air toward release side of band servo to assist in removing retainer.
mechanic_notes: Direct a jet of air toward release side if difficulty is encountered in removing band servo retainer.

caption: Fig. AT-67 Removing manual plate
description: Interior view of linkage components on manual shaft showing parking brake lever, manual plate, and parking rod.
mechanic_notes: Pry snap rings from ends of parking lever, back off lock nut, and remove manual plate and parking rod.

caption: Fig. AT-68 Measuring seal ring to ring groove clearance
description: Cross-sectional inspection diagram showing feeler gauge measurement between seal ring and groove in oil distributor.
mechanic_notes: Correct clearance between seal ring and ring groove is 0.04 to 0.16 mm (0.0016 to 0.0063 in). Replace if worn beyond limits.

caption: Fig. AT-69 Installing one-way clutch inner race
description: Torquing hex-head slotted bolt for one-way clutch inner race using special hex extension ST25570001 and torque wrench GG91060000.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.3 to 1.8 kg-m (9 to 13 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Torque hex-head slotted bolt to 1.3 to 1.8 kg-m (9 to 13 ft-lb) using special extension and torque wrench.

caption: Fig. AT-70 Measuring ring to plate clearance
description: Feeler gauge measuring clearance between snap ring ① and retaining plate ② in low and reverse brake.
measurements_and_specs: Low and reverse brake clearance: 0.80 to 1.25 mm (0.031 to 0.049 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure clearance between snap ring and retaining plate; select appropriate retaining plate thickness.

caption: Fig. AT-71 One-way clutch
description: Perspective view of one-way clutch assembly showing orientation arrow mark on outer cage.
mechanic_notes: Install one-way clutch so arrow mark '→' points toward front of vehicle; must rotate freely clockwise only.

caption: Fig. AT-72 Installing planetary carrier
description: Technician lowering rear clutch hub and front planetary carrier into position.
mechanic_notes: Install rear clutch hub and front planetary carrier carefully into place.

caption: Fig. AT-73 Installing connecting shell
description: Technician installing connecting shell over planetary gearing components.
mechanic_notes: Assemble connecting shell and parts up to front clutch in reverse order of disassembly.

caption: Fig. AT-74 End play
description: Cross-sectional reference diagram illustrating front end play and total end play measurement locations.
measurements_and_specs: Total end play: 0.25 to 0.50 mm (0.010 to 0.020 in)
Front end play: 0.5 to 0.8 mm (0.020 to 0.031 in)
mechanic_notes: Diagram showing relationships between thrust washer 1, bearing race 7, oil pump gasket 6, and cases for total and front end play adjustments.

caption: Fig. AT-75 Measuring the distance "A" and "C"
description: Sectional diagram showing vernier caliper depth measurement of distances A (to bearing race surface) and C (to thrust washer surface) inside transmission case.
mechanic_notes: Measure distance A and C using vernier calipers from front face of transmission case.

caption: Fig. AT-76 Measuring the distance "B" and "D"
description: Sectional diagram showing vernier caliper measurement of distances B and D on oil pump cover.
mechanic_notes: Measure distance B and D on oil pump cover from mounting flange face.

caption: Fig. AT-77 Measuring the distance "L"
description: Cross-sectional diagram illustrating measurement of distance 'L' from transmission case end to vacuum throttle valve rod end with valve fully depressed.

callouts.L: Distance from case end to pushed-in valve rod end

measurements_and_specs: Measured distance L used to select diaphragm rod length (29.0 to 31.0 mm)
mechanic_notes: Push vacuum throttle valve fully in, measure length L, and select diaphragm rod corresponding to table.

caption: Fig. AT-78 Sectional view of front clutch
description: Sectional view of front clutch assembly showing arrangement of piston, return springs, dished plate, driven plates, drive plates, retaining plate, and snap rings.
mechanic_notes: Pay close attention to stacking sequence of plates: dished plate first, followed by alternating driven and drive plates, then retaining plate and snap ring.

caption: Fig. AT-79 Removing snap ring
description: Using Clutch Spring Compressor ST25420001 to compress springs and Snap Ring Remover ST25320001 to remove snap ring from front clutch spring retainer.
mechanic_notes: Compress return springs evenly with compressor tool before removing snap ring.

caption: Fig. AT-80 Modifying coil spring compressor
description: Dimensional modification diagram showing where to grind off hatched portion (1.5 mm deep by 20 mm wide) on legs of Clutch Spring Compressor ST25420000.
measurements_and_specs: Cut off hatched portion: 1.5 mm (0.059 in) by 20 mm (0.079 in)
mechanic_notes: When using older compressor ST25420000, grind 1.5 mm x 20 mm off toe-tips of three legs to clear clutch drum.

caption: Fig. AT-81 Blowing out piston
description: Technician using compressed air jet directed into front clutch drum oil hole to blow out piston.
mechanic_notes: Hold a shop rag over drum opening when blowing air to catch piston safely.

caption: Fig. AT-82 Inserting clutch plate
description: Technician carefully inserting lined drive plates and steel driven plates into front clutch drum.
mechanic_notes: Dip all clutch plates in clean ATF prior to installation in drum.

caption: Fig. AT-83 Measuring ring to plate clearance
description: Feeler gauge measuring clearance between snap ring ① and retaining plate ② in front clutch drum.
measurements_and_specs: Specified clearance: 1.6 to 2.0 mm (0.063 to 0.079 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure clearance with feeler gauge; select from 6 available retaining plates to obtain 1.6 to 2.0 mm clearance.

caption: Fig. AT-84 Testing front clutch
description: Functional air check of front clutch mounted on oil pump cover by applying compressed air into oil hole.
mechanic_notes: With clutch mounted on oil pump cover, direct air jet into clutch oil hole to verify positive piston engagement.

caption: Fig. AT-85 Sectional view of rear clutch
description: Sectional view of rear clutch assembly showing arrangement of rear clutch drum, piston, dished plate, return springs, retainer, plates, and snap rings.
mechanic_notes: Notice correct orientation of dish plate and stack sequence of drive and driven plates.

caption: Fig. AT-86 Removing snap ring
description: Compressing coil spring retainer with tool ST25420001 and removing snap ring with tool ST25320001 from rear clutch drum.
mechanic_notes: Compress coil springs evenly to release tension from snap ring before prying out.

caption: Fig. AT-87 Blowing out piston
description: Applying compressed air into rear clutch drum oil passage to dislodge and remove piston.
mechanic_notes: Direct a jet of compressed air into oil hole in clutch drum while holding piston with a cloth.

caption: Fig. AT-88 Measuring ring to plate clearance
description: Feeler gauge measuring clearance between snap ring ① and retaining plate ② in rear clutch.
measurements_and_specs: Specified clearance: 0.8 to 1.6 mm (0.031 to 0.063 in)
mechanic_notes: Specified clearance is 0.8 to 1.6 mm (0.031 to 0.063 in). Adjust using retaining plates if out of spec.

caption: Fig. AT-89 Testing rear clutch
description: Bench testing assembled rear clutch on oil pump cover with compressed air.
mechanic_notes: Install rear clutch on oil pump cover and apply air pressure to test positive clutch operation.

caption: Fig. AT-90 Testing low & reverse brake
description: Directing compressed air into oil passage in transmission case to verify positive engagement of low & reverse brake.
mechanic_notes: Blow compressed air into oil hole in transmission case to verify definite low & reverse brake application.

caption: Fig. AT-91 Removing piston
description: Technician withdrawing servo piston from brake band servo bore.
mechanic_notes: Blow out servo piston by directing air into release-side hole in piston; inspect piston for score marks.

caption: Fig. AT-92 Sectional view of servo piston
description: Cross-sectional engineering view of the transmission case, brake band, and band servo piston mechanism showing apply and release passages and return spring.
mechanic_notes: Extreme care must be taken to avoid damaging the rubber ring when installing seal lace.

caption: Fig. AT-93 Testing piston (Apply side)
description: Testing servo piston operation by applying compressed air nozzle into the apply-side passage in transmission case.
mechanic_notes: Blow compressed air from apply-side of piston to test for definite piston operation.

caption: Fig. AT-94 Testing piston (Release side)
description: Testing band servo retainer tightness using compressed air while plugging apply hole with thumb.
mechanic_notes: With apply-side plugged with thumb, blow air into cylinder from release-side. If retainer raises, attaching bolts are loose.

caption: Fig. AT-95 Testing secondary governor
description: Sectional schematic of the governor assembly mounted on output shaft showing primary and secondary governors and air test point A.

callouts.A: Air test port (Line pressure 1 from control valve)

mechanic_notes: Blow air under light pressure into hole A; listen for buzzing noise like that of a model plane.

caption: Fig. AT-96 Measuring clearance
description: Feeler gauge and straight edge measuring clearance between pump gears and oil pump cover.
mechanic_notes: Inspect gear teeth for wear or damage before measuring.

caption: Fig. AT-99 Measuring runout
description: Dial indicator checking total runout of oil pump cover mounted on assembling gauge ST25580000.
measurements_and_specs: Total indicator reading: within 0.07 mm (0.0028 in)
mechanic_notes: Check runout before and after tightening securing bolts to 0.6 to 0.8 kg-m (4.3 to 5.8 ft-lb).

caption: Fig. AT-97 Measuring clearance
description: Cross-sectional detail illustrating clearance measurement between seal ring and ring groove.
measurements_and_specs: Standard clearance: 0.04 to 0.16 mm (0.002 to 0.006 in)
mechanic_notes: Use feeler gauge to measure clearance in groove.

caption: Fig. AT-98 Centering oil pump
description: Centering oil pump cover to pump housing using assembling gauge ST25580000.
mechanic_notes: Align converter housing securing bolt holes when installing.

caption: Fig. AT-100 Measuring pinion washer to carrier clearance
description: Cross-sectional diagram showing feeler gauge measuring clearance between pinion thrust washer and planetary carrier.
measurements_and_specs: Standard clearance: 0.20 to 0.70 mm (0.008 to 0.028 in)
mechanic_notes: Planetary carrier cannot be disassembled. If defective, replace as a unit.

caption: Fig. AT-101 Disassembling valve body
description: Removing oil strainer bolts and nuts from control valve using hexagon wrench HT61000800 and spinner handle HT62350000.
mechanic_notes: Bolts may be removed with screwdriver, but hexagon wrench and spinner handle are recommended.

caption: Fig. AT-102 Removing separate plate
description: Lifting separate plate away from control valve body halves.
mechanic_notes: Do not allow orifice check valve and valve spring in lower valve body to be scattered and lost.

caption: Fig. AT-103 Removing manual valve
description: Sliding manual valve spool out of the control valve body.
mechanic_notes: Handle valve spool carefully to prevent scratching precision surfaces.

caption: Fig. AT-104 Removing side plate
description: Using hexagon wrench HT61000800 and spinner handle HT62350000 to remove valve body side plate screws.
mechanic_notes: Avoid working screws off with ordinary screwdrivers to prevent damaging machine screw heads.

caption: Fig. AT-105 Components parts of control valve
description: Exploded layout of all control valve spools, plugs, sleeves, springs, and end plates around the main valve body.
mechanic_notes: Organize parts in a part rack to ensure each valve, plug, and spring returns to its designated bore.

caption: Fig. AT-106 Valve spring
description: Dimensional engineering diagram of a valve spring showing wire diameter, mean coil diameter, free length, as-installed length, and tension measurement points.
mechanic_notes: Compare spring dimensions with the Valve Spring Chart before installation.

caption: Fig. AT-107 Installing side plate
description: Torqueing side plate screws on valve body using Torque Driver ST25160000 and Hexagon Wrench HT61000800.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 0.25 to 0.35 kg-m (1.8 to 2.5 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten side plates evenly to 0.25 to 0.35 kg-m (1.8 to 2.5 ft-lb).

caption: Fig. AT-108 Installing valve body
description: Securing upper and lower valve bodies together using Torque Driver ST25160000 and Hexagon Wrench HT61000800.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 0.25 to 0.35 kg-m (1.8 to 2.5 ft-lb)
Reamer bolt torque: 0.5 to 0.7 kg-m (3.6 to 5.1 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Note difference in tightening torque between standard valve body bolts and reamer bolts.

caption: Fig. AT-109 Position of check valve and spring
description: Plan view of valve body maze passages showing exact locations of throttle relief valve and two orifice check valves.
mechanic_notes: Ensure orifice check valves and relief springs are correctly positioned before joining valve body sections.

caption: Fig. AT-110 Downshift solenoid
description: Location of the electric downshift solenoid threaded into the side of the transmission case above the oil pan rail.
mechanic_notes: Watch for oil leakage around solenoid threads in transmission case.

caption: Fig. AT-111 Construction of inhibitor switch
description: Exploded mounting assembly of inhibitor switch, manual shaft, washers, nuts, manual plate, and range select lever.
wiring_and_connections: Inhibitor switch wire harness (BY, RB wires)
mechanic_notes: Align switch body with manual shaft in 'N' range using 1.5 mm (0.059 in) pin.

caption: Fig. AT-112 Shift Schedule
description: Shift schedule graph plotting negative intake manifold vacuum (-mmHg / -inHg) against output shaft speed (rpm) and car speed (km/h and MPH) for upshifts (1->2, 2->3) and downshifts (3->2, 2->1, 1_2->1_1) including kickdown range.
measurements_and_specs: Car speed: 0 to 120 km/h (0 to 80 MPH)
mechanic_notes: Use this graph to verify upshift and downshift vehicle speeds under varying engine vacuum loads.

caption: Fig. AT-113 Measuring Line Pressure
description: Transmission case illustration showing the locations of test ports 1 (Line pressure), 2 (Governor pressure), and 3 (Servo release pressure) with gauge connected.
mechanic_notes: Remove blind plugs to connect pressure gauge for test measurements.

caption: Fig. BE-1 Wiring harness (2 seater)
description: Chassis layout illustration showing the routing and placement of body wiring harnesses throughout the 2-seater vehicle body.

callouts.A: Front combination lamp

mechanic_notes: Identifies primary connection locations between engine room, dash, console, and EFI sub-harnesses.

caption: Fig. BE-2 Engine room harness
description: Diagram of engine room harness routing showing branch connections to fusible link, alternator, and transmission switches.
mechanic_notes: Routing along engine bay skirt and front radiator core support.

caption: Fig. BE-3 Engine room harness
description: Physical harness layout showing junction connection between Electronic Fuel Injection harness and Engine Room harness.
mechanic_notes: Harness connection along inner fender apron.

caption: Fig. BE-4 Engine sub-harness (A/T models)
description: Engine sub-harness routing for automatic transmission models servicing downshift solenoid and inhibitor switch.
mechanic_notes: Used exclusively on automatic transmission vehicles.

caption: Fig. BE-5 Instrument harness
description: Instrument panel harness assembly and routing behind the dashboard.
wiring_and_connections: Connects with 3 connectors at junction block under RH dash (white, black, blue).
mechanic_notes: Feeds gauges, clock, tachometer, speedometer, glove box, and warning lamps.

caption: Fig. BE-6 Dash harness
description: Under-dash harness installation showing junction block, relay bracket, transistor ignition unit, fuse block, and EFI ECU.
wiring_and_connections: To air conditioner harness branch connector shown at center lower dash.
mechanic_notes: Junction block and fuse block are mounted under the right side of the instrument panel.

caption: Fig. BE-7 Dash harness (2 seater)
description: Floor and rear body dash harness routing in 2-seater body shell.

callouts.To seat belt switch: Driver seat belt buckle switch lead

mechanic_notes: Specific branch routing along floor pan and wheel arches for 2-seater models.

caption: Fig. BE-8 Dash harness (2 + 2 seater)
description: Floor and rear body dash harness routing in 2+2 seater body shell.
mechanic_notes: Extended harness length accommodates 2+2 rear passenger compartment.

caption: Fig. BE-9 Console harness
description: Center console harness assembly and switch connector pigtails.
wiring_and_connections: Connects to dash harness with a pair of multi-pin connectors.
mechanic_notes: Services A/T shift indicator, hazard switch, rear defogger switch, radio, seat belt warning lamp, and ashtray illumination.

caption: Fig. BE-10 Electronic fuel injection harness
description: Engine room harness and electronic fuel injection harness layout along the engine bay apron.
mechanic_notes: Connects to injectors, dropping resistor, throttle switch, air flow meter, cold start valve, and thermotime switch.

caption: Fig. BE-11 Fuse block
description: Fuse box cavity layout, circuit labeling, amperage ratings, and under-dash installation relative to the relay bracket, timer unit, and transistor ignition unit.
mechanic_notes: Use specified fuses only. Never use a fuse of higher rating.

caption: Fig. BE-12 Fusible link
description: Mounting of the fusible link block and cover on the engine compartment relay bracket.
components: Fusible link for electronic fuel injection system

callouts.4: Fusible link for electronic fuel injection system

wiring_and_connections: Connected between battery (+) cable and main harnesses.
mechanic_notes: Never wrap fusible links in vinyl tape. Ensure clear separation from rubber/vinyl hoses.

caption: Fig. BE-13 Relay bracket
description: Engine compartment hoodledge relay bracket showing layout of the 5 relays.
mechanic_notes: Located on the right-hand hoodledge in the engine compartment.

caption: Fig. BE-14 Relay bracket
description: Passenger compartment dash side panel relay bracket and components installation.
mechanic_notes: Mounted on dash side panel inside the cabin.

caption: Fig. BE-15 Relay bracket
description: Interior relay bracket component arrangement showing 4 relays and seat belt warning timer unit.
mechanic_notes: Interior passenger compartment relay cluster.

caption: Fig. BE-16 Circuit diagram for headlamp
description: Complete electrical circuit diagram for the headlamp system, showing battery feed through fusible links, light switch, dimmer switch, left and right 10A headlamp fuses, sealed beams, and high beam indicator lamp.
mechanic_notes: Ground connection for headlamps is routed through the body earth near the horn. Dimmer switch selects between high and low filaments.

caption: Fig. BE-17 Circuit diagram for turn signal lamp
description: Wiring schematic of the turn signal lamp system showing power from ignition switch through ignition relay, 10A flasher fuse, hazard switch, flasher unit, combination switch lever, and front/rear combination lamps.
mechanic_notes: Turn signals are powered only with ignition ON via the ignition relay. Power routes through hazard switch normally-closed contacts.

caption: Fig. BE-18 Circuit diagram for hazard warning system
description: Wiring schematic of hazard warning flashers showing continuous battery feed via fusible link and 10A hazard fuse to hazard flasher unit, pulsing all four turn signal filaments simultaneously.
mechanic_notes: Operates independently of ignition switch position via constant battery BATT rail.

caption: Fig. BE-19 Circuit diagram for stop lamp system
description: Wiring schematic for brake/stop lamps showing circuit from battery through fusible link, 15A horn/stop fuse, brake pedal stop lamp switch, and rear combination lamp stop filaments.
mechanic_notes: Stop lamp switch is normally open, closing when brake pedal is depressed. Powered from BATT rail at all times.

caption: Fig. BE-20 Circuit diagram for clearance and tail lamp
description: Electrical circuit schematic for parking clearance, side marker, tail, and license plate lamps operated by the 1st position of the light switch.
mechanic_notes: Light switch contacts 4 and 5 connect to separate front and rear circuits on 1st and 2nd switch positions.

caption: Fig. BE-21 Circuit diagram for back-up lamp system
description: Wiring schematic for reverse/back-up lamps, showing power feed from ignition switch through ignition relay, 10A fuse, transmission reverse switch (M/T) or inhibitor switch (A/T), and rear combination back-up bulbs.
mechanic_notes: Switch contacts close only when transmission is in reverse gear.

caption: Fig. BE-22 Circuit diagram for meter illumination lamp
description: Wiring diagram for instrument panel, gauge, and control panel backlighting controlled by the illumination rheostat dimmer.
mechanic_notes: Rheostat modulates the ground return circuit (RL wire) of all instrument backlights to control illumination brightness.

caption: Fig. BE-23 Circuit diagram for interior lamp
description: Wiring schematic for interior dome/courtesy lamp, operated by door jamb plunger switches and tailgate switch (2+2 models) or manual dome switch.
mechanic_notes: Interior lamp receives unswitched 12V (LW wire). Door switches ground the BR circuit when doors or tailgate open.

caption: Fig. BE-24 Circuit diagram for glove box and cigarette lighter illumination
description: Wiring diagram for glove box, cigarette lighter, and ashtray illumination circuits tied to tail lamp/clearance feed.

caption: Fig. BF-39 Removing finisher and combination lamp assembly

caption: Fig. BF-40 Adjusting door hinge
description: Door hinge adjustment directions and allowable adjustment limits.

measurements_and_specs: Special tool: Door Hinge Wrench ST08720000 (J 25610)

callouts.6: Rear inside handle escutcheon (GS30 2 + 2 seater only)

description: Using a flat tool or screwdriver to pop door finisher retaining clips from door inner panel.
mechanic_notes: Pry close to clip positions to avoid breaking fiberboard panel backing.

caption: Fig. BF-46 Door window glass and regulator for S30 (2 seater)
description: Exploded view of door window glass, sash, front and rear guide rails, guide channels A and B, regulator mechanism, and crank handle for S30 2-seater.

caption: Fig. BF-47 Door window glass and regulator for GS30 (2 + 2 seater)
description: Exploded view of door window glass, sash, front and rear guide rails, guide channels A and B, regulator mechanism, and crank handle for GS30 2+2 seater.
mechanic_notes: Specific to GS30 2+2 seater door. Different door sash and glass length from 2-seater.

caption: Fig. BF-48 Guide rail adjusting mechanism
description: Adjusting bolts and slotted holes on inner door frame for front and rear window guide rails.
measurements_and_specs: Lower bolt: tighten fully then back off 4 turns and lock
mechanic_notes: Initial setting for lower adjusting bolt: tighten all the way, then return 4 turns and lock.

caption: Fig. BF-49 Proper clearance between outside door panel and glass
description: Cross section through door window opening showing clearance between glass outer surface and outer door panel skin.
mechanic_notes: Adjust guide rail upper adjusting bolts to establish 22 to 24 mm clearance.

caption: Fig. BF-50 Adjusting front and rear guide rails
description: Fore and aft adjustment arrows for front and rear guide rails to eliminate sideways glass free play.
mechanic_notes: Move rails fore and aft to eliminate unwanted sideways glass play.

caption: Fig. BF-51 Adjusting guide channel A
description: Diagram showing glass tilt conditions (A - front tilted down, B - rear tilted down) and how adjusting guide channel A corrects parallel alignment with top rail.
mechanic_notes: Move guide channel A up for condition (A); move down for condition (B).

caption: Fig. BF-52 Removing door trim
description: Door inner frame after removal of door trim and water screen showing access cutouts.
mechanic_notes: Remove water seal screen carefully to access regulator and guide channel fasteners.

caption: Fig. BF-53 Removing screws attaching glass back plate to guide channel B
description: Accessing screws connecting the door glass bottom bracket to regulator guide channel B.
mechanic_notes: Support glass securely from dropping when screws are removed.

caption: Fig. BF-54 Removing guide rail
description: Removing front and rear vertical guide rails through inner door panel access openings.
mechanic_notes: Remove guide rails after lifting glass upwards and out.

caption: Fig. BF-55 Removing regulator assembly
description: Withdrawing the regulator mechanism assembly through the lower inner door panel opening.
mechanic_notes: Collapse arms to maneuver mechanism through the lower stamped cutout.

caption: Fig. BF-56 Door lock mechanism for S30 (2 seater)
description: Exploded view of the door lock mechanism, rods, interior handle, and lock knob for S30 2-seater.
mechanic_notes: Single inner handle configuration for two-seater models.

caption: Fig. BF-57 Door lock mechanism for GS30 (2 + 2 seater)
description: Exploded view of door lock linkage for GS30 2+2 seater showing front remote handle, rear inside handle, rods, and lock mechanism.
mechanic_notes: GS30 2+2 model includes an auxiliary rear inside door release handle and linkage.

caption: Fig. BF-58 Adjusting outside door handle free play
description: Adjusting nylon nut on outside handle pushrod to establish 0 to 1.0 mm clearance with lock lever.
mechanic_notes: Turn nylon adjusting nut to set zero-to-minimal clearance without pre-loading latch.

caption: Fig. BF-59 Adjusting inside door handle
description: Adjusting inside door handle in elongated mounting slots with lock knob engaged.
mechanic_notes: Move handle rearward in slotted holes until it stops, then tighten screws.

caption: Fig. BF-60 Removing outside door handle
description: Loosening outside door handle attaching nuts from inner door cavity.
mechanic_notes: Remove handle together with vertical connecting rod.

caption: Fig. BF-61 Removing door lock assembly
description: Removing latch mechanism screws from door shut-face and withdrawing latch from inside door.
mechanic_notes: Withdraw lock assembly through access hole in inner door panel.

caption: Fig. BF-62 Removing door lock striker
description: Loosening screws securing striker plate to body pillar.
mechanic_notes: Use impact screwdriver if striker screws are excessively tight.

caption: Fig. BF-63 Body side and door weatherstrips
description: Door opening perimeter view and cross-sectional profiles of body side and door sash weatherstrips for 2-seater and 2+2 seater.

callouts.Section: A-A: Body side weatherstrip cross section on pillar flange
callouts.Section: B-B (2 seater): Door sash upper weatherstrip profile for 2-seater
callouts.Section: B-B, C-C (2 + 2 seater): Door sash upper weatherstrip profile for 2+2 seater

mechanic_notes: Profiles differ between 2-seater and 2+2 models at section B-B/C-C.

caption: Fig. BF-64 Removing body side weatherstrip
description: Removing scuff plate and pulling body side weatherstrip off the door aperture pinchweld.
mechanic_notes: Loosen scuff plate screws before pulling weatherstrip.

caption: Fig. BF-65 Prying off rivets
description: Prying off plastic rivets retaining door weatherstrip to door sash groove using a screwdriver.
mechanic_notes: Pry carefully to release rivets without tearing weatherstrip rubber channel.

caption: Fig. BF-66 Front windshield glass
description: Exploded view of front windshield glass, perimeter weatherstrip, stainless moldings, and cross section A-A showing adhesive application points.
measurements_and_specs: Apply adhesive to body flange lip and weatherstrip mating groove as shown in section A-A
mechanic_notes: Apply adhesive to specific sealing contact points on weatherstrip before mounting glass.

caption: Fig. BF-67 Removing front windshield glass
description: Separating windshield glass adhesive bead using a spatula worked around flange from outside.
mechanic_notes: Always start removal from upper side portion to prevent sudden drop.

caption: Fig. BF-68 Tools for installation of windshield glass
description: Required hand tools for installing windshield glass: capillary tube, spatula, and draw string.
mechanic_notes: Capillary tube used for injecting adhesive into rubber channel; strong nylon string used to pull rubber lip over pinchweld.

caption: Fig. BF-69 Structural view of side window for S30 (2 seater)
description: Exploded view of fixed quarter side window, frame sash, weatherstrips, joint covers, and rubber seals for S30 2-seater.
mechanic_notes: Fixed quarter glass installation on S30 2-seater.

caption: Fig. BF-70 Structural view of side window for GS30 (2 + 2 seater)
description: Exploded view of hinged/opening rear side window glass, center pillar, upper bracket, sash, latch handle, rubber washer, and finisher nut for GS30 2+2 seater.
mechanic_notes: Hinged vent window design specific to GS30 2+2 models, utilizing pivot brackets and toggle latch handle.

caption: Fig. BF-71 Structural view of tail gate glass
description: Exploded view of tail gate glass, surrounding rubber weatherstrip, and stainless trim moldings with cross section A-A.
measurements_and_specs: Use sealing agent rather than adhesive during installation
mechanic_notes: Use non-hardening sealing agent instead of adhesive for tailgate glass.

caption: Fig. BF-72 Structural view of front and rear seats
description: Exploded structural view of front reclining bucket seats, slide rails, and GS30 2+2 folding rear seat assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Slide travel: 180 mm (7.09 in), pitch 20 mm (0.79 in)
mechanic_notes: Rear seatback folds flush with floor on 2+2 model.

caption: Fig. BF-73 Removing front attaching bolts of front seat
description: Removing front mounting bracket bolts securing front seat track to floor pan.
mechanic_notes: Slide seat rearward to expose front floor bracket bolts.

caption: Fig. BF-74 Removing rear seat cushion
description: Removing front securing screws to detach rear seat cushion on GS30 2+2.
mechanic_notes: GS30 2+2 only: unscrew front retaining screws before lifting cushion.

caption: Fig. BF-75 Removing rear seatback
description: Removing hinge pivot bolts attaching rear seatback to body side structure on GS30 2+2.
mechanic_notes: Fold seatback forward and pull mat away to reach hinge mounting bolts.

caption: Fig. BF-76 Removing inner lap belt
description: Removing floor anchor bolt securing inner buckle stalk and wire harness.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect buckle switch harness connector before unbolting anchor.

caption: Fig. BF-77 Removing strut cover clip
description: Removing synthetic resin plastic clip from rear strut tower trim cover.
mechanic_notes: S30 models: pry center pin to remove clip without breaking cover.

caption: Fig. BF-78 Removing shoulder belt (for S30 2 seater models)
description: Removing shoulder belt guide anchor bolt and escutcheon on rear strut tower for S30 2-seater.
mechanic_notes: Keep washers and spacers in proper order for reassembly.

caption: Fig. BF-79 Removing shoulder belt (for GS30 2 + 2 seater models)
description: Removing shoulder belt upper anchor bolt and escutcheon on B/C-pillar for GS30 2+2 seater.
mechanic_notes: Requires removal of quarter panel trim and weatherstrip to reach anchor bolt.

caption: Fig. BF-80 Removing shoulder and outer lap belts
description: Removing ELR retractor cover and two floor anchor bolts securing outer retractor unit.
mechanic_notes: Shoulder and outer lap belts are an integral retractor unit; replace as a set.

caption: Fig. BF-81 Removing rear seat belts
description: Loosening rear floor anchor bolts securing rear seat belts on GS30 2+2.
mechanic_notes: Rear seats must be removed before unbolting rear seat belt retractors.

caption: Fig. BF-82 Body side trim (2 + 2 seater)
description: Exploded view of interior body side trim panels for GS30 2+2 seater including quarter panel garnish, rail garnish, reservoir protector, and rear trim.
mechanic_notes: Use punch/skinny bar to push center pin of expansion fasteners to remove.

caption: Fig. BF-83 Spare tire compartment lid
description: Exploded view of rear floor spare tire well lid, hinges, and prop rod/support mechanism.
mechanic_notes: Flush floor mounted spare tire cover.

caption: Fig. BF-84 Tail gate trim
description: Layout of retaining clips and screws for the tailgate inner trim finisher panel.
mechanic_notes: Carefully release perimeter clips to prevent tearing trim panel.

caption: Fig. BF-85 Floor console
description: Exploded view of center floor console, shift boot opening, armrest pocket, mounting screws, and harness connections.
mechanic_notes: Remove 5 screws and unplug wiring before lifting console over shifter.

caption: Fig. BF-86 Inside rearview mirror
description: Exploded view of inside rearview mirror, mounting bracket, base cover, and attaching screws.
mechanic_notes: Pry off base cover to access mounting screws.

caption: Fig. BF-87 Instrument panel
description: Exploded view of the dashboard assembly, instrument upper garnish, padded main dashboard shell, lower brackets, and mounting hardware.
mechanic_notes: Always disconnect battery cable before beginning dash removal. Speedometer cable must be uncoupled.

caption: Fig. BF-88 Removing instrument finisher
description: Detaching center gauge / heater control instrument finisher from dash structure.
mechanic_notes: Remove screws securing finisher before withdrawing center panel.

caption: Fig. BF-89 Instrument panel under cover
description: Lower steering column / pedal area under-dash trim cover and retaining screws.
mechanic_notes: Remove two screws to take down under cover.

caption: Fig. BF-90 Sealing body panel joint
description: Overview map and cross sections detailing factory sealer locations on body panel seams and joints (Sections A-A through H-H).

callouts.Section: A-A: Inner sill and outer sill joint
callouts.Section: B-B: Body side member, rear floor panel, and rear fender panel joint
callouts.Section: C-C: Roof panel and drip rail joint
callouts.\"D\" portion: Gasoline filler unit (Right side) - lower portion and overall circumference
callouts.Section: E-E: Rear fender panel, mud guard, tail rail main, and complement band joint

callouts.Section: G-G: Cowl top outer panel, cowl top inner panel, dash lower panel, and front floor panel
callouts.Section: H-H: Rear fender panel, rod sealer, and wheel housing outer panel

mechanic_notes: Reapply appropriate seam sealer and rod sealer to these specific joint profiles during body repair to prevent water leaks and corrosion.

caption: Fig. BF-91 Sealing rear panel joint
description: Detailed seam sealing locations on rear body panel, tail member, spare tire housing, and quarter extension joints (Sections J-J and K-K).

callouts.Section: J-J: Rear fender panel to extension rear panel joint
callouts.Section: K-K: Rear panel, tail member, spare tire housing, spot sealer, and rod sealer joints

mechanic_notes: Apply spot sealer and rod sealer as specified to prevent exhaust gas and moisture ingress into luggage compartment.

caption: Fig. BF-92 Sealing rear wheel housing
description: Rear wheelhouse sealing points and wiring grommet adhesive sealing (Section L-L).

callouts.Section: L-L: Grommet to body sheet metal sealing with adhesive

wiring_and_connections: Harness grommet through rear wheelhouse/side member
mechanic_notes: Ensure adhesive seal around rubber grommet L-L to prevent wheel splash from entering body cavity.

caption: Door adjusting wrench ST08720000 (Kent-Moore J 25610)
description: Special curved offset box wrench designed to reach door hinge mounting bolts inside the fender gap.
mechanic_notes: Permits adjusting or removing door hinges without removing front fenders.

caption: Fig. BR-1 Brake system
description: Chassis layout schematic showing hydraulic brake lines, master cylinder, Master-Vac, NP-valve, 3-way connector, front disc brakes, rear drum brakes, and hand brake control lever.
mechanic_notes: NP-valve is connected between master cylinder rear outlet and rear wheel circuits to modulate hydraulic pressure and prevent rear lockup.

caption: Fig. BR-2 Brake pedal mounting
description: Brake pedal assembly mounted to pedal bracket under dashboard with stop lamp switch, fulcrum pin, and return spring.
mechanic_notes: Fulcrum pin tightening torque: 3.5 to 4.0 kg-m (25 to 29 ft-lb).

caption: Fig. BR-3 Brake pedal components
description: Exploded view of brake pedal arm, bushings, sleeve, fulcrum bolt, clevis pin, return spring, and pedal pad.
mechanic_notes: Lubricate pedal shaft sleeve unit and clevis pin unit with multi-purpose grease.

caption: Fig. BR-4 Adjusting brake pedal
description: Diagram illustrating brake pedal height measurement from floor to pedal pad upper surface, lock nut, and stopper adjustment.
measurements_and_specs: 206 mm (8.11 in) with pedal stopper non-effected
203 mm (7.99 in) pedal height after stopper adjustment
15 mm (0.59 in) pedal depression for stop lamp switch illumination
mechanic_notes: Turn back stopper to reduce pedal height from 206 mm (8.11 in) to 203 mm (7.99 in).

caption: Fig. BR-5 Master cylinder
description: Exploded view of tandem master cylinder body, front/rear reservoirs, primary and secondary piston assemblies, check valves, and bleeder.
mechanic_notes: NABCO and TOKIKO makes are not interchangeable. Match parts to the brand of the body.

caption: Fig. BR-6 Cross-sectional view of master cylinder
description: Cross-sectional cutaway diagram of tandem master cylinder showing internal passages, primary piston, secondary piston, return springs, check valve, and reservoir fluid ports.
measurements_and_specs: Allowable cylinder to piston clearance: max 0.15 mm (0.0059 in)
mechanic_notes: Apply clean brake fluid to cylinder bore and pistons, and light rubber grease to piston cups during reassembly.

caption: Fig. BR-7 Brake line
description: Schematic routing of galvanized steel brake tubes, flexible pressure hoses, 3-way connectors, NP-valve, and bridge tubes across chassis.
measurements_and_specs: Brake tube tightening torque: 1.5 to 1.8 kg-m (11 to 13 ft-lb)
Pressure hose tightening torque: 1.7 to 2.0 kg-m (12 to 14 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Use flare nut torque wrench GG94310000. Ensure hoses do not contact tires or suspension members during steering and travel.

caption: Fig. BR-8 Cross-sectional view of NP-valve
description: Cutaway diagram of NP-valve (proportioning valve) showing internal plunger, lip seal, cup seal, spring, Y-seal, and inlet/outlet fluid paths.
mechanic_notes: Port connections: Master cylinder front side, Master cylinder rear side, To front wheel cylinder, To rear wheel cylinder.

caption: Fig. BR-9 NP-valve
description: External view of NP-valve showing body mounting and direction arrow mark for correct line installation.
mechanic_notes: Connect brake lines with 'F' mark toward front brake side and with arrow mark toward rear brake side.

caption: Fig. BR-10 Front disc brake
description: Exploded view of Girling-Sumitomo model S-16 front disc brake caliper assembly, pistons, seals, dust covers, pads, shims, and retaining hardware.
mechanic_notes: Anti-squeal shims are directional; install with arrow mark pointing in rotor forward rotating direction.

caption: Fig. BR-11 Piston seal automatic adjusting operation
description: Cross-sectional diagrams illustrating elastic deformation of piston seal during compression and return retraction during decompression.
mechanic_notes: Movement exceeding elastic displacement slips along seal surface for auto-adjustment; seal returns piston upon decompression.

caption: Fig. BR-12 Removing pad
description: Removal procedure of retaining clip, pin, anti-squeal spring, and brake pad from caliper.
mechanic_notes: Remove clip, slide out retaining pin, take off anti-squeal spring, then extract pads with shims.

caption: Fig. BR-13 Applying grease
description: Illustration indicating shaded areas on caliper guides and both sides of anti-squeal shims where brake grease must be applied, showing rotation arrow on shim.
mechanic_notes: Apply pad grease to working portions of caliper and both sides of shim. Ensure shim arrow points in forward rotor rotation direction. Never grease pad friction faces.

caption: Fig. BR-14 Removing calipers
description: Removing brake hydraulic line and two caliper mounting bolts from knuckle spindle.
measurements_and_specs: Caliper installation bolt torque: 7.3 to 9.9 kg-m (53 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Use flare nut wrench on brake line.

caption: Fig. BR-15 Removing piston
description: Applying compressed air to caliper fluid inlet while retaining ring is removed to expel pistons.
mechanic_notes: Gradually apply compressed air. Hold smoother piston with wood block to extract both pistons evenly.

caption: Fig. BR-16 Measuring runout
description: Dial indicator setup positioned at rotor pad contact surface centerline to measure total indicator runout while turning rotor.
measurements_and_specs: Runout limit: 0.10 mm (0.0039 in) Total indicator reading
mechanic_notes: Wheel bearings must be correctly adjusted prior to runout measurement.

caption: Fig. BR-17 Measuring parallelism
description: Micrometer measurement taken around the circumference of brake rotor pad contact surface to determine parallelism / thickness variation.
measurements_and_specs: Parallelism limit: Less than 0.03 mm (0.0012 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure thickness at multiple points around entire periphery on the same circumference.

caption: Fig. BR-18 Rear brake
description: Exploded view of leading-trailing rear drum brake showing backing plate, wheel cylinder, brake shoes, return springs, anti-rattle pins, toggle lever, and automatic adjuster.
mechanic_notes: Front shoe lining is low; rear shoe lining is high. Fore-shoe is in trailing side and after-shoe is in leading side.

caption: Fig. BR-19 Sectional view of rear brake
description: Cross-sectional assembly drawing of rear drum brake mechanism showing wheel cylinder, shoe web engagement, adjuster strut, and drum contact.
mechanic_notes: Shows alignment of automatic adjuster strut between leading and trailing shoes.

caption: Fig. BR-20 Adjuster assembly (Left-hand side)
description: Exploded detail of left-hand brake automatic adjuster assembly, including threaded adjusting screw, sleeve, toggle lever, ratchet claw, and pivot pin.
mechanic_notes: Adjuster mechanisms differ between LH and RH sides; threads are side-specific.

caption: Fig. BR-21 Removing toggle lever stopper
description: Technique for removing cotter pin and stopper from toggle lever through the backing plate aperture when brake drum is stuck.
mechanic_notes: Fully pull up center hand brake lever, push/tap out cotter pin to release stopper, then release lever to slacken shoes for drum removal.

caption: Fig. BR-22 Applying brake grease
description: Lube points on brake shoes, adjuster assembly, adjusting nut threads, and toggle lever contacts indicated by bold arrows.
mechanic_notes: Apply brake grease to adjuster sliding slots, threaded screw shaft, and shoe web contact tips. Do not contaminate friction linings.

caption: Fig. BR-23 Applying brake grease
description: Six lubrication points on the rear brake backing plate (brake disc) ledges and anchor block where brake shoe edges slide.
mechanic_notes: Apply thin layer of brake grease to the 6 shoe ledge contact pads on backing plate and anchor block.

caption: Fig. BR-24 Removing wheel cylinder
description: Disconnection of rear hydraulic brake line and removal of two wheel cylinder mounting bolts on backing plate.
measurements_and_specs: Wheel cylinder bolt torque: 0.6 to 0.8 kg-m (4.3 to 5.8 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Use flare nut wrench on brake line fitting.

caption: Fig. BR-25 Wheel cylinder and adjustor
description: Exploded view of rear wheel cylinder body, bleeder screw, dust boot, piston, cup seal, spring, and automatic adjuster strut with toggle lever.
mechanic_notes: NABCO and TOKIKO wheel cylinders are not interchangeable. Match parts by manufacturer.

caption: Fig. BR-26 Applying rubber grease to piston cup
description: Cross section of wheel cylinder piston cup assembly showing application points for rubber grease along lip groove and sealing contact.
mechanic_notes: Apply rubber grease to cup grooves and lips prior to inserting into cylinder.

caption: Fig. BR-27 Hand brake linkage
description: Component layout of parking brake linkage showing control lever, front rod, center lever, equalizer, rear cables, wire hangers, and adjusting rod.
mechanic_notes: Linkage is located inside tunnel; propeller shaft removal required for access.

caption: Fig. BR-30 Removing control lever
description: Removal of center console boot fasteners and control lever pivot mounting bolt from passenger compartment floor.
mechanic_notes: Remove right-hand seat to remove control lever into cabin.

caption: Fig. BR-28 Removal of hand brake
description: Under-chassis view showing disconnection of adjusting rod nut, clevis pins, hanger spring, and four mounting bolts of center arm.
mechanic_notes: Center arm nuts are welded to floor panel.

caption: Fig. BR-29 Removing rear cable
description: Disconnection of parking brake cable from wheel brake backing plate toggle lever and removal of cable housing retainer clips.
mechanic_notes: Remove wheel-side retainers and equalizer-side retainer to withdraw cable.

caption: Fig. BR-31 Cross-sectional view of Master-Vac
description: Comparative cross-sectional cutaways of both M75 type (top) and M90 type (bottom) vacuum brake boosters detailing internal valves, reaction disc, power piston, and return springs.
components: Power piston (Valve body and diaphragm plate)

callouts.5: Power piston (Valve body and diaphragm plate)

mechanic_notes: M75 type fitted to 2-seater models; M90 type fitted to 2+2 GS30 models.

caption: Fig. BR-32 Installing vacuum gauge
description: Connecting vacuum test gauge into line between check valve and Master-Vac booster.
measurements_and_specs: Max allowable drop in 15 sec: 25 mmHg (0.98 inHg)
mechanic_notes: Engine stopped at 500 mmHg; monitor drop after 15 seconds without braking and with full braking force.

caption: Fig. BR-33 Removing check valve
description: Location and removal of brake booster vacuum line check valve from engine compartment.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect spring clips at both ends to remove check valve.

caption: Fig. BR-34 Cross-sectional view of check valve
description: Cutaway view of check valve showing internal valve disc, spring, and flow direction from Master-Vac side to manifold side.
measurements_and_specs: Max allowable leak at 500 mmHg in 15 sec: 10 mmHg (0.39 inHg)
mechanic_notes: One-way flow only: opens towards intake manifold side.

caption: Fig. BR-35 Performance curve of Master-Vac (M90 type)
description: Output performance graph for M90 (9-inch) booster plotting brake fluid pressure (psi, kg/cm²) against pedal operating force (kg, lb) at 500 mmHg and 0 mmHg vacuum.
mechanic_notes: Knee point occurs at approximately 25-30 kg pedal force with 500 mmHg vacuum.

caption: Fig. BR-36 Performance curve of Master-Vac (M75 type)
description: Output performance graph for M75 (7.5-inch) booster plotting brake fluid pressure against pedal force at 500 mmHg and 0 mmHg vacuum.
mechanic_notes: Knee point occurs at approximately 30-35 kg pedal force with 500 mmHg vacuum.

caption: Fig. BR-37 Removal method of Master-Vac
description: Numbered sequence for disconnecting pedal return spring, clevis pin, master cylinder nuts, and Master-Vac firewall mounting nuts.
mechanic_notes: Remove in numerical order 1 to 6.

caption: Fig. BR-38 Removing rear shell
description: Removal of operating rod clevis, lock nut, and rubber valve body guard.
mechanic_notes: Remove clevis, lock nut, and guard prior to unscrewing rear shell.

caption: Fig. BR-39 Removing rear shell
description: Using special tool Master-Vac Wrench ST08080000 to rotate and unlock rear shell from front shell lugs.
mechanic_notes: Turn tool counterclockwise to disengage interlocking shell tabs.

caption: Fig. BR-40 Removing seal
description: Prying off oil seal assembly from rear shell housing using a flat screwdriver.
mechanic_notes: Do not disassemble seal unless necessary; avoid scratching rear shell seat.

caption: Fig. BR-41 Separating diaphragm
description: Peeling rubber diaphragm bead out of the annular groove in bakelite diaphragm plate.
mechanic_notes: Detach diaphragm bead carefully to avoid tearing.

caption: Fig. BR-42 Removing air silencer retainer
description: Prying air silencer retainer evenly out of diaphragm plate using screwdriver blade.
mechanic_notes: Never tap screwdriver with a hammer; pry evenly around retainer.

caption: Fig. BR-43 Pulling out stop key
description: Extracting valve plunger stop key from valve body hub while vibrating push rod.
mechanic_notes: Point key hole downward, lightly push rod and vibrate to disengage stop key.

caption: Fig. BR-44 Removing valve operating rod assembly
description: Withdrawing valve operating rod, silencer elements, and air valve plunger assembly from power piston.
mechanic_notes: Rod and plunger assembly are staked together and cannot be disassembled.

caption: Fig. BR-45 Removing reaction disc
description: Removing rubber reaction disc from center cavity of diaphragm plate.
mechanic_notes: Always replace reaction disc with a new one at each reassembly.

caption: Fig. BR-46 Removing spacer
description: Detaching mounting stud spacer from front shell housing using screwdriver.
mechanic_notes: Pry spacer off front shell studs.

caption: Fig. BR-47 Installing oil seal
description: Pressing oil seal into rear shell using drift tool ST08090000 (9") or ST08060000 (7.5").
measurements_and_specs: Length 'A': 10.2 to 10.8 mm (0.402 to 0.425 in) for 9 in dia
Length 'A': 6.7 to 7.0 mm (0.264 to 0.276 in) for 7.5 in dia
mechanic_notes: Align tool pawl with seal hole; drive until specified protrusion 'A' is achieved.

caption: Fig. BR-48 Length at "A"
description: Cross section showing seal depth dimension 'A' measured from retainer edge in rear shell.
measurements_and_specs: Length 'A': 10.2 to 10.8 mm (0.402 to 0.425 in) for 228.60 mm (9 in) diaphragm
Length 'A': 6.7 to 7.0 mm (0.264 to 0.276 in) for 190.50 mm (7.5 in) diaphragm
mechanic_notes: Critical seal press depth dimension A.

caption: Fig. BR-49 Requiring grease place
description: Arrows pointing to outer cylindrical sliding surfaces of plunger assembly requiring Master-Vac grease.
mechanic_notes: Apply thin coat of Master-Vac grease to sliding periphery of plunger assembly.

caption: Fig. BR-50 Inserting stop key
description: Pushing valve plunger stop key home into slot of bakelite diaphragm plate.
mechanic_notes: Diaphragm plate is bakelite; insert key gently without cracking plate.

caption: Fig. BR-51 Tightening rear shell
description: Turning rear shell clockwise using wrench ST08080000 until locking notches engage front shell tabs.
mechanic_notes: Align scribe marks, turn clockwise until tool reaches notch in shell retainer.

caption: Fig. BR-52 Length at "B"
description: Diagram illustrating push rod tip protrusion dimension 'B' beyond booster front shell mounting face.
mechanic_notes: Adjust push rod tip length to 9.75 to 10.00 mm before mounting master cylinder.

caption: Fig. BR-53 Adjusting push rod length
description: Holding push rod serrations with pliers while turning adjusting screw tip with wrench.
mechanic_notes: Lock push rod body securely to prevent turning inner diaphragm while adjusting tip.

caption: GG94310000 Flare nut torque wrench
description: Special flare nut torque wrench designed for hydraulic brake line fittings.
mechanic_notes: Prevents rounding of flare nuts on tubing joints.

caption: ST08080000 Master-Vac wrench
description: Spanner wrench with locating pins to engage Master-Vac rear shell for opening and closing booster halves.
mechanic_notes: Used to twist and lock rear shell to front shell notches.

caption: ST08060000 Master-Vac oil seal retainer drift (4.5", 6", 7.5")
description: Flanged driver drift with alignment pawl for installing oil seal to precise depth 'A' in 7.5-inch Master-Vac rear shell.
measurements_and_specs: Depth A: 6.7 to 7.0 mm (0.264 to 0.276 in)
mechanic_notes: Applicable to 7 1/2" Master-Vac on 2-seater models.

caption: ST08090000 Master-Vac oil seal retainer drift (9")
