description: Flanged driver drift with alignment pawl for installing oil seal to precise depth 'A' in 9-inch Master-Vac rear shell.
measurements_and_specs: Depth A: 10.2 to 10.8 mm (0.402 to 0.425 in)
mechanic_notes: Applicable to 9" Master-Vac on 2+2 seater models.

caption: Fig. CL-1 Construction of clutch
description: Cross-sectional cutaway drawing showing the construction and major internal components of the assembled clutch unit on the flywheel, including diaphragm spring, pressure plate, disc, and release bearing sleeve.
mechanic_notes: All dimensions indicated in mm (in). S30 2-seater uses C225S (225 mm OD); GS30 2+2 uses D240K (240 mm OD).

caption: Fig. CL-2 Supporting clutch assembly
description: Illustration showing Clutch Aligning Bar KV30100100 inserted through the clutch disc hub and cover to support the assembly weight during removal and installation.
mechanic_notes: Insert alignment tool until fully seated to prevent disc damage when loosening cover bolts.

caption: Fig. CL-3 Measuring clutch lining
description: Measurement of clutch lining wear using a depth gauge to measure depth from friction surface to rivet head.

callouts.Above 0.3 mm (0.012 in): Allowable minimum depth to rivet head

mechanic_notes: Replace disc when facings are worn down to less than 0.3 mm (0.012 in) above rivet head.

caption: Fig. CL-4 Repairing disc runout
description: Clutch disc mounted on mandrel/lathe with dial gauge measuring runout at radius R, and bending tool used to correct runout.

callouts.R: Radius from hub center for runout inspection

mechanic_notes: Never hold disc plate forcibly with pliers or bend excessively to avoid cracking facing.

caption: Fig. CL-5 Measuring the height of diaphragm spring
description: Cross-sectional setup of clutch cover assembly mounted to Base Plate ST20050010 with Distance Piece ST20050100 and Set Bolts ST20050051 for measuring spring height A.

callouts.A: Diaphragm spring height

measurements_and_specs: Height A (C225S): 33 to 35 mm (1.30 to 1.38 in)
Height A (D240K): 37.5 to 39.5 mm (1.48 to 1.56 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure height A at several points around the fingers with vernier depth gauge.

caption: Fig. CL-6 Adjusting spring height
description: Technician using Diaphragm Spring Adjusting Wrench ST20050240 to pry and bend diaphragm spring fingers to uniform height.
mechanic_notes: Carefully pry fingers up or down to bring all tips within 0.5 mm height tolerance.

caption: Fig. CL-7 Installing clutch cover assembly
description: Installation cross-section of clutch disc and cover assembly onto flywheel using Clutch Aligning Bar KV30100100.
mechanic_notes: Keep disc facings, flywheel and pressure plate clean and dry.

caption: Fig. CL-8 Removing clutch release mechanism
description: View of the clutch housing interior showing removal of the release mechanism components.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect holder spring before withdrawing sleeve assembly.

caption: Fig. CL-9 Disassembling release bearing
description: Technician using universal puller and adapter plates to pull the release bearing off the bearing sleeve.
mechanic_notes: Support bearing sleeve properly while pulling bearing.

caption: Fig. CL-10 Installing release bearing
description: Press setup pressing release bearing onto sleeve, applying force only to inner race.
mechanic_notes: Do not press outer race. Press only on inner race.

caption: Fig. CL-11 Lubricating recess of bearing sleeve
description: Cross section of bearing sleeve indicating inner recess to be packed with multi-purpose grease.

callouts.Pack this recess: Inner annular grease recess in bearing sleeve

mechanic_notes: Pack inner groove lightly with multi-purpose grease.

caption: Fig. CL-12 Lubricating points of withdrawal lever and front cover
description: Diagram showing contact points on withdrawal lever fork ends, ball pin pivot socket, and transmission front cover nose to lubricate.
mechanic_notes: Apply very light coat of multi-purpose grease; avoid excess.

caption: Fig. CL-13 Removing pilot bushing
description: Removal of pilot bushing from rear crankshaft bore using Pilot Bushing Puller ST16610001 (Kent-Moore J 23907).
mechanic_notes: Expand puller jaws inside bushing and turn center bolt to extract.

caption: Fig. CL-14 Installing pilot bushing
description: Cross-sectional drawing showing the installation depth of the pilot bushing into the crankshaft bore.
mechanic_notes: Bushing need not be oiled. Drive in squarely with a soft hammer/drift to specified depth.

caption: Fig. CL-15 Clutch operating system
description: Schematic diagram of the complete hydraulic clutch control linkage and operating system from pedal to clutch disc.
wiring_and_connections: Hydraulic line connecting master cylinder to operating cylinder
mechanic_notes: Operating cylinder is non-adjustable; pedal depression directly actuates master cylinder and slave cylinder.

caption: Fig. CL-16 Non-adjustable operating cylinder
description: Internal cross-section of the non-adjustable clutch operating cylinder showing piston stroke and automatic compensation dimension S.
mechanic_notes: Non-adjustable design uses dimension S to self-adjust as clutch disc facing wears.

caption: Fig. CL-17 Pedal height adjustment
description: Side view schematic of clutch pedal linkage showing pedal height measurement b, free play a, lock nuts A and B, pedal stopper, and lubrication points.

callouts.a: Free play: 1.0 to 5.0 mm (0.039 to 0.197 in)

measurements_and_specs: Free play (a): 1.0 to 5.0 mm (0.039 to 0.197 in)
Lock nut A torque: 0.8 to 1.2 kg-m (5.8 to 8.7 ft-lb)
Lock nut B torque: 0.8 to 1.2 kg-m (5.8 to 8.7 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: First adjust pedal height with stopper bolt (lock nut A), then adjust free play with push rod (lock nut B). Measure free play on top face of pedal pad.

caption: Fig. CL-18 Exploded view of clutch pedal
description: Exploded view drawing of the clutch pedal assembly, fulcrum pin, bushings, return spring, and clevis connection.
measurements_and_specs: Fulcrum pin torque: 3.5 to 4.8 kg-m (25 to 35 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Measure pedal height from toe board before disassembly. Grease clevis pin friction surfaces.

caption: Fig. CL-19 Exploded view of master cylinder
description: Detailed exploded view of clutch master cylinder and internal valve components.
mechanic_notes: Never detach reservoir from cylinder body. Always renew rubber cups upon disassembly.

caption: Fig. CL-20 Operating cylinder
description: Operating cylinder mounted on clutch housing, connected to clutch hydraulic hose and withdrawal lever.
mechanic_notes: Keep clutch hose routed away from exhaust pipe.

caption: Fig. CL-21 Exploded view of operating cylinder
description: Exploded diagram of the clutch slave operating cylinder and internal components.
mechanic_notes: Pay attention to cup direction when sliding over piston. Discard old cup and dust boot.

caption: KV30100100 Clutch aligning bar
description: Special service tool drawing of clutch aligning arbor KV30100100.
mechanic_notes: Used to align and center clutch disc with pilot bushing and cover during assembly.

caption: ST20050240 Diaphragm adjusting wrench
description: Special service tool drawing of slotted diaphragm spring toe bending wrench ST20050240.
mechanic_notes: Used to pry diaphragm spring fingers to uniform height.

caption: ST20050100 Distance piece
description: Special service tool drawing of ring distance pieces ST20050100 used for clutch cover height measurement.
mechanic_notes: Placed between clutch cover and base plate.

caption: ST16610001 Pilot bushing puller
description: Special service tool drawing of internal expanding collet pilot bushing puller ST16610001 (Kent-Moore J 23907).
mechanic_notes: Extracts pilot bushing from rear crankshaft bore without damaging crank.

caption: ST20050010 Base plate
description: Special service tool drawing of circular fixture base plate ST20050010.
mechanic_notes: Simulates flywheel surface when checking diaphragm spring height.

caption: GG94310000 Flare nut torque wrench
description: Special service tool drawing of flare nut torque wrench and crowfoot adapter GG94310000.
mechanic_notes: Prevents rounding and overtightening of hydraulic tube flare nuts.

caption: ST20050051 Set bolts
description: Special service tool drawing of stepped set bolts ST20050051 used to secure clutch cover to base plate.
mechanic_notes: Secures cover to base plate ST20050010.

caption: Fig. CO-1 Cooling system (Inset: Models equipped with radiator reservoir tank)
description: Cutaway flow diagram of the L28 cooling system showing coolant circulation pathways through the cylinder block, cylinder head, thermostat, water pump, and downflow radiator. Inset at lower-left illustrates configuration for models equipped with a radiator reservoir tank.
measurements_and_specs: Radiator cap preset relief pressure: 0.9 kg/cm² (13 psi)
mechanic_notes: When thermostat is closed, coolant recirculates within block and head for rapid warmup. Once normal operating temperature is achieved, coolant circulates through radiator core.

caption: Fig. CO-2 Water pump and front cover
description: Exploded view showing relationship of centrifugal water pump assembly to engine front cover and integrated volute chamber.
mechanic_notes: Volute chamber is cast directly into front cover assembly. Water pump outer bearing race is press-fit into aluminum body; unit cannot be disassembled.

caption: Fig. CO-3 Removing water pump
description: Procedure diagram showing removal of water pump housing and gasket from front cover of engine.
mechanic_notes: Clean cooling system with suitable cleaner before pump removal. Always replace gasket with a new one upon installation.

caption: Fig. CO-4 Cross-sectional view of Tem-coupling
description: Cross-sectional and front elevation views of temperature-sensing viscous fan coupling (Tem-coupling), showing internal fluid passages, bimetal thermostat, slide valve, and labyrinth drive surfaces.
measurements_and_specs: ON condition fan speed: up to about 2,450 rpm
OFF condition fan slip speed: about 1,600 rpm
mechanic_notes: Coiled bimetal senses radiator discharge air temp. When hot, bimetal expands opening slide valve (2) to deliver silicone oil to labyrinth (6). When cold, valve closes and centrifugal force collects oil back into reserve chamber (3).

caption: Fig. CO-5 Characteristic of Tem-coupling
description: Performance graphs comparing fan speed vs water pump speed for conventional fixed-ratio slip coupling versus variable ON/OFF temperature-controlled Tem-coupling.
mechanic_notes: Tem-coupling limits top fan speed and dramatically cuts power drag and acoustic noise when coolant temperatures are moderate or low.

caption: Fig. CO-6 Removing thermostat
description: Exploded view of thermostat assembly, gasket, water outlet neck, and housing bolted onto cylinder head.
mechanic_notes: Always replace gasket when reassembling. Tighten securing bolts evenly.

caption: Fig. CO-7 Inspecting thermostat
description: Testing thermostat valve opening lift in hot water bath using a screwdriver marked at 8 mm (0.31 in).
measurements_and_specs: Valve lift inspection height: 8 mm (0.31 in)
mechanic_notes: Thermostat cannot be repaired; replace if opening temperature or minimum 8 mm lift is out of specification.

caption: Fig. CO-8 Radiator for manual transmission
description: Perspective view of downflow radiator assembly with top tank, bottom tank, filler neck, hoses, and drain cock for manual transmission models.
measurements_and_specs: Manual transmission capacity: 10.3 liters (10 7/8 US qt, 9 1/8 Imp qt)
mechanic_notes: Automatic transmission radiators additionally integrate a transmission fluid cooler inside the bottom tank.

caption: Fig. CO-9 Radiator shroud (for the model equipped with air conditioner)
description: Two-piece cooling fan shroud design used on factory air-conditioned models.
mechanic_notes: Lower shroud is detached and removed downwards before removing radiator; upper shroud lifts out with radiator.

caption: Fig. CO-10 Testing radiator cap
description: Bench testing radiator cap relief pressure using a hand pump pressure tester and cap adapter.
mechanic_notes: Inspect rubber seal for cracks or hardness. Cap must hold pressure and release at specified relief value.

caption: Fig. CO-11 Testing radiator pressure
description: Cooling system leak detection test using hand pressure pump attached directly to radiator filler neck.
mechanic_notes: Apply 1.6 kg/cm² (23 psi) to locate seam leaks, hose leaks, or core defects. Repair or replace radiator if leaking.

caption: Fig. CO-12 Structural view of cooling system
description: Side elevation structural cross-section showing alignment of radiator, bottom tank oil cooler, water pump, fan, and filler neck.
mechanic_notes: Illustrates packaging of automatic transmission fluid cooler inside the radiator bottom tank.

caption: Fig. CO-13 Operation of reservoir tank
description: Dual diagram illustrating dynamic valving in radiator cap and fluid transfer with reservoir tank during pressure relief and vacuum recovery states.
mechanic_notes: When engine heats up, thermal expansion forces relief valve open into reservoir tank. When cooling down, vacuum valve opens allowing coolant to siphon back into radiator.

caption: Fig. CO-14 Installing reservoir tank
description: Exploded view showing installation of coolant reservoir tank, mounting bracket, hoses, and hardware to front radiator core support.
mechanic_notes: Upper bracket attaches to core support together with radiator; lower bracket mounts with stud bolts. Slide reservoir tank into bracket; take care not to strike or damage radiator fins during assembly.

caption: Fig. EC-1 Crankcase emission control system
description: Cross-sectional cutaway diagram showing crankcase ventilation gas flow routes with P.C.V. valve detail under partial and full throttle conditions.
wiring_and_connections: Ventilation hose between throttle chamber and rocker cover
Hose between crankcase and P.C.V. valve to intake manifold
mechanic_notes: Ensure that flame arrester is surely inserted in hose between throttle chamber and rocker cover. Check for hissing sound and strong vacuum at P.C.V. valve inlet at idle.

caption: Fig. EC-2 Location of emission control system components
description: Phantom vehicle perspective showing layout and locations of all major emission control and EFI components on the Datsun 280Z chassis and engine bay.
mechanic_notes: Shows component locations throughout vehicle including under-hood EFI components, chassis underbody catalytic converter, and passenger cabin / rear fuel system elements.

caption: Fig. EC-3 Schematic drawing of B.C.D.D.
description: Internal pneumatic cutaway and electrical control schematic of the B.C.D.D. unit showing Non-California and California altitude corrector configurations.

callouts.3: Speed detecting switch Below 16 km/h (10 MPH): ON (For M/T)
callouts.4: Inhibitor switch \"N\" or \"P\" position: ON (For A/T)

measurements_and_specs: Speed detecting switch closes below 16 km/h (10 MPH)
wiring_and_connections: Ignition switch to amplifier and solenoid valve
mechanic_notes: California model incorporates altitude corrector with adjusting nut and lock spring; Non-California model utilizes adjusting screw.

caption: Fig. EC-4 Removing B.C.D.D.
description: Illustration of the underside of the throttle chamber indicating which three screws to remove and cautioning against removing the four assembly screws.
measurements_and_specs: Securing screws tightening torque: 20 to 40 kg-cm (17 to 35 in-lb)
mechanic_notes: Do not unscrew the four B.C.D.D. assembly screws (2). Replace B.C.D.D. as an assembly if malfunctioning.

caption: Fig. EC-5 Checking B.C.D.D. circuit with function test connector (for manual transmission)
description: Wiring test diagram and multimeter hookup to terminals A and B of the function test connector for manual transmission vehicles.

callouts.4: Speed detecting switch (Above 10 mph: OFF / Below 10 mph: ON)

wiring_and_connections: Terminals A and B of function test connector
mechanic_notes: Do not attach test leads to terminals other than designated A and B.

caption: Fig. EC-6 Checking B.C.D.D. circuit with function test connector (for automatic transmission)
description: Circuit schematic and tester connection diagram for testing B.C.D.D. via the test connector on automatic transmission models.

callouts.2: Inhibitor switch (N or P position: ON / 1, 2, D or R position: OFF)

measurements_and_specs: Voltage in N or P: 12 V (d-c)
Resistance in gear (1, 2, D, R): 15 to 28 ohms
wiring_and_connections: Terminals A and B of function test connector
mechanic_notes: Check for 12V in N/P and 15 to 28 ohms in drive/reverse ranges across terminals A and B.

caption: Fig. EC-7 Checking solenoid valve
description: Connecting jumper test wire from battery positive terminal to the disconnected B.C.D.D. solenoid valve harness connector to listen for valve click.
mechanic_notes: Turn on ignition key without starting engine, ensure solenoid clicks when energized.

caption: Fig. EC-8 Checking amplifier
description: Circuit schematic showing ammeter connection between ignition key circuit and amplifier to test current draw upon key turn-on.

callouts.3: Speed detecting switch (Above 16 km/h / 10 MPH: OFF, Below 16 km/h / 10 MPH: ON)

measurements_and_specs: Tester range: DC ampere (1A min full scale)
wiring_and_connections: Test probes in series with amplifier circuit
mechanic_notes: Do not confuse positive line with negative line. Tester needle should deflect when ignition is switched ON.

caption: Fig. EC-9 Removing harness of solenoid valve
description: Disconnecting the electrical plug harness from the B.C.D.D. vacuum control solenoid valve on the throttle chamber.
mechanic_notes: Always disconnect solenoid harness prior to performing B.C.D.D. operating pressure check or adjustment.

caption: Fig. EC-10 Connecting vacuum gauge
description: Vacuum gauge connection via rubber hose tee to the intake manifold vacuum fitting.
measurements_and_specs: Quick-response Bourdon type boost gauge recommended
wiring_and_connections: Rubber vacuum hose to intake manifold fitting
mechanic_notes: Use Bourdon tube boost gauge for fast response during rapid throttle snapping.

caption: Fig. EC-11 Adjusting operating pressure (California models)
description: Adjusting the B.C.D.D. operating pressure on California models using a wrench on the adjusting nut through the lock spring.
mechanic_notes: Turn adjusting nut in or out with lock spring in place. Always set lock spring properly to prevent drift in operating pressure.

caption: Fig. EC-12 Adjusting operating pressure (Non-California models)
description: Cross-section and screwdriver adjustment of the B.C.D.D. operating pressure adjusting screw on Non-California models.
mechanic_notes: Turn adjusting screw counterclockwise if operating pressure is lower than set level. Clockwise turn decreases vacuum setting.

caption: Fig. EC-13 Changes in operating pressure versus changes in atmospheric pressure and altitude (California models)
description: Engineering graph plotting operating vacuum of B.C.D.D. (mmHg and inHg) against atmospheric pressure and altitude in thousands of feet and kilometers.
components: Operating vacuum scale (300 to 600 mmHg / 12 to 24 inHg)
Atmospheric pressure scale (450 to 750 mmHg / 18 to 30 inHg)
Altitude scale (0 to 6000 ft / 0 to 2.0 km)

callouts.A: Arrow line tracing from atmospheric pressure

mechanic_notes: Use trace line A when atmospheric pressure is known, trace line B when altitude is known.

caption: Fig. EC-14 E.G.R. control system
description: Functional schematic diagram of the complete E.G.R. circuit showing routing between intake manifold, throttle chamber, E.G.R. valve, B.P.T. valve, thermal vacuum valve, and exhaust manifold.
measurements_and_specs: Operating range: water temp 50 to 95°C (122 to 203°F)
B.P.T. valve exhaust threshold: 21 to 33 mmH2O (0.82 to 1.30 inH2O)
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum lines between throttle chamber, thermal vacuum valve, B.P.T. valve, and E.G.R. control valve
Exhaust pressure sensing line to B.P.T. valve
mechanic_notes: E.G.R. is deactivated at idle and full throttle. California models include vacuum delay valve (8).

caption: Fig. EC-15 E.G.R. control valve
description: Cross-sectional detail of the E.G.R. control valve showing internal diaphragm, spring, valve shaft, valve seat, and valve chamber.
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum port on top of diaphragm chamber
mechanic_notes: Inspect diaphragm for leaks and valve stem for sticking or carbon deposits.

caption: Fig. EC-16 Thermal vacuum valve
description: Sectional views of the thermal vacuum valve at three temperature states: below 47-53°C (closed), 50-95°C (open), and above 92-98°C (closed).
mechanic_notes: Wax element expands to open valve in normal range and closes valve above overheating threshold.

caption: Fig. EC-17 B.P.T. valve
description: Cross-sectional cutaway of the back-pressure transducer (B.P.T.) valve showing air filter, diaphragm, exhaust pressure port, and air bleed.
measurements_and_specs: Actuation pressure: 21 to 33 mmH2O (0.82 to 1.30 inH2O)
mechanic_notes: Diaphragm bleeds air to vent vacuum until sufficient exhaust backpressure pushes diaphragm closed.

caption: Fig. EC-18 Vacuum delay valve
description: Installation orientation and hose routing of the vacuum delay valve located between thermal vacuum valve (brown side) and B.P.T. valve (black side).
wiring_and_connections: Brown side connected toward thermal vacuum valve
Black side connected toward B.P.T. valve
mechanic_notes: Pay strict attention to valve color orientation: Brown side faces thermal vacuum valve, Black side faces B.P.T. valve.

caption: Fig. EC-19 Operation of vacuum delay valve
description: Flow direction schematic of vacuum delay valve showing open umbrella flow toward thermal vacuum valve and restricted flow toward B.P.T. valve.
mechanic_notes: One-way operation allows rapid flow during release and restricted flow during vacuum application.

caption: Fig. EC-20 Removing E.G.R. control valve
description: Removal of E.G.R. control valve nuts from intake manifold studs and vacuum hose disconnection.
wiring_and_connections: Flatten hose clip to disconnect vacuum hose
mechanic_notes: Flatten clip connecting vacuum hose to E.G.R. control valve and remove hose by hand. Replace gasket upon reassembly.

caption: Fig. EC-21 Removing B.P.T. valve
description: Dismounting B.P.T. valve and control tube from intake manifold bracket.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect both vacuum hoses and unbolt B.P.T. valve from bracket.

caption: Fig. EC-22 Removing thermal vacuum valve
description: Removal and installation angle of thermal vacuum valve threaded into heater housing at 30 degree tilt angle.
mechanic_notes: Install thermal vacuum valve at a tilt angle of 30° as shown. Tighten to 2.2 kg-m (16 ft-lb) max. Drain coolant before removal.

caption: Fig. EC-23 Checking thermal vacuum valve
description: Checking vacuum presence at the hose disconnected from the thermal vacuum valve with finger while engine is revved.
wiring_and_connections: Hose disconnected at B.P.T. valve side
mechanic_notes: Ensure throttle chamber vacuum is felt with finger when engine is warm (50 to 95°C) at 3,000-3,500 rpm.

caption: Fig. EC-24 Checking B.P.T. valve
description: Checking for vacuum at the disconnected hose from the B.P.T. valve leading to the E.G.R. valve at 3,000 to 3,500 rpm.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum should be present when operating properly
wiring_and_connections: Hose disconnected at E.G.R. valve side
mechanic_notes: If vacuum is not present at hose end during 3,000 to 3,500 rpm rev, replace B.P.T. valve.

caption: Fig. EC-25 Checking E.G.R. control valve
description: Feeling diaphragm of E.G.R. control valve with finger to confirm movement when revving engine from idle to 3,000-3,500 rpm.
mechanic_notes: Place finger under diaphragm to feel upward movement as engine is revved. If it does not move, replace valve.

caption: Fig. EC-26 Checking thermal vacuum valve
description: Blowing air orally through thermal vacuum valve submerged in heated water bath to verify opening and closing temperatures.
mechanic_notes: Do not allow water to get inside the thermal vacuum valve while heating.

caption: Fig. EC-27 Checking vacuum delay valve
description: Testing vacuum delay valve by blowing orally from each side while covering opposite port with finger.
mechanic_notes: Resistance should be greater when blowing from B.P.T. valve side with thermal valve side covered.

caption: Fig. EC-28 Checking vacuum delay valve
description: Submerging B.P.T. side port into cup of water while blowing through the other port to observe small air bubbles.
mechanic_notes: Small air bubbles indicate proper orifice flow. Avoid oil or dirt entering valve.

caption: Fig. EC-29 Checking B.P.T. valve
description: Testing B.P.T. valve leakage by applying pressure above 50 mmH2O to lower fitting while orally sucking vacuum port.
mechanic_notes: If leakage occurs while sucking port back under applied pressure, replace valve.

caption: Fig. EC-30 Checking E.G.R. control valve
description: Testing E.G.R. valve diaphragm and seat by applying oral vacuum suction to vacuum hose port.
measurements_and_specs: Hold time: > 30 seconds after vacuum is cut off
mechanic_notes: Valve must open fully and hold open position for more than 30 seconds after sealing hose.

caption: Fig. EC-31 Cleaning E.G.R. control valve
description: Cleaning carbon deposits from the E.G.R. control valve seating surface using a wire brush.
mechanic_notes: Clean seating surface and port with brush and compressed air. Check for wrinkles or deformation.

caption: Fig. EC-32 Location of catalytic converter
description: Vehicle side profile outline indicating catalytic converter position in the exhaust system under the floorpan.
mechanic_notes: California models only. Positioned under passenger floor area in exhaust line.

caption: Fig. EC-33 Operation of catalytic converter
description: Flow diagram showing exhaust gases (HC, CO) mixing with excess air from exhaust manifold through catalytic converter bed to form CO2 and H2O.
mechanic_notes: Catalyst promotes oxidation of unburned hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide using residual excess oxygen.

caption: Fig. EC-34 Removing catalytic converter
description: Unbolting catalytic converter flange bolts connecting to front and rear exhaust tubes and lower heat shelter.
mechanic_notes: Never wet catalyzer with water or oil. Handle carefully to prevent internal ceramic fracture.

caption: Fig. EC-35 Connecting emission adjuster
description: Connecting the variable resistance emission adjuster tool to the disconnected water temperature sensor harness connector.
measurements_and_specs: Probe insertion depth: minimum 500 mm (19.69 in)
Pass criterion with #6 injector disconnected: < 1% CO
wiring_and_connections: Emission adjuster plugged into water temp sensor harness
mechanic_notes: Simulate rich condition with emission adjuster, then cut #6 cylinder; CO must drop below 1% if catalyst is active.

caption: Fig. EC-36 Floor temperature warning system circuit
description: Schematic of floor temperature warning circuit showing battery, ignition switch, ignition relay, floor sensor relay, floor sensor, and floor temperature lamp.
wiring_and_connections: Ignition switch B, IG, S, A terminals
mechanic_notes: Floor sensor acts as normally closed contact at low temperature; opens when overheated, de-energizing relay and illuminating warning lamp.

caption: Fig. EC-37 Location of floor sensor
description: Chassis elevation outline showing location of the floor temperature sensor mounted above catalytic converter floor area.
mechanic_notes: Sensor is located under passenger floor carpet area above the exhaust pipe / catalytic converter section.

caption: Fig. EC-38 Operation of floor sensor
description: Internal bimetal mechanism of the floor sensor showing contacts closed (normal) and contacts open (overheated condition).
mechanic_notes: Bimetallic disc snaps open at elevated floor temperatures, breaking relay coil ground.

caption: Fig. EC-39 Removing floor sensor
description: Interior passenger footwell view showing removal of floor protector and sensor screws.
mechanic_notes: Remove protective cover before loosening floor sensor mounting screws.

caption: Fig. EC-40 Location of floor sensor relay
description: Perspective drawing showing floor sensor relay and brake warning lamp check relay mounted beneath passenger seat.
wiring_and_connections: Relay harness plug under passenger seat
mechanic_notes: Remove front passenger seat to access the floor sensor relay on seat bracket.

caption: Fig. EC-41 Location of floor temperature lamp
description: Dashboard center console view showing location of FLOOR TEMP warning light lens on heater/vent finisher panel.
mechanic_notes: Remove center console instrument finisher panel to replace bulb or warning unit.

caption: Fig. EC-42 Wiring diagram of floor temperature warning system
description: Complete schematic diagram of floor temperature warning system showing wire colors, connector pinouts, battery, fusible links, starting motor, ignition switch, fuse box, ignition relay, floor sensor relay, floor sensor, and floor temperature warning lamp.
mechanic_notes: Shows all multi-pin harness connectors, wire color coding, and relay pin numbers for floor temperature warning circuitry.

caption: Fig. EC-43 Floor temperature warning lamp ON with ignition switch in \"START\" position
description: Current flow path through circuit diagram when ignition switch is in START position, proving bulb bulb-check functionality.
wiring_and_connections: BY line energized from STA terminal to illuminate warning lamp during cranking
mechanic_notes: Heavy lines trace circuit from starter terminal through warning lamp to ground during cranking.

caption: Fig. EC-44 Floor temperature warning lamp ON with floor sensor turned OFF
description: Current flow path when floor sensor bimetal opens (OFF state), de-energizing relay and routing 12V through relay normally-closed contacts to warning lamp.
wiring_and_connections: Current flow traced through de-energized relay contacts to lamp
mechanic_notes: When sensor heats above 115°C, its internal contact opens, cutting relay coil ground; relay returns to NC position and lights bulb.

caption: Fig. EC-45 Checking floor sensor relay
description: Terminal pin numbering and internal coil/switch diagram of the floor sensor relay for bench continuity testing.
measurements_and_specs: Terminals 2-4: NC contact (Yes normal, No energized)
Terminals 1-3: NO contact (No normal, Yes energized)
wiring_and_connections: 12V DC applied across coil terminals 5 and 6
mechanic_notes: Use fused test lead when energizing terminals 5 and 6.

caption: Fig. EC-46 Schematic drawing of evaporative emission control system
description: Chassis perspective view showing complete evaporative plumbing: fuel tank, filler cap, separator, vapor lines, check valve, and canister.
components: Fuel filler cap with vacuum relief valve

callouts.5: Fuel filler cap with vacuum relief valve

wiring_and_connections: Plumbing lines connecting rear separator, underbody vapor line, and engine compartment canister
mechanic_notes: Fuel tank is sealed with a vacuum relief filler cap. Vapors pass through liquid/vapor separator and check valve to canister.

caption: Fig. EC-47 Evaporative emission control system (Fuel vapor flow when engine is at rest or at idling)
description: Functional flow schematic at rest or idle showing vapor trapped in activated carbon while purge control valve remains closed.
components: Fuel filler cap with vacuum relief valve

callouts.2: Fuel filler cap with vacuum relief valve

mechanic_notes: At rest or idle, purge control valve diaphragm spring holds valve closed so vapors are retained in activated carbon.

caption: Fig. EC-48 Evaporative emission control system (Fuel vapor flow when engine is running)
description: Functional flow schematic showing purge control valve opened by port vacuum during running conditions, admitting fresh air through canister bottom and purging vapors to intake manifold.
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum signal line to throttle chamber port
Purge line to intake manifold port
mechanic_notes: Throttle vacuum lifts diaphragm against spring, pulling fresh air through canister bottom filter and purging absorbed vapors into engine.

caption: Fig. EC-49 Checking evaporative emission control system
description: Apparatus setup for pressure testing vapor vent line, separator, and tank using manometer, 3-way connector cock, and hand air pump.
measurements_and_specs: Max allowable pressure drop: 25 mmH2O (0.98 inH2O) over 2.5 minutes
wiring_and_connections: Manometer tee connected to disconnected vent line at canister
mechanic_notes: If pressure drops immediately, filler cap or vent hoses leak. If pressure does not drop when cap removed, line is clogged.

caption: Fig. EC-50 Checking carbon canister purge control valve
description: Inhaling oral suction on disconnected rubber hose to canister purge control valve diaphragm port to check for diaphragm leakage.
mechanic_notes: There must be no leakage when inhaling on hose. If leaking, replace diaphragm kit.

caption: Fig. EC-51 Carbon canister purge control valve
description: Exploded view of the purge control valve assembly on top of the carbon canister.
mechanic_notes: Diaphragm kit consists of retainer, diaphragm, and spring.

caption: Fig. EC-52 Replacing carbon canister filter
description: Hand removal and replacement of the fibrous bottom filter pad of the carbon canister.
mechanic_notes: Filter pad is easily pulled out from bottom recess of canister body when dirty.

caption: Fig. EC-53 Fuel filler cap
description: Cross-sectional cutaway of fuel filler cap vacuum relief valve mechanism showing internal spring and sealing gasket.
mechanic_notes: Oral inhalation should produce slight resistance then click as valve opens. Replace cap if clogged or free-leaking.

caption: Fig. EC-54 Checking fuel check valve
description: Cross-sectional flow diagram of two-way fuel check valve showing differential resistance between fuel tank side and engine side.
mechanic_notes: Air blown into engine side should flow freely toward tank; air blown into tank side should show considerable resistance.

caption: Fig. EE-1 Checking specific gravity
description: Illustration of checking battery electrolyte specific gravity and temperature using a hydrometer and a thermal gauge inserted into the battery cells.
mechanic_notes: Insert hydrometer vertically into cell; ensure float moves freely without clinging to sides.

caption: Fig. EE-2 Checking specific gravity
description: Close-up diagram showing how to read the top level of the hydrometer float with scale at eye level.
mechanic_notes: Read the scale line aligned with the surface meniscus of the electrolyte.

caption: Fig. EE-3 Charging condition
description: Graph showing relationship between specific gravity at 20°C (68°F) (1.06 to 1.28) and charging condition percentage (0% to 100%). Lines indicate max charging specific gravity 1.28 and 1.26.
components: Graph curves for 1.28 and 1.26 specific gravity
mechanic_notes: Recharge if battery charge condition is below 60% or specific gravity is below 1.20.

caption: Fig. EE-4 Specific gravity at electrolyte temperature
description: Nomograph chart for converting specific gravity at electrolyte temperature St (-10°C to 50°C) to converted specific gravity S20 (1.10 to 1.30).

caption: Fig. EE-5 Freezing point of electrolyte
description: Graph showing the freezing point temperature of battery electrolyte (°C and °F) vs specific gravity (1.00 to 1.32), indicating the shaded freezing zone.
mechanic_notes: A discharged battery will freeze and crack the case at normal winter temperatures.

caption: Fig. EE-6 Reduction gear starting motor [S114-254]
description: Cross-sectional cutaway illustration of the Hitachi S114-254 reduction gear starter motor highlighting the planetary/reduction gearing arrangement and brush placement.
mechanic_notes: Pinion gear is located independently of armature; commutator and brushes are located on the pinion/reduction gear side.

caption: Fig. EE-7 Circuit diagram of starting system
description: Complete electrical schematic and harness wiring diagram of the starting system showing battery, fusible links, ignition switch, starting motor, inhibitor switch (A/T only), and ignition / inhibitor relay.

callouts.M: Manual transmission only / Solenoid motor terminal
callouts.A: Automatic transmission only

mechanic_notes: Note: (M) indicates M/T only; (A) indicates A/T only. Inhibitor switch prevents cranking unless A/T is in P or N.

caption: Fig. EE-8 Reduction gear type starting motor
description: Functional schematic diagram showing the internal electrical circuits (series coil, shunt coil, contacts) and mechanical linkages (shift lever, reduction gear, overrunning clutch, pinion gear) of the starter motor.
mechanic_notes: Plunger pulls in and closes movable contactor 6 across stationary contacts 5, cutting out pull-in series coil 10 while hold-in shunt coil 7 maintains engagement.

caption: Fig. EE-9 Reduction gear type starting motor (S114-254)
description: Exploded view diagram of the Hitachi S114-254 starter motor showing all individual components and assembly order.
mechanic_notes: Pay attention to the position of dust covers, packing, O-rings, and adjusting washers during disassembly.

caption: Fig. EE-10 [Removing magnetic switch and center housing]
description: Illustration of detaching the magnetic switch assembly and O-ring/torsion spring from the center housing.
mechanic_notes: Torsion spring can be pulled off magnetic switch after separating.

caption: Fig. EE-11 Removing brush holder
description: Hand illustration demonstrating how to lift the brushes and extract the brush holder assembly from the armature commutator.
mechanic_notes: Lift brush on negative side away from commutator surface to withdraw holder safely.

caption: Fig. EE-12 Removing center housing
description: Illustration of unscrewing bolts securing the center housing to the gear case and detaching the housing.
mechanic_notes: Detach center housing carefully to access pinion gear.

caption: Fig. EE-13 Testing field coil for continuity
description: Ohmmeter probes connected to the two positive terminals of the field coil inside the yoke to check for electrical continuity.
measurements_and_specs: Continuity check: conduction required; open circuit means replace
mechanic_notes: If tester shows no conduction, field coil is open. Replace yoke assembly.

caption: Fig. EE-14 Testing field coil for ground
description: Circuit tester probes applied between the starter yoke body and positive field coil lead to test for insulation breakdown / grounding.
measurements_and_specs: Ground test: high resistance / no continuity required
mechanic_notes: If very little resistance is read, field coil is grounded. Replace yoke assembly.

caption: Fig. EE-15 Inspecting brush spring tension
description: Spring scale hooked to the brush spring clip to measure pull tension at the moment of release from the brush.
measurements_and_specs: Spring tension: 1.6 to 2.0 kg (3.5 to 4.4 lb)
mechanic_notes: Read tension when spring just releases from brush. Replace if outside specification.

caption: Fig. EE-16 Undercutting insulating mica
description: Diagram illustrating proper vs incorrect undercut profiles and depth of commutator segment insulating mica using a file.

callouts.Correct: Proper square cut 0.5 to 0.8 mm deep

mechanic_notes: Undercut must be square at bottom, not V-groove. Deburr copper segments slightly.

caption: Fig. EE-17 Testing armature for ground
description: Circuit tester probes placed between armature shaft/core and commutator segments to detect short to ground.
mechanic_notes: Any continuity between any commutator segment and the core/shaft indicates a bad armature.

caption: Fig. EE-18 Testing armature for short
description: Armature mounted on a growler tester with a thin steel blade held over the core while slowly rotating to check for shorted windings.
mechanic_notes: If the iron blade vibrates or is attracted to the core, armature coil is shorted.

caption: Fig. EE-19 Pinion and reduction gear overrunning clutch
description: Exploded view showing the pinion gear shaft, reduction gear, spring, and washer of the overrunning clutch assembly.
mechanic_notes: Pinion gear shaft must slide freely through reduction gear.

caption: Fig. EE-20 Testing brush for ground
description: Circuit tester probes applied across the brush holder plate between positive and negative sides to check for insulation breakdown.
measurements_and_specs: Continuity indicates ground short (replace brush holder)
mechanic_notes: Ensure positive brush holder is properly insulated from the base plate.

caption: Fig. EE-21 No-load testing
description: Wiring hookup schematic for starter motor no-load test showing 12V battery, high-capacity ammeter (0-1000A), switch, voltmeter, and starter motor terminals S, B, and E.
mechanic_notes: Connect switch between battery positive and starter 'S' terminal; monitor current draw and RPM.

caption: Fig. EE-22 Circuit of magnetic switch assembly test
description: Circuit schematic for testing the starter magnetic switch pull-in: positive battery connects through switch to S terminal, negative battery connects to M terminal.
mechanic_notes: Connect negative battery to M terminal and positive through switch to S terminal to actuate plunger.

caption: Fig. EE-23 Measuring clearance "l"
description: Illustration of measuring pinion gap clearance 'l' between pinion energized position and manual pull-out stop against reduction gear.

callouts.Clearance l: Gap difference between electric stroke and full hand stroke

measurements_and_specs: Clearance l: 0.3 to 1.5 mm (0.012 to 0.059 in)
Adjusting washer sizes: 0.5 mm (0.020 in), 0.8 mm (0.031 in)
mechanic_notes: Adjust clearance by adding or removing washers under magnetic switch mounting.

caption: Fig. EE-24 Simplified charging circuit (1)
description: Simplified circuit schematic (1) showing initial excitation state with ignition switch ON and engine stopped: current flows from battery through charge lamp to rotor coil and Tr1 to ground.
mechanic_notes: Charge warning lamp is illuminated because battery voltage passes through lamp to terminal L and Tr1 to ground.

caption: Fig. EE-25 Simplified charging circuit (2)
description: Simplified charging circuit schematic (2) with alternator running below regulation voltage: stator supplies rotor current via sub-diodes D7-D9; voltage at L equals B so charge lamp turns OFF.
mechanic_notes: Equal voltage across charge lamp extinguishes bulb while alternator self-excites through D7-D9.

caption: Fig. EE-26 Simplified charging circuit (3)
description: Simplified charging circuit schematic (3) when battery voltage exceeds specified setpoint: Zener diode ZD conducts, turning ON Tr3, which turns OFF Tr1 and stops rotor field current.
measurements_and_specs: Regulated voltage threshold triggers ZD conduction
mechanic_notes: Tr3 ON shorts base of Tr2/Tr1 to ground, cutting off field current until voltage drops below threshold.

caption: Fig. EE-27 Circuit diagram of charging system
description: Comprehensive wiring harness schematic of the Datsun 280Z charging system including alternator, IC voltage regulator, battery, fusible links, fuse block, ignition switch, ignition relay, and bulb check relay.
mechanic_notes: Bulb check relay connects charge lamp circuit during cranking for bulb verification.

caption: Fig. EE-28 Alternator
description: Exploded view diagram of the Hitachi LR160-42 alternator with built-in IC regulator showing all internal and external components in order of assembly.
mechanic_notes: Contains 9 total diodes: 3 positive, 3 negative, and 3 trio/sub-diodes mounted on heat sink plates.

caption: Fig. EE-29 Separating front cover
description: Illustration of alternator through bolts removed and separating front cover with rotor from rear cover with stator.
mechanic_notes: Tap front bracket lightly with wooden mallet to split housings.

caption: Fig. EE-30 Removing pulley and fan
description: Exploded illustration of pulley nut, spring washer, pulley, fan, and spacer being removed from the rotor shaft.
mechanic_notes: Hold rotor in vise with soft jaws to prevent scratching pole pieces when breaking nut loose.

caption: Fig. EE-31 Removing rotor
description: Illustration showing removal of rotor assembly from the front cover after removing bearing retainer setscrews.
mechanic_notes: Remove bearing retainer screws before pressing rotor out of front bearing.

caption: Fig. EE-32 [Pressing rear bearing onto rotor shaft]
description: Arbor press fixture used for installing or supporting the rear bearing on the alternator rotor shaft.
mechanic_notes: Apply force only to bearing inner race when pressing.

caption: Fig. EE-33 Pulling out rear bearing
description: Bearing puller tool attached to pull the rear bearing off the rotor slip ring shaft.
mechanic_notes: Take care not to gouge or damage copper slip rings with puller jaws.

caption: Fig. EE-34 [Disconnecting stator leads]
description: Technician using a soldering iron and needle-nose pliers to unsolder stator coil lead wires from the diode plate terminals.
mechanic_notes: Perform soldering/unsoldering as quickly as possible to avoid overheating silicon diodes.

caption: Fig. EE-35 [Removing brush assembly and diode holder]
description: Exploded view showing screws and mounting positions for brush assembly with IC regulator and diode holder in the rear cover.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect diode wires with soldering iron before loosening screws.

caption: Fig. EE-36 Continuity test of rotor coil
description: Multimeter / circuit tester probes applied across both slip rings of the rotor to test for continuity through the field coil.
measurements_and_specs: Continuity must exist across slip rings
mechanic_notes: If there is no continuity, field coil is open. Replace rotor assembly.

caption: Fig. EE-37 Testing rotor coil for ground
description: Circuit tester probes applied between slip ring and rotor iron pole core to check for short to ground.
mechanic_notes: If continuity exists, rotor coil or slip ring is grounded; replace rotor.

caption: Fig. EE-38 Testing stator for continuity
description: Ohmmeter probes testing continuity between the different phase leads of the disconnected stator winding.
measurements_and_specs: Continuity must exist between all phase leads
mechanic_notes: If no continuity between individual terminals, winding is broken; replace stator.

caption: Fig. EE-39 Testing stator for ground
description: Tester probe connected to stator lamination core while other probe contacts each winding lead wire to ensure no ground fault.
mechanic_notes: If any winding lead conducts to the laminated core, stator coil is grounded; replace stator.

caption: Fig. EE-40 [Auxiliary diodes]
description: Diagram showing the physical location of the trio auxiliary (sub) diodes mounted on the brush assembly plate.
mechanic_notes: Sub-diodes supply excitation field current to rotor once alternator is spinning.

caption: Fig. EE-41 Conductive direction of diode
description: Illustration of diode polarity markings: Black mark indicates current flows from terminal to case; Red mark indicates current flows from case to terminal.

callouts.Black: Direction of current: terminal to case
callouts.Red: Direction of current: case to terminal

mechanic_notes: Black marking = reverse polarity / positive plate; Red marking = forward polarity / negative plate.

caption: Fig. EE-42 [Checking positive diode]
description: Checking positive diodes on SR holder plate using ohmmeter probes between plate case and individual diode terminals.
measurements_and_specs: Conduction in forward bias only; no conduction in reverse bias
mechanic_notes: Conduction should occur only when tester negative probe is on terminal and positive on case.

caption: Fig. EE-43 Checking diode
description: Checking negative diodes pressed into the rear cover using ohmmeter probes between rear housing and diode terminals.
measurements_and_specs: Conduction when tester positive is on terminal and negative on case
mechanic_notes: Negative diodes conduct in the opposite probe configuration from positive diodes.

caption: Fig. EE-44 Checking diode
description: Testing the sub-diodes on the brush holder using ohmmeter test probes across the diode terminals.
mechanic_notes: Diodes must conduct in one direction only. If conducting both ways or neither way, replace.

caption: Fig. EE-45 Removing sub-diode
description: Using needle-nose pliers as a heat sink on diode lead while unsoldering the sub-diode terminal.
mechanic_notes: Pinch diode lead with pliers to prevent destructive heat transfer to the silicon wafer.

caption: Fig. EE-46 Brush wear limit
description: Illustration of the alternator carbon brush and brush holder showing the stamped brush wear limiting line.

callouts.Brush wear limiting line: Limit line scored on brush body

mechanic_notes: Replace brush assembly if brush is worn down to the limiting line.

caption: Fig. EE-47 Measuring spring pressure
description: Measuring brush spring pressure with a spring balance while the brush tip projects 2 mm (0.08 in) from the holder.
measurements_and_specs: New spring pressure: 255 to 345 gr (8.99 to 12.17 oz)
Rate of decrease: ~20 gr (0.71 oz) per 1 mm (0.04 in) wear
mechanic_notes: Measure pressure when brush is projected exactly 2 mm from holder face.

caption: Fig. EE-48 Tightening pulley nut
description: Tightening the alternator pulley nut with a torque wrench while securing the rotor shaft.
measurements_and_specs: Pulley V-groove deflection limit: less than 0.3 mm (0.012 in)
mechanic_notes: Check that V-groove runout/deflection is under 0.3 mm after torquing nut.

caption: Fig. EE-49 Inserting brush lift
description: Two-panel illustration showing how to push the brushes up and retain them using a brush lift wire inserted through the rear cover access hole, and then releasing it.
mechanic_notes: Insert wire from outside to hold brushes retracted during assembly. When withdrawing wire, push towards center to prevent damaging slip ring.

caption: Fig. EE-50 Testing alternator
description: Wiring test diagram for on-vehicle alternator performance test showing connection of voltmeter between BAT terminal and ground (E).
mechanic_notes: Turn headlights on high beam before running test. Do not exceed 1,100 rpm during initial test, and do not race engine.

caption: Fig. EE-51 IC voltage regulator
description: Front and rear view of the integrated circuit (IC) voltage regulator unit attached to the brush holder, showing terminal markings E, F, L, S, B and model stamping TRIZ-27 12V.
components: Terminals E, F, L, S, B
measurements_and_specs: Regulator stamp: TRIZ-27 12 V FAB026 684 BSLFE
mechanic_notes: Unit is permanently sealed; if defective, replace entire IC regulator and brush assembly.

caption: Fig. EE-52 Circuit of regulator
description: Internal electronic circuit schematic of the IC voltage regulator showing terminal connections B, S, L, F, E, transistors Tr1, Tr2, Tr3, zener diode ZD, thermistor Rh, and biasing resistors.
components: Resistors R1, R2, R3, R4, R5
Terminals B, S, L, F, E
mechanic_notes: Thermistor Rh compensates regulated voltage based on ambient temperature.

caption: Fig. EE-53 Testing regulator
description: Wiring test setup for IC regulator bench testing steps 2 through 5, showing two 12V batteries, 10-ohm resistor R1, variable resistor Rv, voltmeters V1, V2, V3, V4, and terminals E, F, L, S, B.
mechanic_notes: Stop test if resistors become excessively hot. Terminal S connected to center tap of Rv.

caption: Fig. EE-54 Testing regulator
description: Characteristic graph showing acceptable band of voltage V4 (V) on Procedure (5) (13.0 to 15.5V) versus regulator case temperature (-30°C to 110°C / -22°F to 230°F).
mechanic_notes: Regulated voltage decreases with increasing temperature due to internal thermistor compensation.

caption: Fig. EE-55 Testing regulator
description: Modified circuit schematic for step 6 test of the IC regulator with terminal S disconnected from Rv and connected to BAT1.
measurements_and_specs: V4 must be 0.5 to 2.0V higher than in step 5
mechanic_notes: Verifies regulator sense circuit switching behavior.

caption: Fig. EE-56 Ignition system circuit diagram
description: Functional circuit diagram of the contactless ignition system showing primary and secondary circuits, connections between the battery, ignition switch, starter, ignition coil, transistor ignition unit, distributor reluctor, pick-up coil, rotor head, and six spark plugs.
wiring_and_connections: Battery positive to ignition switch and starter
Ignition switch to ignition coil primary winding and transistor ignition unit
Pick-up coil signal wires to transistor ignition unit
Secondary winding high tension wire to distributor rotor head
Distributor cap terminals to spark plugs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
mechanic_notes: Pick-up coil detects reluctor tooth pass and triggers the transistor ignition unit to open coil primary current, collapsing magnetic flux to fire secondary spark.

caption: Fig. EE-57 Ignition system circuit diagram
description: Detailed electrical system wiring diagram showing full vehicle connections between fusible link, battery, engine earth, ignition switch, distributor, terminal block, condenser, ignition coil (+ and - terminals), and transistor ignition unit with wire colors.
wiring_and_connections: BW : Black with white stripe (Switched power)
WR : White with red stripe (Battery feed)
L : Blue (Ignition coil negative to transistor ignition unit)
mechanic_notes: Color codes: B = Black, BW = Black with white stripe, WR = White with red stripe, R = Red, G = Green, L = Blue. Condenser connects to BW lead at ignition coil (+).

caption: Fig. EE-58 Exploded view of distributor
description: Exploded view diagram of the complete contactless distributor assembly showing internal and external components numbered 1 through 18.
mechanic_notes: The contactor on the breaker plate is used to eliminate vacuum advance hysteresis. Reluctor is keyed to the shaft with a roll pin.

caption: Fig. EE-59 Checking air gap
description: Measurement illustration showing a flat feeler gauge inserted into the air gap between a reluctor tooth and the pick-up coil pole piece.
measurements_and_specs: Air gap: 0.2 to 0.4 mm (0.008 to 0.016 in)
mechanic_notes: Loosen pick-up coil screws to adjust gap to 0.2-0.4 mm (0.008-0.016 in).

caption: Fig. EE-60 Removing pick-up coil
description: Procedure illustration showing removal of screws securing the pick-up coil assembly and harness within the distributor housing.
wiring_and_connections: Distributor harness disconnected at terminal block
mechanic_notes: Disconnect distributor harness at terminal block prior to removing securing screws.

caption: Fig. EE-61 Removing vacuum controller
description: Removing the two retaining screws securing the vacuum controller assembly to the distributor body.
mechanic_notes: Detach vacuum controller after removing the two securing screws.

caption: Fig. EE-62 Removing breaker plate setscrews
description: Using a screwdriver to unscrew the setscrews retaining the breaker plate assembly inside the distributor.
mechanic_notes: Remove breaker plate setscrews to take out the breaker plate.

caption: Fig. EE-63 Removing knock pin
description: Driving the knock pin out of the distributor drive pinion gear using a hammer and small pin punch.
mechanic_notes: Punch knock pin out to detach the lower drive pinion.

caption: Fig. EE-64 Removing rotor shaft and drive shaft assembly
description: Withdrawing the rotor shaft and drive shaft sub-assembly upward out of the distributor housing.
mechanic_notes: Slide the combined rotor shaft and drive shaft out of housing once pinion is removed.

caption: Fig. EE-65 Removing rotor shaft
description: Unscrewing the internal rotor shaft setscrew from the top cavity of the rotor shaft with a screwdriver.
mechanic_notes: Mark rotor shaft and drive shaft first; remove packing from top of rotor shaft to access setscrew.

caption: Fig. EE-66 Cam-to-contactor clearance
description: Diagram illustrating clearance adjustment between the distributor shaft cam lobe and contactor arm on the breaker plate.
mechanic_notes: Adjust cam-to-contactor clearance to exactly 0.3 mm (0.012 in) after reinstalling contactor.

caption: Fig. EE-67 Driving in roll pin
description: Diagram showing correct rotational orientation of the reluctor roll pin with its longitudinal slit facing outward.
mechanic_notes: Always drive in roll pin with its slit toward the outer end of shaft. Always use a new roll pin.

caption: Fig. EE-68 Transistor ignition unit circuit diagram
description: Functional block diagram of the transistor ignition unit internal sub-circuits and wiring connections to the starter, ignition switch, battery, ignition coil, and distributor.
wiring_and_connections: Power switching circuit connected to ignition coil (-)
Lock preventing circuit and duty control circuit connected to power switching
Distributor pick-up leads to spark timing signal monitoring circuit
Ignition switch lead connected to starter and coil (+)
mechanic_notes: Unit contains power switching, duty control, spark timing monitoring, and lock preventing circuits.

caption: Fig. EE-69 External view of ignition unit
description: Perspective view of the transistor ignition unit casing and multi-wire plug connector showing the push-release latch.
mechanic_notes: Located on right-hand dash side panel in passenger compartment. Push latch of connector to remove.

caption: Fig. EE-70 Checking power supply wiring and battery
description: Connecting a DC voltmeter (50-volt range) between terminal BW (+) and terminal B (-) of the disconnected transistor ignition unit harness connector.
mechanic_notes: Turn on ignition switch before measuring. Full battery voltage must be present across BW and B.

caption: Fig. EE-71 Checking primary circuit
description: Connecting a DC voltmeter (50-volt range) between terminal L and terminal B on the disconnected transistor ignition unit connector.
mechanic_notes: Checks primary coil circuit continuity through the ignition switch and coil primary winding to connector terminal L.

caption: Fig. EE-72 Checking ignition coil assembly
description: Measuring resistance across the positive (+) and negative (-) primary terminals of the isolated ignition coil using an ohmmeter on x 1 range.
measurements_and_specs: Criterion: Approx. 0 ohm is OK; more than 1.8 ohm is N.G.
wiring_and_connections: Engine room harness disconnected from coil
mechanic_notes: Disconnect engine room harness before checking resistance across (+) and (-) terminals.

caption: Fig. EE-73 Checking pick-up coil
description: Connecting an ohmmeter (Resistance: x 10 range) between terminals G and R on the disconnected transistor ignition unit connector.
mechanic_notes: Pick-up coil resistance must be approximately 720 ohms. Far less or more indicates faulty coil.

caption: Fig. EE-74 Checking pick-up coil power signal pulse
description: Connecting a circuit tester on AC 2.5-volt range across terminals G and R while cranking the engine with starter motor.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect cold start valve harness before test. The needle should deflect slightly while cranking.

caption: Fig. EE-75 Checking pick-up coil power signal pulse
description: Connecting oscilloscope positive probe to terminal R and negative probe to terminal G of the ignition unit harness connector.
mechanic_notes: Set SLOPE switch to positive. Crank engine and observe generated waveform.

caption: Fig. EE-76 Wave form of pick-up coil
description: Oscilloscope waveform comparison of pick-up coil signal: continuous full line represents normal (OK), dashed line or absence represents abnormal (N.G.).
mechanic_notes: A full smooth sine-like waveform confirms normal pick-up coil signal generation.

caption: Fig. EE-77 Checking operation of transistor ignition unit
description: Connecting oscilloscope positive lead to ignition coil (-) terminal and negative lead to body metal ground.
wiring_and_connections: Oscilloscope positive probe to coil (-) terminal
Oscilloscope negative probe to body ground
mechanic_notes: Tests transistor unit primary switching by monitoring primary voltage waveform at coil negative terminal.

caption: Fig. EE-78 Wave form of pulse
description: Oscilloscope voltage waveform traces: pattern (a) displays a proper high-voltage induced primary spike (OK); pattern (b) displays a deformed/flat pulse (N.G.).
mechanic_notes: Pattern (a) confirms proper switching transistor operation. Pattern (b) indicates internal transistor unit defect.

caption: Fig. EE-79 Wave form of duty pulse
description: Oscilloscope trace illustrating duty cycle measurement at engine idle, showing conduction time t, total cycle period T, and formula t/T x 100 = 8 to 20%.
mechanic_notes: Measure at engine idle speed. Duty ratio must be within 8% to 20%.

caption: Fig. EE-80 Checking lock preventive circuit
description: Connecting a DC voltmeter (50-volt range) between the ignition coil (-) terminal and body metal ground to check the lock preventive circuit.
measurements_and_specs: Expected voltage: Power source (battery) voltage as soon as switch is turned ON
mechanic_notes: When ignition switch is turned on without cranking, tester should immediately read battery voltage, verifying primary current cut-off.

caption: Fig. EE-81 Wave form of lock preventive circuit
description: Oscilloscope voltage trace showing rapid rise from 0V up to power source (battery) voltage immediately upon turning ignition switch ON.
measurements_and_specs: Voltage level: 0V to Power source voltage
mechanic_notes: Waveform must sharply transition to full battery voltage upon switch closure, confirming lock prevention cut-off.

caption: Fig. EE-82 Wiring diagram for item (1) (Power supply wiring and battery check)
description: Schematic highlighting in bold the power feed and ground circuit for test Item 1: from battery positive through fusible link and ignition switch to connector terminal BW, and from connector terminal B to earth ground.
wiring_and_connections: BW: Black with white stripe (Switched battery feed)
mechanic_notes: Bold traces illustrate the exact supply and ground paths tested during Item 1 power supply verification.

caption: Fig. EE-83 Wiring diagram for item (2)-1 (Checking primary circuit)
description: Schematic highlighting in bold the primary ignition circuit path for test Item 2-1: battery positive, fusible link, ignition switch, ignition coil (+) and (-) terminals, through lead L to the disconnected ignition unit connector.
wiring_and_connections: L: Blue (Coil - to connector pin L)
mechanic_notes: Bold lines show the complete circuit path tested when verifying primary coil voltage at connector pins L and B.
