caption: Fig. EM-46 Service valve seat dimensions
description: Sectional profile and service insert dimensions for L28 intake and exhaust valve seats.
measurements_and_specs: Intake outer dia: 45.597 to 45.613 mm (1.7952 to 1.7958 in)
Exhaust outer dia: 37.580 to 37.596 mm (1.4795 to 1.4802 in)
mechanic_notes: Ensure counterbore depth stop is set accurately to prevent cutting into aluminum head base.

caption: Fig. EM-47 Standard valve seat dimensions
description: Standard valve seat cut angles and contact widths for L28 intake and exhaust valves.
measurements_and_specs: Intake seat diameters: 39 mm, 41.6 mm, 43.8 mm, 45 mm
mechanic_notes: Use 3-angle cut to position contact width centered on valve face.

caption: Fig. EM-48 Checking camshaft bearing
description: Checking camshaft bearing tower internal bore with a cylinder bore/dial indicator gauge.
measurements_and_specs: Bearing ID standard: 48.000 to 48.016 mm (1.8898 to 1.8904 in)
mechanic_notes: If bearing tower is worn beyond limit, replace cylinder head assembly (towers are integral).

caption: Fig. EM-49 Valve timing diagram
description: Polar circular timing diagram depicting intake open/close and exhaust open/close events relative to TDC and BDC.
measurements_and_specs: See timing angle specifications table on EM-12
mechanic_notes: Rotation is clockwise; applies to all six cylinders.

caption: Fig. EM-50 Checking camshaft bend
description: Camshaft supported in V-blocks at front and rear journals while measuring runout on center journal with dial indicator.
mechanic_notes: Bend value is 1/2 of Total Indicator Reading (TIR) over one 360-degree rotation.

caption: Fig. EM-51 Checking cylinder block surface
description: Checking cylinder block deck flatness using precision straightedge and feeler gauge.
mechanic_notes: Combined head and block deck resurfacing must not exceed 0.20 mm (0.0079 in).

caption: Fig. EM-52 Measuring cylinder bore diameter
description: Measuring cylinder bore internal diameter using a precision dial bore indicator gauge.
measurements_and_specs: Standard bore: 86.000 to 86.050 mm (3.3858 to 3.3878 in)
mechanic_notes: Check bore diameter at 3 depth levels in both thrust and axial directions.

caption: Fig. EM-53 Cylinder bore measuring positions
description: Diagram of cylinder bore measuring depths (20 mm, 60 mm, 100 mm from top deck) and axes (X thrust vs Y axial).

callouts.A: 20 mm (0.79 in) from top deck

measurements_and_specs: Depths: 20 mm, 60 mm, 100 mm (0.79 in, 2.36 in, 3.94 in)
mechanic_notes: Out-of-round = X - Y; Taper = A - B.

caption: Fig. EM-54 Measuring piston diameter
description: Measuring piston outside skirt diameter with an outside micrometer.
mechanic_notes: Measure at specified skirt height to determine true size A.

caption: Fig. EM-55 Measuring piston skirt diameter
description: Location schematic showing the 21 mm height position on the piston skirt for measuring diameter.

callouts.about 21 mm (0.83 in): Measurement point 21 mm from bottom of skirt

measurements_and_specs: about 21 mm (0.83 in) above bottom edge
mechanic_notes: Always measure skirt diameter at exactly 21 mm from the bottom edge in thrust direction.

caption: Fig. EM-56 Measuring piston fit in cylinder
description: Checking piston-to-bore clearance using 0.04 mm feeler gauge strip attached to spring balance scale.
measurements_and_specs: Extracting pull force: 0.2 to 1.5 kg (0.4 to 3.3 lb)
mechanic_notes: Slowly pull feeler gauge straight upward; test at 20°C (68°F).

caption: Fig. EM-57 Measuring piston ring side clearance
description: Measuring side clearance between piston ring and ring land using a feeler gauge.
mechanic_notes: Measure around entire circumference of groove.

caption: Fig. EM-58 Measuring ring gap
description: Checking piston ring end gap in cylinder bore using feeler gauge after squaring ring with inverted piston.
mechanic_notes: Square ring inside bore using piston crown before taking measurement.

caption: Fig. EM-59 Piston pin fitting
description: Manual thumb-push check of piston pin fit in piston bosses at room temperature.
measurements_and_specs: Pin to piston clearance: 0.006 to 0.013 mm (0.0002 to 0.00051 in)
mechanic_notes: Pin should be a snug finger-push fit at room temperature (20°C / 68°F).

caption: Fig. EM-60 Measuring piston pin diameter
description: Measuring piston pin outside diameter using micrometer.
measurements_and_specs: OD standard: 20.993 to 20.998 mm (0.8265 to 0.8267 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure at center and both ends.

caption: Fig. EM-61 Checking rod alignment
description: Checking connecting rod bend and twist on an alignment arbor fixture with feeler feelers.
measurements_and_specs: Bend/torsion limit: 0.05 mm per 100 mm (0.0020 in per 3.94 in)
mechanic_notes: Check both bend and twist on dedicated aligner fixture.

caption: Fig. EM-62 Checking big end play
description: Measuring connecting rod big end side thrust clearance on crank journal using feeler gauge.
measurements_and_specs: Big end play standard: 0.2 to 0.3 mm (0.008 to 0.012 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure between connecting rod thrust cheek and crank journal shoulder.

caption: Fig. EM-63 Crankshaft and journal dimensions
description: Crankshaft schematic showing main journal and rod pin diameters, journal widths, and measuring axes.
measurements_and_specs: Main journal dia: 54.942 to 54.955 mm (2.1631 to 2.1636 in)
Crank pin dia: 49.961 to 49.974 mm (1.9670 to 1.9683 in)
Main journal widths: 30.5 mm, 19.5 mm, 27 mm, 19.5 mm
mechanic_notes: Out-of-round: X-Y; Taper: A-B. Standard limit < 0.01 mm.

caption: Fig. EM-64 Checking crankshaft bend
description: Checking crankshaft runout on V-blocks with a dial indicator resting on center main journal.
mechanic_notes: Bend is half total dial reading over 360 degree revolution.

caption: Fig. EM-65 Checking crankshaft end play
description: Measuring crankshaft axial thrust end play using feeler gauge at center thrust main bearing.
measurements_and_specs: End play standard: 0.05 to 0.18 mm (0.0020 to 0.0071 in)
mechanic_notes: Pry crankshaft back and forth and check clearance with feeler gauge at thrust bearing flange.

caption: Fig. EM-66 Pulling out pilot bushing
description: Removing transmission pilot bushing from crankshaft tail with puller ST16610001.
mechanic_notes: Insert collet fingers behind bushing inside crankshaft rear bore.

caption: Fig. EM-67 Press-fitting new pilot bushing
description: Pressing new pilot bushing into crankshaft flange to specified protrusion depth.
measurements_and_specs: Protrusion height above flange: 6.5 to 7.0 mm (0.256 to 0.276 in)
mechanic_notes: Do not oil pilot bushing; it is oil-impregnated bronze.

caption: Fig. EM-68 Plastigage
description: Plastigage wax strip and measurement scale envelope.
mechanic_notes: Do not rotate crankshaft while plastigage strip is in place.

caption: Fig. EM-69 Measuring bearing clearance
description: Comparing compressed plastigage width against scale envelope to read oil clearance.
measurements_and_specs: Torque cap to 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Measure at widest part of squashed wax strip.

caption: Fig. EM-70 Checking bearing crush
description: Schematic of bearing shell crush height 'H' protruding above parting face when seated under test weight.
measurements_and_specs: Main bearing crush: 0 to 0.03 mm (0 to 0.0012 in)
Connecting rod crush: 0.015 to 0.045 mm (0.0006 to 0.0018 in)
mechanic_notes: Lock one side flush and measure protrusion H at opposite parting face with feeler gauge.

caption: Fig. EM-71 Checking camshaft sprocket runout
description: Dial indicator setup measuring runout of camshaft sprocket mounted on camshaft supported on V-blocks.
measurements_and_specs: Runout limit: 0.1 mm (0.004 in) total indicator reading
mechanic_notes: If runout exceeds 0.1 mm (0.004 in), replace camshaft sprocket.

caption: Fig. EM-72 Checking camshaft end play
description: Measuring camshaft end play with a feeler gauge inserted between locating plate and camshaft journal front shoulder.
measurements_and_specs: Camshaft end play: 0.08 to 0.38 mm (0.0031 to 0.0150 in)
mechanic_notes: Check end play clearance using feeler gauge between locating plate and camshaft.

caption: Fig. EM-73 Camshaft locate plate
description: Camshaft locate plate showing oblong groove angular range (4° 15') and lower locator notch angle (10°).
mechanic_notes: If camshaft sprocket location notch comes off the left end of the oblong groove at TDC compression No. 1, chain stretch is beyond limits.

caption: Fig. EM-74 Adjusting camshaft sprocket location
description: Comparison diagram showing camshaft sprocket location holes 1 to 3 and timing marks (1) to (3) before and after adjustment.
mechanic_notes: When No. 2 hole is used, No. 2 timing mark must also be used. If chain stretch exceeds No. 3 hole capability, replace chain assembly.

caption: Fig. EM-75 Camshaft drive mechanism
description: Exploded view of the timing chain drive system showing sprockets, chain, guides, and tensioner.
mechanic_notes: Inspect tensioner shoe and chain guides for wear or grooves.

caption: Fig. EM-76 Checking flywheel deviation
description: Measuring flywheel clutch friction face runout using a dial indicator mounted on engine block.
measurements_and_specs: Runout limit: 0.15 mm (0.0059 in) total indicator reading
Ring gear heating temp: 180 to 220°C (356 to 428°F)
mechanic_notes: Replace flywheel if surface runout exceeds 0.15 mm (0.0059 in).

caption: Fig. EM-77 Oil seal of crankshaft
description: Cross-sectional orientation diagram for front cover and rear crankshaft oil seals showing front direction.
mechanic_notes: Pay attention to mounting direction. Install new seals during engine overhaul.

caption: Fig. EM-78 Applying sealant (Front cover and gasket)
description: Front of cylinder block showing sealant application points at front cover gasket corners.
mechanic_notes: Apply sealant at corners of front cover and cylinder block.

caption: Fig. EM-79 Applying sealant (Main bearing cap and cylinder block)
description: Rear main bearing cap showing sealant bead of 20 to 25 mm applied to each side where it mates with cylinder block.
measurements_and_specs: Sealant bead length: 20 to 25 mm (0.79 to 0.98 in)
mechanic_notes: Apply sealant along sides of rear main bearing cap across 20 to 25 mm (0.79 to 0.98 in).

caption: Fig. EM-80 Applying sealant (Cylinder block)
description: Oil pan mounting face of cylinder block highlighting four step portions where sealant must be applied.
mechanic_notes: Apply sealant to step portions at four mating surfaces (block to rear main bearing cap and front cover).

caption: Fig. EM-81 Installing valve
description: Compressing valve springs on cylinder head using Valve Lifter ST12070000 to insert valve collets.
mechanic_notes: Assemble valve, inner and outer springs, retainer, collets, and rocker guide.

caption: Fig. EM-82 Installing valve spring
description: Uneven pitch valve spring showing red painted narrow-pitch side installed toward cylinder head.
mechanic_notes: Install outer valve spring facing red painted side (narrow pitch) to cylinder head surface.

caption: Fig. EM-83 Installing camshaft locating plate
description: Installing camshaft and locating plate into front of cylinder head.
mechanic_notes: Oblong groove of locating plate must be directed toward front side of engine. Do not damage bearings.

caption: Fig. EM-84 Installing camshaft sprocket
description: Tightening camshaft sprocket retaining bolt on front of cylinder head.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 13 to 15 kg-m (94 to 108 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten sprocket bolt to 13 to 15 kg-m. Check camshaft end play.

caption: Fig. EM-85 Installing rocker arm
description: Depressing valve spring with a screwdriver to install rocker arm beneath camshaft lobe.
mechanic_notes: Press valve spring down using a screwdriver to seat rocker arm on pivot.

caption: Fig. EM-86 Assembling cylinder head
description: Assembled cylinder head showing valve train and camshaft rotated so No. 1 is at TDC compression.
mechanic_notes: Turn camshaft until No. 1 piston is at TDC on its compression stroke.

caption: Fig. EM-87 Installing piston pin
description: Pressing piston pin into connecting rod and piston using Pin Press Stand ST13030001.
mechanic_notes: Apply engine oil to pin and small end of rod. Pressing force must be 0.5 to 1.5 tons.

caption: Fig. EM-88 Assembling piston and connecting rod
description: Assembly orientation of piston and connecting rod showing front mark notch and connecting rod oil hole.
mechanic_notes: Oil jet hole must be directed toward right side of cylinder block; notch on piston head toward front of engine.

caption: Fig. EM-89 Installing piston ring
description: Installing top, second, and oil rings onto piston ring lands using ring expander.
mechanic_notes: Install rings with marked side up. Top ring is chrome-plated; second ring has larger taper.

caption: Fig. EM-90 Main bearings
description: Arrangement of #1 through #7 main bearings and bearing caps from front to rear.
measurements_and_specs: Only center bearing (No. 4) is flanged type
mechanic_notes: All inter-bearings (#2, 3, 5, 6) are same type. Front (#1) and rear (#7) are same type. Upper and lower bearings are interchangeable.

caption: Fig. EM-91 Torque sequence of cap bolts
description: Tightening sequence (1 to 14) for the 7 main bearing caps, starting from center bearing #4 and alternating outwards.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten in 2 to 3 stages outwardly from center bearing in sequence 1 to 14. Arrow marks point forward.

caption: Fig. EM-92 Checking crankshaft end play
description: Checking crankshaft axial end play with a dial indicator positioned at crankshaft nose.
measurements_and_specs: Crankshaft end play: 0.05 to 0.18 mm (0.0020 to 0.0071 in)
mechanic_notes: Check that crankshaft end play is 0.05 to 0.18 mm and turns smoothly.

caption: Fig. EM-93 Driving side oil seal
description: Driving side oil seals into side slots of rear main bearing cap.
mechanic_notes: Apply sealant to side oil seals prior to driving them into rear main bearing cap.

caption: Fig. EM-94 Installing rear oil seal
description: Driving rear oil seal into block using Rear Oil Seal Drift ST15310000.
mechanic_notes: Apply lithium grease to sealing lip; coat shaft and periphery with engine oil.

caption: Fig. EM-95 Installing flywheel
description: Tightening flywheel fixing bolts on rear crankshaft flange.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 13 to 15 kg-m (94 to 108 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten flywheel bolts securely to 13 to 15 kg-m.

caption: Fig. EM-96 Installing piston-rod assembly
description: Installing piston and connecting rod into cylinder using Piston Ring Compressor EM03470000.
mechanic_notes: Apply oil to sliding parts; align front notch on piston head toward front of engine.

caption: Fig. EM-97 Piston ring direction
description: Orientation of top ring, second ring, and oil ring gaps positioned 180° apart, avoiding thrust and pin directions.
mechanic_notes: Stagger ring gaps at 180° to each other, avoiding thrust and pin directions.

caption: Fig. EM-98 Installing connecting rod cap
description: Torquing connecting rod cap nuts onto connecting rod big end.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Arrange connecting rods and caps so cylinder numbers face in same direction. Torque to 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m.

caption: Fig. EM-99 Checking big end play
description: Measuring connecting rod big end side play with feeler gauge between connecting rod thrust shoulder and crankpin web.
measurements_and_specs: Big end play: 0.2 to 0.3 mm (0.008 to 0.012 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure big end side play with feeler gauge. Standard is 0.2 to 0.3 mm.

caption: Fig. EM-100 Cylinder head bolts
description: Top view of cylinder head identifying positions of long bolts (A) and short bolts (B).

callouts.A: Head bolt type A (long)

mechanic_notes: Ensure type A and type B head bolts are installed in their correct designated positions.

caption: Fig. EM-101 Installing timing chain
description: Timing chain routing diagram showing sprocket mating marks and 42 chain links between timing marks.
mechanic_notes: Align mating marks on timing chain with crankshaft sprocket and camshaft sprocket on the right-hand side. 42 links between marks.

caption: Fig. EM-102 Installing chain tensioner
description: Installing chain tensioner assembly into cylinder block with spindle protrusion adjusted to 0 mm.
mechanic_notes: Adjust protrusion of chain tensioner spindle to 0 mm before installing.

caption: Fig. EM-103 Installing front cover
description: Front cover mounted on cylinder block showing timing indicator scale.
measurements_and_specs: Height difference limit: less than 0.15 mm (0.0059 in)
mechanic_notes: Check height difference between cylinder block upper face and front cover upper face (must be less than 0.15 mm). Apply sealant as shown in Fig. EM-78.

caption: Fig. EM-104 Front cover bolts
description: Front cover bolt positions showing different lengths and sizes.
measurements_and_specs: M8 torque: 1.0 to 1.6 kg-m (7 to 12 ft-lb)
M6 torque: 0.4 to 0.8 kg-m (2.9 to 5.8 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Note that different types of bolts are used. Torque M8 to 1.0-1.6 kg-m, M6 to 0.4-0.8 kg-m.

caption: Fig. EM-105 Installing crankshaft pulley
description: Installing crankshaft pulley and water pump on front cover and tightening pulley nut.
measurements_and_specs: Crankshaft pulley nut torque: 12 to 16 kg-m (87 to 116 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Set No. 1 piston at TDC on compression stroke when installing crankshaft pulley and water pump.

caption: Fig. EM-106 Tightening sequence
description: Cylinder head bolt tightening sequence diagram showing numbers 1 to 14, using special wrench ST10120000.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 7.0 to 8.5 kg-m (51 to 61 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten head bolts in sequence from center outward. Remember to tighten two small bolts.

caption: Fig. EM-107 Setting distributor driving spindle
description: Aligning punch mark on distributor driving spindle with oil hole on oil pump shaft.
mechanic_notes: Assemble oil pump and drive spindle, aligning driving spindle punch mark face with oil pump hole.

caption: Fig. EM-108 Installing oil pump
description: Inserting oil pump and spindle assembly into bottom of front cover.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.1 to 1.5 kg-m (8 to 11 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Do not forget gasket. Tighten bolts to 1.1 to 1.5 kg-m.

caption: Fig. EM 109 Setting distributor drive spindle
description: Top view of distributor spindle drive slot oriented at 11:25 a.m. position with smaller bow-shape facing front.
mechanic_notes: Projection on top must be located at 11:25 a.m. position with smaller bow-shape facing toward front.

caption: Fig. EM-110 Adjusting valve clearance
description: Adjusting valve clearance at rocker pivot using special Pivot Adjuster ST10640001 and feeler gauge.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 5.0 to 6.0 kg-m (36 to 43 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: First adjust cold, then re-check hot after warming up engine. Torque lock nut to 5.0-6.0 kg-m.

caption: Fig. EM-111 Location of intake manifold securing bolts
description: Locations of long bolts (40 mm / 1.57 in) and short bolts (32 mm / 1.26 in) on intake manifold.
mechanic_notes: There are two types of 10M bolts. When installing, do not confuse them.

caption: Fig. EM-112 Installing clutch assembly
description: Aligning clutch disc using Clutch Aligning Bar KV30100100 while securing clutch cover to flywheel.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.2 to 2.2 kg-m (9 to 16 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Use Clutch Aligning Bar KV30100100 to center disc. Torque clutch cover bolts to 1.2 to 2.2 kg-m.

caption: Fig. EM-113 Installing compressor
description: Exploded view of air conditioning compressor, mounting bracket, idler pulley, and fasteners.

callouts.*: Tightening torque: 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Compressor mounting bolts (*): 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten bolts marked with asterisk to 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m.

caption: Fig. EM-114 Air conditioning compressor belt tension
description: Checking A/C compressor belt tension with thumb pressure applied midway between idler pulley and compressor pulley.
mechanic_notes: Adjust idler pulley bolt so belt deflection is 8 to 12 mm under 10 kg thumb pressure.

caption: Fig. EM-115 Fan belt tension
description: Checking fan/alternator drive belt deflection with thumb pressure applied midway between pulleys.
mechanic_notes: Deflection should be held within 8 to 12 mm under 10 kg thumb pressure applied midway between pulleys.

caption: Cam lobe height dimension "A"
description: Camshaft profile showing total lobe height dimension "A" from base circle to cam peak.

callouts.A: Standard height of cam

measurements_and_specs: Standard height of cam "A": 40.30 to 40.35 mm (1.5866 to 1.5886 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure total cam lobe height across dimension A. Standard specification is 40.30 to 40.35 mm.

caption: ST19320000 Oil filter wrench
description: Band type oil filter wrench tool.
mechanic_notes: Used to remove spin-on oil filter.

caption: ST05340001 Engine attachment
description: Engine mounting adapter plate with mounting bolts for attaching block to overhaul stand.
mechanic_notes: Bolts to right-hand side of cylinder block to mount engine onto engine stand.

caption: ST0501S000 Engine stand assembly
description: Mobile engine stand assembly with rolling caster base and rotating mount head.
mechanic_notes: Used to support engine during overhaul.

caption: ST16540000 Puller crank pulley
description: Two-bolt mechanical puller crossbar for removing crankshaft pulley / damper.
mechanic_notes: Used to pull crankshaft pulley from crankshaft nose.

caption: ST17420001 Chain stopper
description: Wedge-shaped chain stopper block to retain timing chain when cylinder head is removed.
mechanic_notes: Holds timing chain in position to prevent tensioner spindle from extending.

caption: ST10120000 Cylinder head bolt wrench
description: Deep reach socket adapter wrench for tightening cylinder head bolts.
components: Cylinder head bolt wrench socket tool
mechanic_notes: Special deep socket extension for reaching cylinder head bolts between rocker gear.

caption: KV101041S0 Crankshaft main bearing cap puller
description: Bridge-type puller with threaded adapters for extracting main bearing caps from cylinder block.
mechanic_notes: Pulls main bearing caps evenly without distorting block dowels.

caption: ST13030001 Piston pin press stand
description: Support fixture and pilot drift for pressing piston pins into connecting rods under hydraulic press.
mechanic_notes: Used with press (0.5 to 1.5 tons) for installing piston pins.

caption: ST12070000 Valve lifter
description: C-frame valve spring compressor tool for removing and installing valve springs and collets.
mechanic_notes: Compresses inner and outer valve springs to install or remove collets.

caption: KV101039S0 Valve guide reamer set
description: Valve guide reamers and drift set including 12.2 mm reamer, 8.0 mm reamer, and replacement drift.
mechanic_notes: Used for reaming valve guide holes in cylinder head and finishing valve guide bore.

caption: ST11650001 Cutter set valve seat
description: Case containing valve seat cutter set for refacing intake and exhaust valve seats.
mechanic_notes: Used for refacing valve seats to 45 degree angle.

caption: ST16610001 Pilot bushing puller
description: Internal expanding collet puller for removing pilot bushing from rear of crankshaft.
mechanic_notes: Used to pull pilot bushing out of crankshaft flange.

caption: ST15310000 Crankshaft rear oil seal drift
description: Knurled circular drift tool for installing crankshaft rear main oil seal.
mechanic_notes: Drives rear crankshaft oil seal squarely into position.

caption: EM03470000 Piston ring compressor
description: Adjustable spring band piston ring compressor with friction brake lock.
mechanic_notes: Compresses piston rings flush with skirt during installation into cylinder bore.

caption: ST10640001 Pivot adjuster
description: Curved offset open wrench for adjusting valve rocker pivots and tightening lock nuts.
mechanic_notes: Specially shaped to clear valve train components when setting valve lash.

caption: KV30100100 Clutch aligning bar
description: Stepped clutch alignment arbor matching transmission input shaft splines and pilot bushing bore.
mechanic_notes: Centers clutch friction disc relative to flywheel pilot bushing during pressure plate torquing.

caption: Fig. ER-1 Releasing pressure in fuel system
description: Depressurization of the electronic fuel injection system using two jumper wires connected from the battery terminals to the cold start valve connector for 2-3 seconds.
wiring_and_connections: Jumper wire between battery (+) terminal and cold start valve connector terminal
Jumper wire between battery (-) terminal and cold start valve connector terminal
mechanic_notes: Be careful to keep both terminals separate in order to avoid short circuit.

caption: Fig. ER-2 Removing hood
description: Two mechanics supporting and removing the engine hood from the body hinge mounts.
mechanic_notes: Mark hood hinge locations on hood prior to bolt removal to facilitate proper reinstallation; have an assistant help lift the hood.

caption: Fig. ER-3 Removing air flow meter
description: Removal of the air flow meter and loosening clamps from the air duct boot.
wiring_and_connections: Air flow meter wire harness connector
mechanic_notes: Loosen clamps securing duct to air flow meter and body before removal.

caption: Fig. ER-4 Removing canister and disconnecting fuel hoses
description: Removal of the carbon canister and disconnecting fuel return hose and fuel charge hose.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect canister vapor lines and fuel supply/return lines before lifting engine.

caption: Fig. ER-5 Disconnecting accelerator linkage
description: Disconnecting the mechanical accelerator linkage rod and electrical harness plug for the fuel injectors.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect mechanical throttle rod linkage and injector sub-harness connector.

caption: Fig. ER-6 Disconnecting wire for throttle valve switch and B.C.D.D. solenoid valve
description: Disconnecting wire connectors for throttle valve switch, B.C.D.D. solenoid valve, and distributor condenser.
mechanic_notes: Unplug the three connectors near the throttle chamber and distributor.

caption: Fig. ER-7 Disconnecting wire for block terminal
description: Disconnecting high tension spark wire between coil and distributor and the distributor harness block terminal.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect high-tension lead at distributor cap and disconnect harness block terminal connector.

caption: Fig. ER-8 Disconnecting wire for cold start valve and air regulator
description: Disconnecting electrical connectors for cold start valve and auxiliary air regulator.
wiring_and_connections: Cold start valve electrical harness connector
mechanic_notes: Release wire retaining clips on electrical plugs before pulling connectors.

caption: Fig. ER-9 Disconnecting wire for thermostat housing
description: Disconnecting electrical sensors and switches located on the front thermostat housing.
mechanic_notes: Note wire harness connector positions: thermal transmitter (1), thermotime switch (2), water temperature sensor (3).

caption: Fig. ER-10 Disconnecting heater inlet and outlet hoses
description: Disconnecting heater core coolant inlet and outlet hoses from engine fittings.
mechanic_notes: Loosen hose clamps and slide heater hoses off metal pipe nipples.

caption: Fig. ER-11 Disconnecting wire for oil pressure sending unit
description: Disconnecting terminal lead wire from the oil pressure sending unit on the engine block.
wiring_and_connections: Oil pressure sending unit electrical terminal wire
mechanic_notes: Pull off terminal wire connection from gauge sending unit under the distributor.

caption: Fig. ER-12 Removing clutch operating cylinder
description: Removal of clutch operating cylinder from clutch housing, speedometer cable disconnection, and back-up lamp switch wiring disconnection.

callouts.1: Clutch operating cylinder (Tightening torque: 2.5 to 3.0 kg-m / 18 to 22 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Clutch operating cylinder tightening torque: 2.5 to 3.0 kg-m (18 to 22 ft-lb)
wiring_and_connections: Back-up lamp switch electrical wire connector
mechanic_notes: Unbolt clutch operating slave cylinder without disconnecting hydraulic line to avoid bleeding; disconnect speedometer cable and back-up lamp switch harness.

caption: Fig. ER-13 Disconnecting exhaust front tube
description: Unbolting exhaust front pipe flange nuts from the exhaust manifold with a wrench.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4.6 to 6.1 kg-m (33 to 44 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tightening torque: 4.6 to 6.1 kg-m (33 to 44 ft-lb). Allow exhaust to cool completely before removal.

caption: Fig. ER-14 Removing front tube bracket
description: Removing the bracket securing the exhaust front tube to the transmission rear extension housing.
mechanic_notes: Hold front tube end up with a thread or wire to prevent tube from falling after bracket removal.

caption: Fig. ER-15 Removing insulator
description: Unbolting floor tunnel heat insulator shield and resting it onto the exhaust tube.
mechanic_notes: Remove insulator securing bolts and let heat shield rest on exhaust pipe to clear transmission crossmember.

caption: Fig. ER-16 Removing propeller shaft
description: Unbolting the four propeller shaft companion flange bolts at the differential carrier.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 3.5 to 4.5 kg-m (25 to 33 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Put match marks on both shaft and companion flange so shaft can be reinstalled in original balance position. Plug rear extension housing to prevent oil leakage. Tightening torque: 3.5 to 4.5 kg-m (25 to 33 ft-lb).

caption: Fig. ER-17 Removing rear engine mounting member
description: Unbolting the rear engine mounting crossmember bolts from the vehicle body frame rails.

callouts.A: Rear engine mounting member to body bolts

measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque Ⓐ: 3.2 to 4.3 kg-m (23 to 31 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Support transmission with jack before loosening crossmember bolts. Tightening torque Ⓐ: 3.2 to 4.3 kg-m (23 to 31 ft-lb).

caption: Fig. ER-18 Removing engine
description: Engine and transmission assembly hoisted out of the engine compartment as a single unit using an overhead crane and sling chains.
mechanic_notes: Raise engine and transmission together at an angle to clear front body and radiator core support. Be careful not to knock against adjacent body parts.

caption: Fig. ER-19 Sectional view of front engine mounting, and front insulator
description: Sectional view of front engine mounting brackets and suspension member, showing torque specifications and top/bottom orientation of rubber insulators.

callouts.A: Front engine mounting bracket to engine bolt (T: 3.1 to 4.1 kg-m / 22 to 30 ft-lb)
callouts.B: Front insulator to engine mounting bracket nut (T: 1.6 to 2.1 kg-m / 12 to 15 ft-lb)
callouts.C: Front insulator to suspension member nut (T: 3.2 to 4.3 kg-m / 23 to 31 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque Ⓐ (bracket to engine): 3.1 to 4.1 kg-m (22 to 30 ft-lb)
Tightening torque Ⓑ (insulator to bracket): 1.6 to 2.1 kg-m (12 to 15 ft-lb)
Tightening torque Ⓒ (insulator to suspension member): 3.2 to 4.3 kg-m (23 to 31 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Left and right front insulators are interchangeable, but pay careful attention to their upper and lower orientation. Right side bracket shape differs from left side bracket.

caption: Fig. ER-20 Rear engine mounting and rear insulator
description: Exploded view of the transmission rear extension mount, rubber insulator, crossmember member, bushings, and attachment hardware.

callouts.A: Tightening torque of bolts or nuts: 3.2 to 4.3 kg-m (23 to 31 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque Ⓐ of bolts or nuts: 3.2 to 4.3 kg-m (23 to 31 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Note forward orientation arrow for rear engine mounting member and insulator. Tighten bolts and nuts to 3.2 to 4.3 kg-m (23 to 31 ft-lb).

caption: Fig. ET-2 Adjusting valve clearance
description: Illustration showing valve clearance adjustment using Pivot Adjuster ST10640001 and feeler gauge on an OHC L-series cylinder head, with valve positions numbered 1 through 12 from front to rear.
measurements_and_specs: Pivot lock nut torque: 5.0 to 6.0 kg-m (36 to 43 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Engine oil temperature must be above 80°C (176°F). Never adjust with engine running. Rotate crankshaft four complete turns to complete all four adjustment steps.

caption: Fig. ET-3 Fan belt tension
description: Illustration demonstrating fan belt tension measurement using thumb pressure midway between alternator pulley and fan pulley.
mechanic_notes: Check for cracks or damage prior to tension measurement.

caption: Fig. ET-4 Cooler compressor belt tension
description: Illustration of cooler (air conditioning) compressor belt tension check and idler pulley adjustment bolt.
mechanic_notes: Adjust tension by turning idler pulley bolt in or out.

caption: Fig. ET-5 Testing radiator cap
description: Testing radiator pressure cap relief valve pressure using a hand pump cap tester and adapter.
mechanic_notes: Replace cap assembly if pressure is not maintained within specification.

caption: Fig. ET-6 Cooling system pressure test
description: Testing engine cooling system for leaks by applying pressure with radiator tester attached to filler neck.
mechanic_notes: Radiator cap must be removed. Inspect all hoses and joints while pressurized.

caption: Fig. ET-7 Testing compression pressure
description: Connecting compression tester gauge to spark plug port to measure cranking cylinder compression.
measurements_and_specs: Minimum: 11.5 kg/cm² (164 psi) at 300 to 400 rpm
mechanic_notes: Disconnect cold start valve and all fuel injector connectors before cranking engine.

caption: Fig. ET-8 Checking electrolyte level
description: Visual guide for checking battery cell electrolyte levels showing Overflow, Correct, and Shortage conditions.

callouts.Shortage: Electrolyte level too low (needs distilled water)

mechanic_notes: Pour distilled water if shortage is indicated.

caption: Fig. ET-9 Checking specific gravity of battery electrolyte
description: Measuring battery electrolyte specific gravity with a glass hydrometer inserted into battery cell vent.
measurements_and_specs: Other climates: 1.26 full charge (permissible over 1.20) at 20°C (68°F)
mechanic_notes: Hold hydrometer vertical at eye level to read specific gravity scale.

caption: Fig. ET-10 Adjusting ignition timing
description: Adjusting ignition timing by loosening distributor set screw and rotating distributor housing while checking timing mark with timing light.
mechanic_notes: Loosen set screw just enough to turn distributor by hand, align timing mark, then retighten securely.

caption: Fig. ET-11 Ignition timing indicator
description: Diagram of crankshaft pulley notch aligned with timing indicator pointer at 10 degrees BTDC.
mechanic_notes: Ensure dirt and dust are cleaned off pulley and indicator prior to reading with timing light.

caption: Fig. ET-12 Checking spark plug gap
description: Checking spark plug electrode gap using a round wire feeler gauge.
measurements_and_specs: Standard gap: 1.0 to 1.1 mm (0.039 to 0.043 in)
Canada gap: 0.7 to 0.8 mm (0.028 to 0.031 in)
Tightening torque: 1.5 to 2.0 kg-m (11 to 14 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Adjust gap by bending ground electrode only; do not bend center electrode.

caption: Fig. ET-13 Checking high tension cable
description: Testing high tension ignition cable resistance using an ohmmeter connected between plug boot terminal and distributor cap internal terminal.
wiring_and_connections: Ohmmeter connected between spark plug terminal and distributor cap electrode
mechanic_notes: Do not remove cables from cap initially. If resistance exceeds 30,000 ohms, test cable alone before replacing.

caption: Fig. ET-14 Adjusting idling speed
description: Adjusting idle speed using screwdriver on idle speed adjusting screw located on throttle chamber.
mechanic_notes: Air conditioner must be OFF during idle speed inspection and adjustment.

caption: Fig. ET-15 Idle mixture ratio adjustment
description: Procedure for forcing full-load enrichment during idle CO adjustment by shorting terminals 3 and 18 of throttle valve switch connector with a jumper wire, and adjusting air flow meter bypass screw.
components: Connector of throttle valve switch harness

callouts.5: Connector of throttle valve switch harness

wiring_and_connections: Jumper wire between terminal No. 3 and No. 18 on throttle valve switch harness connector
mechanic_notes: Turn bypass screw clockwise for rich mixture, counterclockwise for lean mixture.

caption: Fig. ET-16 Altitude switch (California models)
description: Location and harness disconnection point for the altitude switch on California models, situated near steering column / pedal support.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect connector when adjusting idle CO above 750 m (2,500 ft) on California models; reconnect after adjustment.

caption: Fig. ET-17 Rubber plug
description: Installing replacement rubber sealing plug into air flow meter bypass screw recess after mixture adjustment.
mechanic_notes: Install a new rubber plug (furnished as a service part) to seal air bypass screw cavity against moisture and unmetered air.

caption: Fig. ET-18 Releasing pressure in fuel system
description: Relieving residual fuel rail line pressure before filter replacement using jumper wires connected to battery and cold start valve for 2-3 seconds.
wiring_and_connections: Jumper wires from 12V battery to cold start valve harness terminals
mechanic_notes: Prevent short circuits by keeping jumper clips separate.

caption: Fig. ET-19 Fuel filter
description: Fuel filter mounting bracket, fuel inlet/outlet hose orientation, and securing bolt location.
measurements_and_specs: Clamp torque: 0.10 to 0.15 kg-m (0.7 to 1.1 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Do not reuse hose clamps after loosening. Ensure clamp is positioned 1 mm from hose end.

caption: Fig. ET-20 Air regulator hoses
description: Routing of air regulator bypass hoses connecting air duct, air regulator, and intake manifold.
mechanic_notes: Check for hardening, cracks, or loose clamps which introduce unmetered false air.

caption: Fig. ET-21 Air cleaner filter
description: Exploded view of the air cleaner assembly showing housing, filter element, cover, ducting, and wing nuts.
mechanic_notes: Do not brush or blow compressed air on viscous paper filter; replace according to maintenance schedule.

caption: Fig. ET-22 Crankcase emission control system
description: Cutaway diagram of positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) flow, showing fresh air intake pathway and blow-by gas extraction through PCV valve into intake manifold.
wiring_and_connections: Ventilator hose between crankcase baffle and PCV valve
Ventilation hose with flame arrester between rocker cover and throttle chamber
mechanic_notes: White open arrows indicate fresh air intake; solid black arrows indicate blow-by gas flow through internal engine passages.

caption: Fig. ET-23 Checking evaporative emission control system
description: Test setup schematic for evaporative vapor line pressure leak check using 3-way cock, compressed air source, manometer, and connections to vapor-liquid separator and carbon canister.
measurements_and_specs: Allowable drop after 2.5 minutes: within 25 mmH2O (0.98 inH2O)
wiring_and_connections: Vapor line between carbon canister and vapor-liquid separator
mechanic_notes: Removing filler cap should cause manometer reading to drop quickly to zero; failure to drop indicates clogged vent line.

caption: Fig. ET-24 Replacing carbon canister filter
description: Removal and replacement of bottom filter element from charcoal carbon canister body.
mechanic_notes: Check for saturated or contaminated filter element and replace periodically.

caption: Fig. ET-25 Fuel filler cap
description: Sectional view of fuel tank filler cap showing internal vacuum relief valve and spring mechanism.
mechanic_notes: Clean housing and test by inhaling; slight initial resistance should be felt followed by audible valve clicking and opening.

caption: ST10640001 Pivot adjuster
description: Special service tool ST10640001 (Kent-Moore J 25615-01) curved pivot adjuster offset wrench used for valve lash adjustment on L-series OHC engines.
mechanic_notes: Enables loosening and tightening of rocker pivot lock nut while adjusting pivot screw.

caption: ST19320000 Oil filter wrench
description: Special service tool ST19320000 (Kent-Moore J 25664) band-type oil filter removal wrench.
components: ST19320000 Oil filter wrench band and handle
mechanic_notes: Use only for filter removal; replacement oil filter should be hand tightened.

caption: Fig. FA-1 Front axle and suspension assembly
description: Cross-sectional and component assembly diagram of the front axle and front suspension system, showing strut assembly, transverse link, compression rod, stabilizer bar, front hub, and tightening torques for all primary fasteners.

callouts.A: T: 4.5 to 5.5 kg-m (33 to 40 ft-lb)
callouts.F: Steel wheel: 8 to 9 kg-m (58 to 65 ft-lb); Aluminum wheel: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: F: Steel wheel 8 to 9 kg-m (58 to 65 ft-lb), Aluminum wheel 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: All suspension bolts and nuts should be torqued to specified values. Transverse link, compression rod, and stabilizer bar interact to absorb braking, cornering, and vertical forces.

caption: Fig. FA-2 Tightening wheel bearing lock nut
description: Torquing the front wheel bearing lock nut using a torque wrench and socket to seat the bearings.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 2.5 to 3.0 kg-m (18 to 22 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten lock nut to 2.5 to 3.0 kg-m to seat the bearings prior to backing off.

caption: Fig. FA-3 Loosen wheel bearing lock nut 60°
description: Loosening the wheel bearing lock nut by 60 degrees using a wrench to achieve initial running clearance.
measurements_and_specs: Loosen angle: 60 degrees (up to 15 degrees additional if needed to align hole)
mechanic_notes: After seating, back off 60 degrees. Align adjusting cap slot with spindle hole; may loosen up to 15 degrees more if necessary.

caption: Fig. FA-4 Measuring wheel bearing rotation starting torque
description: Measuring front wheel bearing preload using a spring scale attached to a wheel hub stud at a 90-degree angle.

callouts.90\u00b0: Angle of pull relative to center line

measurements_and_specs: Starting torque (new parts): 4.0 to 8.5 kg-cm (3.5 to 7.4 in-lb)
Starting force at bolt (new parts): 0.7 to 1.5 kg (1.5 to 3.3 lb)
Starting torque (used parts): 1.0 to 4.5 kg-cm (0.9 to 3.9 in-lb)
Starting force at bolt (used parts): 0.2 to 0.8 kg (0.4 to 1.8 lb)
mechanic_notes: Attach spring balance to hub bolt and pull at right angle to a line drawn through center of bearing and hub bolt.

caption: Fig. FA-5 Installing cotter pin
description: Installation and bending of cotter pin through the adjusting cap and spindle hole to lock the wheel bearing adjustment.
mechanic_notes: Spread cotter pin legs away from each other against the sides of the adjusting cap.

file: markdown/1978 280z FSM/diagrams/FA Front Axle and Suspension/fig_fa_6_measuring_toe_in.png
caption: Fig. FA-6 Measuring toe-in
description: Measuring front wheel toe-in across the front wheels using a drive-on/trammel toe-in gauge.
mechanic_notes: Car must be at curb weight on level ground when measuring toe-in.

file: markdown/1978 280z FSM/diagrams/FA Front Axle and Suspension/fig_fa_7_adjusting_toe_in.png
caption: Fig. FA-7 Adjusting toe-in
description: Adjusting front wheel toe-in by loosening side rod lock nut and rotating side rod.
mechanic_notes: Loosen lock nut 1 and rotate side rod 2. Left and right side rods must be adjusted equally.

caption: Fig. FA-8 Standard length of side rod
description: Dimensional cross section of the steering rack side rod ball socket and stopper nut showing standard length dimension.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Distance between centers of side rods should be equal on both sides. Stopper nut end surface forms the steering stopper against rack housing.

caption: Fig. FA-9 Measuring steering angle, camber and caster
description: Front wheel positioned on turning radius gauge turntable with alignment gauge attached to wheel hub to measure steering angle, camber, and caster.
mechanic_notes: Adjust steering angle using turning radius gauge before performing final toe-in adjustment.

caption: Fig. FA-10 Removing brake tube and caliper fixing bolts
description: Disconnecting the brake tube flare nut and removing the caliper fixing bolts on the front strut assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Brake tube flare nut tightening torque: 1.5 to 1.8 kg-m (11 to 13 ft-lb)
Caliper fixing bolt tightening torque: 7.3 to 9.9 kg-m (53 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Disconnect brake hydraulic tube flare nut before removing caliper bolts.

file: markdown/1978 280z FSM/diagrams/FA Front Axle and Suspension/fig_fa_11_removing_hub_cap.png
caption: Fig. FA-11 Removing hub cap
description: Prying off front wheel hub grease cap using two screwdrivers prying equally from opposite sides.
mechanic_notes: Use caution to avoid damaging O-ring under hub cap. Tap lightly with soft hammer if needed.

caption: Fig. FA-12 Removing wheel hub
description: Sliding the front wheel hub assembly off the spindle with bearing installed.
mechanic_notes: Wheel hub may be removed together with disc rotor.

caption: Fig. FA-13 Removing wheel bearing outer race
description: Driving out the wheel bearing outer race from the wheel hub using a hammer and brass drift through hub internal grooves.
mechanic_notes: Utilize two grooves inside hub to alternate drift hits around race perimeter.

caption: Fig. FA-14 Removing disc brake rotor
description: Loosening the four disc brake rotor mounting bolts to separate rotor from wheel hub.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 3.9 to 5.3 kg-m (28 to 38 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Loosen four bolts securing brake disc; torque to 3.9 to 5.3 kg-m upon reassembly.

caption: Fig. FA-15 Removing baffle plate screws
description: Removing screws securing splash baffle / dust shield plate to knuckle spindle.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 0.32 to 0.44 kg-m (2.3 to 3.2 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Loosen screws securing baffle plate in position; tighten to 0.32 to 0.44 kg-m upon assembly.

caption: Fig. FA-16 Installing wheel bearing outer race
description: Pressing or driving wheel bearing outer race into wheel hub using drift ST35300000.
mechanic_notes: Drive outer race squarely into hub until fully seated against shoulder using tool ST35300000.

caption: Fig. FA-17 Lubricating points of wheel hub
description: Cross section of wheel hub showing cavity areas and recesses to be packed with multi-purpose grease.
mechanic_notes: Pack inner cavity recess of hub and hub cap with recommended multi-purpose grease to specified level.

caption: Fig. FA-18 Filling bearing cone with grease
description: Hand packing bearing cone cavities with multi-purpose grease from grease container.
mechanic_notes: Pack cavities between rollers of each bearing cone thoroughly with grease.

caption: Fig. FA-19 Filling grease seal lip pocket with grease
description: Applying grease to the seal lip pocket of a new grease seal prior to installation.
mechanic_notes: Lubricate sealing lips and fill lip pocket with multi-purpose grease before pressing seal into hub.

caption: Fig. FA-20 Sectional view of strut assembly
description: Cross-sectional detail view of front strut cartridge assembly including internal valving, check valves, piston, cylinder, and shock absorber expansion/compression flow operation.
mechanic_notes: The piston rod, piston rod guide, cylinder, and bottom valve are precision matched parts and must be replaced as a set if faulty.

caption: Fig. FA-21 Disconnecting brake hose
description: Disconnecting the brake hose flare nut from strut bracket and removing retaining U-clip/locking spring.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.5 to 1.8 kg-m (11 to 13 ft-lb)
wiring_and_connections: Brake hydraulic flexible hose and hard tube
mechanic_notes: Tighten flare nut to 1.5 to 1.8 kg-m upon reinstallation.

caption: Fig. FA-22 Removing bolts connecting knuckle arm
description: Loosening the two bolts securing the knuckle arm to the bottom flange of the front strut assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 7.3 to 9.9 kg-m (53 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Force transverse link downward with pry bar after bolt removal to detach knuckle arm.

caption: Fig. FA-23 [Upper strut mounting nuts under hood]
description: Location of the three upper strut mounting nuts in the engine compartment / hood ledge tower.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 2.5 to 3.5 kg-m (18 to 25 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Support strut with jack underneath before removing the 3 tower mounting nuts.

caption: Fig. FA-24 Removing front strut Assembly
description: Lowering the jack and removing the front strut assembly with coil spring from vehicle wheel well.
mechanic_notes: Hold strut by hand while lowering jack to prevent falling.

caption: Fig. FA-25 Removing self-locking nut
description: Compressing the coil spring with compressor tool ST3565S001 and unscrewing the top self-locking nut from piston rod.
mechanic_notes: Hook tool evenly over minimum of 3 coils. Protect body stud threads when leveraging screwdriver.

caption: Fig. FA-26 Removing gland packing
description: Unscrewing gland packing nut from top of strut casing using special gland packing wrench KV40100800 while bottom is held in vise.
mechanic_notes: Retract piston rod completely down before loosening gland packing.

caption: Fig. FA-27 Removing piston rod and cylinder
description: Lifting the shock absorber cylinder and piston rod together as a matched assembly out of the strut outer casing.
mechanic_notes: Do not disassemble piston rod guide from cylinder; handle as matched set.

caption: Fig. FA-28 Exploded view of strut assembly
description: Exploded component view of front strut, coil spring, upper seat, insulator, thrust bearing, dust seal, and bound bumper rubber.
mechanic_notes: Assemble components in strict numbered sequence. Check rubber insulator and thrust bearing for wear.

caption: Fig. FA-29 Filling outer casing with fluid
description: Pouring genuine shock absorber oil into the outer casing of the strut assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Fluid type: NISSAN GENUINE STRUT OIL or equivalent
mechanic_notes: Strictly pour 340 cc of genuine strut oil into outer casing to maintain correct shock absorber damping force.

caption: Fig. FA-30 Installing gland packing
description: Sliding gland packing over piston rod guide using special gland packing guide tool ST35540000.
mechanic_notes: Guide protects seal lip during installation over rod threads.

caption: Fig. FA-31 Sectional view of gland packing
description: Cross-sectional view of gland packing assembly highlighting grease lubrication point on internal sealing lip.

callouts.Grease: Lubricate sealing lip with multi-purpose grease

mechanic_notes: Lubricate sealing lip marked with grease before sliding onto rod guide.

caption: Fig. FA-32 Tightening gland packing
description: Torquing gland packing with wrench KV40100800 attached to a torque wrench.
measurements_and_specs: Gland packing tightening torque: 7 to 13 kg-m (51 to 94 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Apply torque formula adjustment when using wrench adapter KV40100800.

caption: Fig. FA-33 Gland packing wrench
description: Dimensional diagram showing gland packing wrench KV40100800 with effective torque adapter offset length 0.10 m (0.33 ft) and torque wrench length l.
mechanic_notes: Use formula C = 7 * (l / (l + 0.10)) kg-m to compensate for the 0.10 m offset.

caption: Fig. FA-34 Bleeding air from strut
description: Technician bleeding trapped air from shock absorber by cycling piston rod in inverted and upright positions.
measurements_and_specs: Rod extension before tightening: approx 120 mm (4.72 in)
mechanic_notes: Extend rod with spindle down, then invert and retract rod fully. Repeat until stroke resistance is equal and smooth.

caption: Fig. FA-35 Strut mounting bearing greasing point
description: Cutaway illustration of strut upper mount indicating grease application points and orientation of thrust bearing.
mechanic_notes: Install mounting bearing so that it points in correct direction. Lubricate indicated bearing races with multi-purpose grease.

caption: Fig. FA-36 Installing front spring
description: Orientation of front coil spring bottom end seated into the contour groove of the strut lower spring seat.

callouts.Lower end: Bottom coil end seated against step

mechanic_notes: Align the lower coil tail cleanly against the seat stop before releasing spring compressor.

caption: Fig. FA-37 Removing stabilizer and compression rod
description: Underbody diagram indicating fastener locations for compression rod bracket nut 1, transverse link bolts 2, stabilizer connecting link nut 3, and stabilizer bar chassis bracket bolts 4.

callouts.1: Nut securing compression rod to bracket
callouts.2: Bolts securing compression rod to transverse link
callouts.3: Nut connecting stabilizer connecting rod to transverse link
callouts.4: Bolts securing stabilizer bracket in position

mechanic_notes: Remove nuts and bolts in sequence 1 to 4 to detach stabilizer bar and compression rod.

caption: Fig. FA-38 Removing transverse link
description: Detaching the transverse link pivot pin from the front suspension crossmember.
mechanic_notes: Loosen transverse link mounting bar and separate link from suspension member.

caption: Fig. FA-39 Removing knuckle arm
description: Separating the steering knuckle arm from the lower ball joint taper stud on the transverse link.
mechanic_notes: Knuckle arm is taper fit to ball joint stud. If stuck, screw nut onto stud and strike nut with hammer.

caption: Fig. FA-40 Removing transverse link bushing
description: Pressing the rubber bushing out of the transverse link eye using press replacer set ST36710000.
components: Transverse link bushing replacer set ST36710000

callouts.ST36710000: Front Transverse Link Bushing Replacer Set

mechanic_notes: Support eye squarely on replacer base and press bushing straight through using drift.

caption: Fig. FA-41 Sectional view of lower ball joint
description: Cross-sectional view of the lower ball joint assembly showing ball stud, seat, grease plug/nipple location, and dust boot.
measurements_and_specs: Turning torque (new parts): 75 to 125 kg-cm (65 to 109 in-lb)
Turning torque (used parts): More than 50 kg-cm (43 in-lb)
mechanic_notes: Lubricate ball joint by replacing plug with nipple and pumping multi-purpose grease until old grease purges.

caption: Fig. FA-42 Sectional view of transverse link bushing
description: Cross section showing transverse link rubber bushing installed flush into transverse link eye, noting front-to-rear orientation.
mechanic_notes: Press bushing until outer tube is flush with transverse link eye surface. Pay careful attention to front/rear orientation.

caption: Fig. FA-43 Tightening knuckle arm castle nut
description: Torquing the castle nut on the knuckle arm ball joint taper stud with socket wrench.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 5.5 to 7.5 kg-m (40 to 54 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Torque castle nut to 5.5 to 7.5 kg-m, then advance up to 60 degrees to align slot with cotter pin hole.

caption: Fig. FA-44 Removing engine mounting bolts
description: Location of engine mounting bolts connecting engine insulator brackets to the front suspension crossmember.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.6 to 2.1 kg-m (12 to 15 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Support engine weight with hoist before removing engine mounting bolts. Tighten to 1.6 to 2.1 kg-m.

caption: Fig. FA-45 Removing suspension crossmember
description: Location of frame mounting bolts securing front suspension crossmember to chassis side rails.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4.5 to 5.0 kg-m (33 to 36 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten crossmember to frame bolts to 4.5 to 5.0 kg-m.

caption: ST35300000 Drift
description: Front wheel bearing outer race installing drift tool.
mechanic_notes: Used to press or drive outer bearing races squarely into front wheel hub.

caption: ST35540000 Gland packing guide
description: Tapered guide sleeve for installing gland packing oil seal over piston rod.
mechanic_notes: Prevents damage to gland packing inner oil seal lips when sliding over piston rod threads and shoulders.

caption: ST3565S001 Coil spring compressor set
description: Coil spring compressor fixture with threaded spindle and safety hooks.
mechanic_notes: Must engage at least three active spring coils securely before compressing.

caption: HT72520000 Ball joint remover
description: Scissor-type mechanical ball joint puller/separator tool.
mechanic_notes: Separates tie rod and ball joint tapered pins without damaging rubber dust boots.

caption: KV40100800 Gland packing wrench
