caption: Fig. MT-1 F4W71B transmission
description: Cross-sectional longitudinal cutaway view of the complete F4W71B 4-speed manual transmission assembly, detailing the main drive gear, synchronizers, mainshaft gears, countershaft cluster, reverse idler gear, striking rod linkage, adapter plate, and housing structure.
mechanic_notes: Main drive gear meshes with counter drive gear; mainshaft is piloted in the main drive gear by needle bearings. Adapter plate supports center bearings.

caption: Fig. MT-2 F4W71B transmission case components
description: Exploded view diagram of the transmission case, adapter plate, bearing retainer, rear extension housing, front cover, gaskets, and attaching hardware.
mechanic_notes: Pay attention to dowel pin alignment between transmission case, adapter plate, and rear extension housing.

caption: Fig. MT-3 F4W71B transmission gear components
description: Exploded view illustrating the gear train components of the F4W71B 4-speed transmission, including main drive gear, mainshaft gears, synchronizer assemblies, countershaft assembly, and reverse idler.
mechanic_notes: Mainshaft nut should be discarded and replaced upon disassembly. Note correct order and orientation of synchronizer insert springs and shifting inserts.

caption: Fig. MT-4 F4W71B transmission shift control components
description: Exploded view diagram of F4W71B internal shift linkage components, including striking lever, guide, striking rod, shift forks, fork rods, check balls, check springs, interlock balls, and control lever assembly.
mechanic_notes: Note orientation of check balls and interlock balls in the adapter plate to prevent dual engagement.

caption: Fig. MT-5 Removing control lever
description: Illustration showing removal of the transmission gearshift control lever by removing the E-ring and pin from the striking rod guide.
mechanic_notes: Place transmission control lever in neutral position before removing E-ring and control lever pin.

caption: Fig. MT-6 Bottom view of car
description: Underside view of vehicle showing disconnection locations for reverse lamp switch wiring, clutch operating cylinder, and speedometer cable.
mechanic_notes: Remove clutch operating cylinder and let it hang or tie out of way; disconnect speedometer cable before dropping rear extension.

caption: Fig. MT-7 Removing propeller shaft
description: Illustration of propeller shaft flange bolts removal at the transmission companion flange.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 3.5 to 4.5 kg-m (25 to 33 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten propeller shaft bolts to 3.5 to 4.5 kg-m (25 to 33 ft-lb) on reassembly.

caption: Fig. MT-8 Tightening torque
description: Diagram illustrating tightening torque patterns and values for transmission bellhousing-to-engine bolts.
measurements_and_specs: Top transmission to engine bolts: 4.4 to 5.9 kg-m (32 to 43 ft-lb)
Bottom bolts (engine rear plate to transmission): 0.9 to 1.2 kg-m (6.5 to 8.7 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Ensure proper torque distribution across upper heavy bellhousing bolts and lower sheet-metal rear plate bolts.

caption: Fig. MT-9 Removing striking rod E-ring and stopper pin
description: Detailed illustration showing the removal of E-ring and stopper guide pin from the rear end of the transmission rear extension housing.
mechanic_notes: Remove E-ring and pull stopper guide pin prior to removing rear extension housing.

caption: Fig. MT-10 Removing return spring plug
description: Technician using a wrench to remove the return spring plug from the side of the rear extension housing.
mechanic_notes: Keep track of return spring, reverse check spring, and plunger when plug is removed.

caption: Fig. MT-11 Removing rear extension
description: Removing rear extension housing from adapter plate by lightly tapping with a soft mallet while turning the striking rod leftward.
mechanic_notes: Turn striking rod toward left to disengage striking lever before tapping rear extension off.

caption: Fig. MT-12 Removing main drive bearing snap ring
description: Using snap ring expander pliers to remove the large snap ring securing the main drive gear front bearing inside the transmission front case.
mechanic_notes: Remove front cover and countershaft front shim before expanding and removing main drive bearing snap ring.

caption: Fig. MT-13 Removing transmission case
description: Separating transmission bellhousing case from the adapter plate using a soft mallet.
mechanic_notes: Tap case gently with soft hammer to break sealant bond without cracking aluminum mating flanges.

caption: Fig. MT-14 Attaching gear assembly to special tool
description: Mounting the adapter plate and gear train assembly onto Setting Plate Adapter ST23810001 clamped in a workbench vise.
mechanic_notes: Mount assembly with countershaft side facing upwards in vise.

caption: Fig. MT-15 Drive out retaining pins
description: Technician using Fork Rod Pin Punch KV31100300 and a hammer to drive out roll pins securing shift forks to fork rods.
mechanic_notes: Retaining roll pins should be replaced with new pins upon reassembly.

caption: Fig. MT-16 Layout of check ball and interlock ball
description: Cutaway diagram showing relative positions and channels of the three check balls, four interlock balls, and fork rods in the adapter plate.
mechanic_notes: CRITICAL: Do not lose check balls or interlock balls. Note order: 1st/2nd fork rod, 2 interlock balls, 3rd/4th rod, 2 interlock balls, reverse rod.

caption: Fig. MT-17 Removing countershaft front bearing
description: Using a two-jaw gear puller to remove counter gear front bearing while transmission gears are doubly engaged to lock rotation.
mechanic_notes: Engage two gears simultaneously (double engage) to prevent shaft rotation during puller operation.

caption: Fig. MT-18 Removing counter drive gear and main drive gear
description: Pulling counter drive gear together with main drive gear off the shafts using a puller.
mechanic_notes: Take care not to allow the pilot needle bearing to drop from the front end of the mainshaft.

caption: Fig. MT-19 Removing mainshaft nut
description: Releasing lock staking on mainshaft rear nut and unscrewing the nut with a socket bar while gears are locked.
mechanic_notes: Unstake lock collar before loosening nut. Always discard used mainshaft nut; never reuse.

caption: Fig. MT-20 Driving out gear assembly
description: Technician supporting mainshaft gear assembly with one hand while tapping the rear end with a soft hammer to drive out mainshaft and counter gear together.
mechanic_notes: Carefully hold front of mainshaft assembly by hand while tapping to prevent the counter gear from dropping.

caption: Fig. MT-21 Removing 1st gear bushing
description: Using Bearing Puller ST30031000 under a hydraulic press to press off 1st gear mainshaft bushing along with 2nd gear and 1st & 2nd synchronizer assembly.
mechanic_notes: Hold mainshaft by hand while pressing out bushing to prevent it from dropping onto the floor.

caption: Fig. MT-22 Mainshaft assembly
description: Exploded view diagram of the complete mainshaft assembly showing sequence of all gears, needle bearings, synchronizer assemblies, bushings, thrust washers, steel ball, main bearing, and nut.
mechanic_notes: Pay strict attention to placement of steel ball (22) that locks thrust washer (17). Observe synchronizer hub front/rear orientation.

caption: Fig. MT-23 Removing main drive bearing
description: Press setup showing Bearing Puller ST30031000 supporting the main drive bearing while the press ram drives out the main drive gear shaft.
mechanic_notes: Remove snap ring and spacer before pressing off bearing.

caption: Fig. MT-24 Removing countershaft bearing
description: Press setup showing countershaft rear bearing removal using Bearing Puller ST30031000 under a shop press.
mechanic_notes: Hold shaft by hand so as not to allow countershaft to drop onto the shop floor when bearing releases.

caption: Fig. MT-25 Inspecting ball bearing
description: Hand inspection of a transmission ball bearing, slowly turning inner race by hand to detect roughness, axial play, or damaged balls/races.
mechanic_notes: Do not spin bearings with compressed air, as lack of lubrication at high speed damages races and balls.

caption: Fig. MT-26 Measuring end play
description: Using a flat feeler gauge (thickness gauge) inserted between gear faces on the mainshaft to measure axial end play.
measurements_and_specs: 1st gear end play: 0.32 to 0.39 mm (0.0126 to 0.0154 in)
2nd gear end play: 0.12 to 0.19 mm (0.0047 to 0.0075 in)
3rd gear end play: 0.13 to 0.37 mm (0.0051 to 0.0146 in)
Reverse counter gear end play: 0.01 to 0.20 mm (0.0004 to 0.0079 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure gear end play with feeler gauge while gears are installed on shaft.

caption: Fig. MT-27 Baulk ring-to-cone gap
description: Cross-sectional detail illustration showing measurement of the gap between the baulk ring face and the gear cone clutch surface.
measurements_and_specs: Standard gap: 1.2 to 1.6 mm (0.047 to 0.063 in)
mechanic_notes: Hold baulk ring firmly against gear cone when checking gap. If clearance is 0.8 mm (0.031 in) or less, baulk ring must be replaced.

caption: Fig. MT-28 Front cover oil seal
description: Cross section showing correct installation direction and lip orientation of front cover oil seal.
mechanic_notes: Press-fit oil seal with sealing lip facing inward/front as indicated by arrow; coat lip with gear oil prior to assembly.

caption: Fig. MT-29 Rear extension oil seal
description: Cross section showing correct press-in orientation of the rear extension housing rear output oil seal.
mechanic_notes: Press-fit oil seal squarely into housing seat; apply grease to oil seal lip and bushing prior to driveshaft installation.

caption: Fig. MT-30 Oil gutter
description: Illustration of the oil gutter installation and bending orientation on the adapter plate.
mechanic_notes: Bend oil gutter on front side and expand on rear side after positioning.

caption: Fig. MT-31 Staking screw
description: Using a center punch to stake bearing retainer attaching screws at two points on the adapter plate.
measurements_and_specs: Screw torque: 1.9 to 2.5 kg-m (14 to 18 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Torque screws to 1.9 to 2.5 kg-m (14 to 18 ft-lb) and stake each screw at two points to prevent loosening.

caption: Fig. MT-32 Installing synchronizer hub
description: Cross-sectional comparison showing correct front-to-rear installation orientation of 4th & 3rd synchronizer hub versus 2nd & 1st synchronizer hub.
mechanic_notes: Notice asymmetry of boss length between 3rd/4th and 1st/2nd synchronizer hubs. Assemble facing proper direction.

caption: Fig. MT-33 Installing thrust washer
description: Technician sliding thrust washer over 1st gear on the mainshaft, ensuring alignment with the locking steel ball.
mechanic_notes: Apply grease to steel ball to hold it in place on mainshaft before sliding thrust washer on.

caption: Fig. MT-34 Transmission Press Stand
description: Detailed diagram of Transmission Press Stand KV31100400 showing hole locations for counter gear, reverse idler shaft, and mainshaft.
mechanic_notes: Provides solid base for pressing mainshaft and countershaft into adapter plate bearings without cocking.

caption: Fig. MT-35 Installing mainshaft assembly
description: Press setup pressing mainshaft assembly into the center bearing on adapter plate supported on Press Stand KV31100400.
mechanic_notes: Ensure bearing is square against shaft; press into place gradually.

caption: Fig. MT-36 Installing counter gear
description: Press setup showing counter gear being pressed into adapter plate rear bearing while assembly rests on Press Stand KV31100400.
mechanic_notes: Support counter gear rear bearing properly on press stand during pressing.

caption: Fig. MT-37 Installing snap ring
description: Installing snap ring in the front end groove of the mainshaft ahead of the 3rd & 4th synchronizer assembly thrust washer.
measurements_and_specs: Snap ring thickness: 1.4 mm, 1.5 mm, or 1.6 mm
mechanic_notes: Select snap ring of thickness that minimizes axial clearance in mainshaft groove.

caption: Fig. MT-38 Installing counter drive gear
description: Pressing counter drive gear onto counter gear using Counter Gear Drift ST23860000 while meshing gears.
mechanic_notes: CRITICAL: Counter drive gear and main drive gear must be driven on simultaneously with teeth meshed.

caption: Fig. MT-39 Installing snap ring
description: Fitting counter drive gear retaining snap ring to front end groove of countershaft.
measurements_and_specs: Counter drive gear snap ring thickness: 1.4 mm, 1.5 mm, or 1.6 mm
mechanic_notes: Secure counter drive gear with the thickest snap ring that fits the groove.

caption: Fig. MT-40 Installing counter gear front bearing
description: Pressing counter gear front bearing onto countershaft using Bearing Drift ST22360002 on Press Stand KV31100400.
mechanic_notes: Ensure bearing is pressed firmly against counter drive gear shoulder.

caption: Fig. MT-41 Installing counter reverse gear snap ring
description: Installing snap ring on rear end of countershaft to retain counter reverse gear with assembly mounted on Setting Plate Adapter ST23810001.
measurements_and_specs: Counter reverse gear snap ring thickness: 1.4 mm, 1.5 mm, or 1.6 mm
mechanic_notes: Select snap ring thickness that gives minimum gear end play (less than 0.20 mm).

caption: Fig. MT-42 Tightening mainshaft nut
description: Tightening the mainshaft rear nut using Special Wrench ST22520000 attached to a click-type or beam-type torque wrench.
measurements_and_specs: Specified nut torque: 14.0 to 17.0 kg-m (101 to 123 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Gears must be doubly engaged to lock the shaft while torquing mainshaft nut.

caption: Fig. MT-43 Setting wrench
description: Schematic diagram showing geometry of torque wrench with Special Wrench ST22520000 extension, defining effective length L and extension offset 0.10 m (0.33 ft).
mechanic_notes: Because ST22520000 extends the lever arm by 0.10 m (0.33 ft), wrench reading C is lower than actual applied torque at the nut.

caption: Fig. MT-44 Converted torque
description: Nomograph chart plotting converted torque scale reading C (kg-m, ft-lb) against effective torque wrench length L (m, ft) with upper and lower limit tolerance lines.

callouts.C: Value read on the torque wrench (kg-m / ft-lb)
callouts.L: Effective length of torque wrench (m / ft)

measurements_and_specs: Target nut torque: 14 to 17 kg-m (101 to 123 ft-lb)
For L = 0.40 m: C = 11.2 to 13.6 kg-m (81 to 98 ft-lb)
For L = 0.50 m: C = 11.7 to 14.2 kg-m (84 to 103 ft-lb)
For L = 0.60 m: C = 12.0 to 14.6 kg-m (87 to 105 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Look up torque wrench length on horizontal axis to find required gauge reading range.

caption: Fig. MT-45 Staking mainshaft nut
description: Using a hammer and punch to stake the thin collar of the mainshaft nut into the groove of the mainshaft.
mechanic_notes: Stake nut securely into mainshaft spline groove to prevent backing off.

caption: Fig. MT-46 Installing 1st & 2nd fork rod
description: Sliding the 1st & 2nd fork rod through adapter plate bores and shift fork.
mechanic_notes: Align detent notches in rod with check ball bore. Use new roll pins.

caption: Fig. MT-47 Installing 3rd & 4th fork rod
description: Installing 3rd & 4th fork rod through adapter plate and 3rd & 4th shift fork.
mechanic_notes: CRITICAL: Install two interlock balls into adapter plate bore before inserting 3rd & 4th fork rod.

caption: Fig. MT-48 Installing reverse fork rod
description: Installing reverse shift fork and reverse fork rod through adapter plate.
mechanic_notes: Install two interlock balls into adapter plate prior to inserting reverse fork rod. Check ball plug torque: 1.9 to 2.5 kg-m (14 to 18 ft-lb).

caption: Fig. MT-49 Fitting main drive bearing snap ring
description: Using snap ring expander to seat large snap ring into the main drive bearing outer race groove through front case opening.
mechanic_notes: Ensure snap ring is fully seated in outer race groove around its entire circumference.

caption: Fig. MT-50 Selecting counter gear front bearing shim
description: Diagram illustrating depth measurement dimension 'A' from front face of transmission case to the counter gear front bearing outer race for shim selection.

callouts.A: Measurement dimension from case front face to bearing face

measurements_and_specs: Dimension 'A' range: 2.92 to 3.71 mm (0.1150 to 0.1461 in)
mechanic_notes: Accurately measure depth 'A' using depth micrometer or vernier caliper to choose proper compensating shim.

caption: Fig. MT-51 FS5W71B transmission
description: Cross-sectional longitudinal cutaway view of FS5W71B 5-speed manual transmission showing overdrive gear arrangement behind adapter plate, servo synchro mechanism, and all internal shafts and gears.
mechanic_notes: FS5W71B features Warner synchromesh on 1st-4th gears and Porsche-type servo synchromesh with band brake on 5th (overdrive) gear.

caption: Fig. MT-52 FS5W71B transmission case components
description: Exploded view diagram of FS5W71B 5-speed transmission casing assemblies, front cover, adapter plate, rear extension housing, breather, and oil seals.
mechanic_notes: Note breather vent location on top of rear extension housing and dust cover on rear sleeve yoke.

caption: Fig. MT-53 FS5W71B transmission gear components
description: Exploded view illustration of all gear train components of FS5W71B 5-speed transmission including overdrive main gear, overdrive synchronizer components, reverse gears, countershaft cluster, and reverse idler shaft.
mechanic_notes: Observe assembly sequence of OD brake band (17), thrust block (16), synchro ring (18), and circlip (15). Discard nuts 22 and 34 after removal.

caption: Fig. MT-54 FS5W71B transmission shift control components
description: Exploded view diagram of FS5W71B shift control linkages, including striking lever, striking guide, striking rod, expansion plug, fork rods (including reverse & OD rod), and shift forks.
mechanic_notes: FS5W71B features combined reverse & overdrive shift fork and fork rod. Expansion plug (7) seals rear end of striking rod bore.

caption: Fig. MT-55 Removing counter gear nut
description: Loosening counter gear nut at rear of countershaft with socket wrench while gears are doubly engaged.
mechanic_notes: Unstake locking flange before loosening. Counter gear nut and mainshaft nut must be discarded and never reused.

caption: Fig. MT-56 Removing counter overdrive gear and bearing
description: Drawing counter overdrive gear and rear ball bearing off the countershaft rear extension using a puller.
mechanic_notes: Use a suitable puller engaged behind the bearing outer/inner race.

caption: Fig. MT-57 Removing mainshaft rear bearing
description: Using Mainshaft Rear Bearing Puller KV32101330 to draw the mainshaft rear ball bearing off the mainshaft.
mechanic_notes: Remove snap rings and speedometer gear before pulling mainshaft rear bearing.

caption: Fig. MT-58 Installing overdrive gear assembly
description: Front face and sectional view of the Porsche-type servo overdrive synchronizer assembly showing placement of synchro ring, brake band, thrust block, anchor block, and circlip.
mechanic_notes: Carefully fit anchor block and thrust block into their respective recesses in the clutch gear before securing with circlip.

caption: Fig. MT-59 Reverse idler gear
description: Assembly cross-section and orientation of the reverse idler gear on its shaft with spacers, needle bearing, and retaining snap rings.
mechanic_notes: Verify forward facing orientation of reverse idler gear step and ensure snap rings are fully engaged in shaft grooves.

caption: Fig. MT-60 Tightening mainshaft nut
description: Tightening mainshaft lock nut on FS5W71B using Special Wrench ST22520000 with gears locked by double engagement.
measurements_and_specs: Counter gear lock nut torque: 10.0 to 13.0 kg-m (72 to 94 ft-lb)
Mainshaft lock nut converted torque formula: Fig. MT-44
mechanic_notes: Use Wrench ST22520000 and calculate converted torque based on torque wrench effective length.

caption: Fig. MT-61 Staking mainshaft nuts
description: Using hammer and punch to stake both the mainshaft lock nut and counter gear lock nut into shaft grooves.
mechanic_notes: Both nuts must be securely staked into the respective shaft locking notches.

caption: Fig. MT-62 Assembling mainshaft rear bearing
description: Driving mainshaft rear bearing onto mainshaft using Bearing Drift ST22350000 and hammer.
mechanic_notes: Drive bearing squarely until seated against shoulder, then select thickest snap ring to eliminate axial play.

caption: ST23810001 Setting plate adapter
description: Setting plate adapter plate fixture for clamping transmission adapter plate securely in a workbench vise during disassembly and assembly.
measurements_and_specs: Reference: Fig. MT-14, Fig. MT-15, Fig. MT-41
mechanic_notes: Applicable to all S30 series models.

caption: ST22360002 Bearing drift
description: Cylindrical bearing drift for pressing counter gear front bearing onto the countershaft.
mechanic_notes: Applicable to all S30 series models.

caption: KV31100300 Fork rod pin punch
description: Pin punch specifically sized for driving roll retaining pins into and out of shift forks and fork rods.
mechanic_notes: Applicable to all S30 series models.

caption: ST22520000 Wrench
description: Special offset torque wrench adapter socket for tightening mainshaft lock nut.
measurements_and_specs: Reference: Fig. MT-42, Fig. MT-43, Fig. MT-60
mechanic_notes: Applicable to all S30 series models. Requires torque calculation conversion formula.

caption: ST30031000 Bearing puller
description: Split-plate bearing puller attachment for dismounting main drive bearing, countershaft bearing, and 1st gear bushing under a press.
measurements_and_specs: Reference: Fig. MT-21, Fig. MT-23, Fig. MT-24
mechanic_notes: Applicable to all S30 series models.

caption: KV32101330 Bearing puller
description: Special puller assembly for drawing off mainshaft rear bearing on FS5W71B transmission.
mechanic_notes: Specific to FS5W71B 5-speed manual transmission.

caption: KV31100400 Transmission press stand
description: Multi-hole transmission press stand supporting the adapter plate and shafts during shop press operations.
measurements_and_specs: Reference: Fig. MT-34, Fig. MT-35, Fig. MT-36, Fig. MT-40
mechanic_notes: Applicable to all S30 series models.

caption: ST22350000 Mainshaft bearing drift
description: Tubular drift sleeve used for driving the mainshaft rear bearing onto the mainshaft of FS5W71B transmission.
mechanic_notes: Specific to FS5W71B 5-speed manual transmission.

caption: ST23860000 Counter gear drift
description: Counter gear drift for pressing counter drive gear onto countershaft with gears meshed.
mechanic_notes: Applicable to all S30 series models.

caption: ST23800000 Transmission adapter
description: Transmission adapter drift sleeve for pressing main drive bearing onto the shaft of the main drive gear.
mechanic_notes: Applicable to all S30 series models.

caption: Fig. PD-1 Cross-sectional view of propeller shaft
description: Cross-sectional view of the 2-joint propeller shaft showing sleeve yoke, journal, bearing race, tube assembly, and flange yoke with dimensions.
measurements_and_specs: L: 565 mm (22.24 in) for HLS30 (2 seater)
L: 865 mm (34.06 in) for GHLS30 (2 + 2 seater)
mechanic_notes: Propeller shaft and universal joint are balanced as an assembly. Dynamic unbalance under 35 gr-cm (0.49 in-oz) at 5,800 rpm.

caption: Fig. PD-2 Cross-sectional view of differential carrier
description: Cross-sectional longitudinal view of the Type R180 differential carrier showing the internal pinion, differential case, bearings, seals, retainers, and torque callouts.

callouts.2: Front oil seal (Supply grease to oil seal lip when assembling)
callouts.9: Side retainer adjusting shim (Adjust side bearing preload and ring gear-to-drive pinion backlash by selecting 9.)
callouts.13: Side oil seal (Supply grease to oil seal lip when assembly.)
callouts.15: Thrust washer (Adjust the pinion mate-to-side gear backlash to 0.1 to 0.2 mm (0.004 to 0.008 in) by 15.)
callouts.27: Pinion bearing adjusting washer (Adjust pinion bearing preload by selecting 26 and 27.)
callouts.A: Tightening torque: 17 to 20 kg-m (123 to 145 ft-lb)
callouts.B: Tightening torque: 0.9 to 1.2 kg-m (6.5 to 8.7 ft-lb)
callouts.C: Tightening torque: 6.0 to 7.0 kg-m (43 to 51 ft-lb)
callouts.D: Tightening torque: 9.0 to 10.0 kg-m (65 to 72 ft-lb)

measurements_and_specs: Pinion mate-to-side gear backlash: 0.1 to 0.2 mm (0.004 to 0.008 in)
Companion flange nut tightening torque: 17 to 20 kg-m (123 to 145 ft-lb)
Side retainer bolt tightening torque: 0.9 to 1.2 kg-m (6.5 to 8.7 ft-lb)
Rear cover to mounting member lock nut tightening torque: 6.0 to 7.0 kg-m (43 to 51 ft-lb)
Ring gear bolt tightening torque: 9.0 to 10.0 kg-m (65 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Supply grease to front oil seal lip and side oil seal lip when assembling.

caption: Fig. PD-3 Holding differential carrier
description: Differential carrier clamped onto Gear Carrier Attachment KV38100800.
mechanic_notes: Mount carrier on Gear Carrier Attachment KV38100800 before removing rear cover.

caption: Fig. PD-4 Removing side bearing outer race
description: Extracting side bearing outer race from side retainer using puller ST33290001.
mechanic_notes: Extract bearing outer race from side retainer using puller ST33290001.

caption: Fig. PD-5 Removing drive pinion nut
description: Loosening drive pinion nut using flange wrench ST31530000 on companion flange.
mechanic_notes: Hold companion flange with wrench ST31530000 while loosening nut.

caption: Fig. PD-6 Removing pinion rear bearing inner race
description: Holding rear bearing inner race with puller ST30031000 and extracting from drive pinion with a press.
mechanic_notes: Extract from drive pinion with a press.

caption: Fig. PD-7 Removing side bearing
description: Extracting side bearing from differential case using puller set ST3306S001.
mechanic_notes: Handle puller with care catching the edge of bearing inner race.

caption: Fig. PD-8 Measuring clearance
description: Feeler gauge inserted between rear face of side gear and thrust washer to measure backlash/clearance.
measurements_and_specs: Normal backlash or clearance: 0.1 to 0.2 mm (0.004 to 0.008 in)
mechanic_notes: Adjust side gear-to-pinion mate backlash or adjust clearance between rear face of side gear and thrust washer.

caption: Fig. PD-9 Tapping bolt head
description: Tapping bolt heads lightly with hammer while tightening in criss-cross pattern.
mechanic_notes: Tighten bolts in criss-cross fashion lightly tapping around bolt heads with a hammer.

caption: Fig. PD-10 Measuring bearing width
description: Measuring side bearing width with Master Gauge KV38101900 and Weight Block ST32501000 under a dial indicator.
mechanic_notes: Measure bearing width using Master Gauge KV38101900 and Weight Block ST32501000 prior to installation.

caption: Fig. PD-11 Installing side bearing cone
description: Press fitting side bearing cone on differential case with drift ST33230000 and adapter ST33061000.
mechanic_notes: Press fit side bearing cone on differential case using drift ST33230000 and adapter ST33061000.

caption: Fig. PD-12 Tightening drive pinion nut
description: Tightening drive pinion nut on dummy shaft using stopper ST31852000.
measurements_and_specs: Pinion nut torque: 17 to 20 kg-m (123 to 145 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten drive pinion nut to specified torque using Stopper ST31852000.

caption: Fig. PD-13 Measuring pinion preload
description: Measuring pinion bearing preload using torque wrench preload gauge ST3127S000.
measurements_and_specs: Pinion bearing preload (without oil seal): 10 to 13 kg-cm (8.7 to 11.3 in-lb)
mechanic_notes: Measure preload without oil seal inserted.

caption: Fig. PD-14 Measuring the clearance
description: Cross-sectional drawing showing height gauge ST31211000, dummy shaft ST31212000, spacer ST31851000, and collar ST31214000 setup for measuring clearance N.
mechanic_notes: Install Height Gauge ST31211000 on carrier with dummy shaft mounted to measure clearance N.

caption: Fig. PD-15 Adjusting pinion height
description: Using thickness gauge to measure clearance between height gauge ST31211000 and dummy shaft ST31212000.
mechanic_notes: Measure clearance N between tip end of height gauge and end surface of dummy shaft.

caption: Fig. PD-16 Variation number on drive pinion
description: Drive pinion head showing set number 41 and head number (H) stamped as +2.
measurements_and_specs: Variation figure in units of 1/100 mm
mechanic_notes: Head number (H) represents dimensional variation in 1/100 mm against standard measurement.

caption: Fig. PD-17 Pressing rear bearing cone
description: Pressing drive pinion rear bearing cone onto drive pinion using Base ST30901000.
mechanic_notes: Fit determined pinion height adjusting washer on drive pinion and press fit rear bearing cone.

caption: Fig. PD-18 Thickness of left and right shims
description: Section diagram of differential carrier highlighting dimensions A, B, C, D, G1, G2, T1, and T2 for calculating side retainer shim thicknesses.

callouts.A: Carrier left bore depth variation
callouts.C: Diff case left bearing seat variation
callouts.D: Diff case right bearing seat variation

mechanic_notes: Use formulas for T1 and T2 to determine proper shim pack thicknesses.

description: Side retainer showing stamped figures G1 and G2.
mechanic_notes: Figures stamped on side retainer flange.

caption: Fig. PD-22 Installing side retainer
description: Installing side retainer into differential carrier using Gear Carrier Side Retainer Guide ST33720000.
components: Gear Carrier Side Retainer Guide ST33720000
mechanic_notes: When installing retainers, take care that side bearing outer races are not damaged by roller.

caption: Fig. PD-23 The arrow mark on retainer
description: Orientation of side retainer showing upward pointing arrow mark.
mechanic_notes: Arrow mark on retainer must point in the prescribed direction as shown.

description: Dial indicator mounted to check backlash of ring gear against drive pinion.
measurements_and_specs: Ring gear backlash: 0.10 to 0.20 mm (0.0039 to 0.0079 in)
mechanic_notes: If backlash is below specified value, move shim from right to left; if over, move inversely.

caption: Fig. PD-25 Heel contact
description: Tooth contact pattern showing heel contact and correction arrow.
mechanic_notes: To correct, increase thickness of drive pinion adjusting washer to bring drive pinion closer to ring gear.

file: markdown/1978 280z FSM/diagrams/PD Propeller Shaft and Differential/fig_pd_26_toe_contact.png
caption: Fig. PD-26 Toe contact
description: Tooth contact pattern showing toe contact and correction arrow.
mechanic_notes: To correct, reduce thickness of drive pinion adjusting washer to move pinion away from ring gear.

file: markdown/1978 280z FSM/diagrams/PD Propeller Shaft and Differential/fig_pd_27_flank_contact.png
caption: Fig. PD-27 Flank contact
description: Tooth contact pattern showing flank contact and correction arrow.
mechanic_notes: Adjust in the same manner as toe contact (reduce thickness of washer).

description: Tooth contact pattern showing face contact and correction arrow.

mechanic_notes: Ideal contact pattern centered across gear tooth profile.

caption: Fig. PD-30 Removing companion flange
description: Standard puller attached to companion flange to extract it from pinion shaft.
mechanic_notes: Extract companion flange using a standard puller.

caption: Fig. PD-33 Measuring pinion preload
description: Measuring pinion preload with Preload Gauge ST3127S000 before disassembly.
mechanic_notes: Check preload before disassembling parts.

caption: Fig. PD-34 Measuring the backlash of ring gear and pinion
description: Dial indicator checking ring gear backlash on R200 carrier.

mechanic_notes: Always use flare nut torque wrench when tightening brake tubing connections.

caption: Fig. ST-1 Structural view of steering system
description: Structural perspective drawing showing the complete steering system layout in relation to the front suspension and steering column assembly.
mechanic_notes: Universal joints require no lubrication. Rubber coupling isolates road vibration.

caption: Fig. ST-2 Removing steering wheel
description: Removing steering wheel using Steering Wheel Puller ST27180001 threaded into the steering wheel hub.
mechanic_notes: Do not strike end of steering column shaft with a hammer. Striking shaft will damage bearing or collapsible shaft. Be careful not to damage cancel pole.

caption: Fig. ST-3 Sectional view of collapsible type steering
description: Sectional view of the steel ball collapsible steering column showing jacket tubes, bearing, spring, bracket, and rubber coupling.
mechanic_notes: Never apply undue stress to steering column in axial direction. Do not apply bending force during installation.

caption: Fig. ST-4 Removing rubber coupling bolt
description: Removing bolt securing the steering column shaft to the rubber coupling flange.
mechanic_notes: Disconnect steering column assembly from lower joint shaft at rubber coupling by removing bolt.

caption: Fig. ST-5 Removing jacket tube bracket securing bolts
description: Location of four bolts securing jacket tube bracket to the dash panel under the dashboard.
mechanic_notes: Remove bolts securing jacket tube bracket to dash panel.

caption: Fig. ST-6 Removing column clamp securing bolts
description: Removing two column clamp securing bolts while supporting the steering column assembly.
mechanic_notes: Support steering column at the top portion while removing two column clamp securing bolts.

caption: Fig. ST-7 Drawing out steering column assembly
description: Withdrawing the complete steering column assembly rearward into the passenger compartment.
mechanic_notes: Draw out steering column assembly from the interior side.

caption: Fig. ST-8 Loosening nut securing lower joint to pinion gear
description: Loosening pinch bolt nut clamping the lower steering joint to the pinion gear serration.
mechanic_notes: Take lower joint assembly out by loosening nut securing lower joint to pinion gear.

caption: Column shaft spring dimensions
description: Inspection dimension diagram of the column shaft spring showing outer diameter and free length.
measurements_and_specs: Load x length: 30 kg (66 lb) x 15 mm (0.59 in)
mechanic_notes: Replace spring if damaged or weakened.

caption: Fig. ST-9 Standard dimension between column clamp and the top end of lower jacket tube
description: Measuring dimension A between column clamp and the upper edge of lower jacket tube to inspect for collapse.
mechanic_notes: When jacket tube is crushed in a collision, dimension A becomes smaller.

caption: Fig. ST-10 Standard dimension B
description: Checking dimension B gap at the column clamp block to determine if the column has begun collapsing.
mechanic_notes: Standard B dimension is 0 mm (0 in). When jacket tube is crushed, dimension B becomes larger.

caption: Fig. ST-11 Inspecting steering wheel for axial play
description: Checking for 0 mm axial play along the column shaft axis at the steering wheel.
mechanic_notes: When steering jacket shaft is crushed, axial play occurs.

caption: Fig. ST-12 Installing steering column assembly
description: Installation diagram of steering column assembly detailing mounting points 1-7 and tightening torques A through F.
measurements_and_specs: A (Lower joint to rubber coupling): 2.3 to 2.7 kg-m (17 to 20 ft-lb)
B (Steering column clamp): 0.8 to 1.1 kg-m (5.8 to 8.0 ft-lb)
C (Jacket tube bracket to dash panel): 0.54 to 0.74 kg-m (3.9 to 5.4 ft-lb)
D (Rubber coupling securing bolt): 1.7 to 2.0 kg-m (12 to 14 ft-lb)
E (Lower joint to pinion gear): 4 to 5 kg-m (29 to 36 ft-lb)
F (Steering wheel nut): 4 to 5 kg-m (29 to 36 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Tighten bolts and nuts correctly and securely to specified torques. Make sure no undue stress is applied to rubber coupling.

caption: Fig. ST-13 Lining up slit with punched mark
description: Aligning universal joint slit with punch mark on the top end of the upper steering shaft.
mechanic_notes: Line up the slits of universal joints with the punched mark located on the top end of upper steering shaft.

caption: Fig. ST-14 Removing steering lock securing screws
description: Location of two headless self-shear screws securing the steering lock housing to the steering jacket tube.
mechanic_notes: Break two self-shear type screws with a drill or other proper tool. Upon installation, cut off screw heads.

caption: Fig. ST-15 Cross-section of rack-and-pinion and side rod assembly
description: Comprehensive cutaway illustration showing internal construction and callouts 1 through 21 of the rack-and-pinion steering gear and side rod linkage.
mechanic_notes: Backlash is held to 0 mm (0 in) by the retainer and retainer spring.

caption: Fig. ST-16 Loosening bolts securing lower joint assembly
description: Loosening coupling bolts connecting the lower joint shaft to the rubber coupling.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 1.7 to 2.0 kg-m (12 to 14 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Disconnect lower joint from steering column at rubber coupling.

caption: Fig. ST-17 Disconnecting lower joint from pinion
description: Disconnecting lower joint pinch clamp from the steering pinion shaft in the engine compartment.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4 to 5 kg-m (29 to 36 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Loosen bolt securing lower joint assembly to pinion, and then remove lower joint assembly from engine compartment.

caption: Fig. ST-18 Removing outer ball stud nut
description: Removing the side rod outer ball stud nut and cotter pin at the steering knuckle arm.
components: Side rod outer ball stud nut

callouts.1: Side rod outer ball stud nut

measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 5.5 to 7.6 kg-m (40 to 55 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Use Ball Joint Puller HT72520000 to detach ball studs from knuckle arms.

caption: Fig. ST-19 Removing bolts securing housing to suspension member
description: Removing bolts and lock nuts securing steering gear housing mounting brackets to the front suspension member.
measurements_and_specs: Bolt to welded nut tightening torque: 2.6 to 3.0 kg-m (19 to 22 ft-lb)
Lock nut tightening torque: 3.1 to 3.5 kg-m (22 to 25 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Remove bolts securing steering gear housing to suspension member.

caption: Fig. ST-20 Removing clamps
description: Removing gear boot clamp and dust cover clamp from the steering gear boot.
mechanic_notes: Remove both left and right clamps.

caption: Fig. ST-21 Disconnecting side rod assembly
description: Unthreading side rod inner socket assembly from the end of the rack shaft.
mechanic_notes: Do not disassemble side rod assembly.

caption: Fig. ST-22 Removing adjust lock nut
description: Loosening adjust lock nut and unthreading the retainer adjust screw from gear housing.
mechanic_notes: Remove retainer spring and steering gear retainer after removing screw.

caption: Fig. ST-23 Removing oil seal
description: Prying the pinion shaft oil seal out from the top of the gear housing.
mechanic_notes: Replace oil seal every disassembly.

caption: Fig. ST-24 Removing bolts and housing cover
description: Removing bolts, pinion housing cover, and pinion adjust shims from the steering gear housing.
mechanic_notes: Save shims for preload adjustment upon reassembly.

caption: Fig. ST-25 Pressing pinion bearing out of pinion shaft
description: Pressing the ball bearing off the pinion shaft using a hydraulic/mechanical press.
mechanic_notes: Properly support pinion to avoid damaging gear teeth.

caption: Fig. ST-26 Rack-and-pinion and side rod components
description: Exploded view diagram of complete steering rack, pinion gear, housing, boots, and side rod linkage with callouts 1 through 22.
mechanic_notes: Thoroughly clean all parts in cleaning solvent and blow dry before inspection.

caption: Fig. ST-27 Cross-section of outer ball joint
description: Internal cross-section of the outer tie rod ball joint showing callouts 1-6 and clearance specification.
measurements_and_specs: Clearance (axial play): 0.1 to 0.5 mm (0.004 to 0.020 in)
Swinging torque: 0.8 to 1.5 kg-m (5.8 to 10.8 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Measure swinging torque and axial play. Replace when values are not within specified range.

caption: Fig. ST-28 Side rod inner ball joint
description: Cross-sectional view of the inner side rod ball socket assembly with callouts 1-8.
mechanic_notes: Check inner ball joint for play. If ball stud is worn and axial play is excessive or joint is hard to swing, replace as a complete unit.

caption: Retainer spring dimensions
description: Dimensional sketch of retainer spring showing 21 mm (0.83 in) outside diameter and 19.6 mm (0.772 in) free length.
measurements_and_specs: Load x length: 20 kg (44 lb) x 16.3 mm (0.642 in)
mechanic_notes: Inspect spring free length and load before reassembly.

caption: Side rod spring dimensions
description: Dimensional sketch of side rod inner spring showing 8 mm (0.31 in) diameter and 19.0 mm (0.748 in) free length.
measurements_and_specs: Load x length: 40 kg (88 lb) x 17.0 mm (0.669 in)
mechanic_notes: Inspect side rod spring free length and load before reassembly.

caption: Fig. ST-29 Pressing bearing onto pinion gear
description: Pressing the ball bearing squarely onto the pinion gear shaft using an arbor press.
mechanic_notes: Press bearing onto pinion gear until firmly seated.

caption: Fig. ST-30 Measuring protruding portion of rack
description: Measuring protruding length of rack bar from housing end with vernier calipers to establish 87.4 mm (3.441 in) center.
mechanic_notes: Make sure that rack protrudes by the same amount from both ends of housing.

caption: Fig. ST-31 Inserting pinion assembly
description: Inserting pinion assembly into housing with the groove on the pinion serration directed upward while meshing teeth.
mechanic_notes: Properly mesh pinion with rack, and insert pinion assembly with the groove on the pinion serration part directed upward.

caption: Fig. ST-32 Measuring protruding portion of rack
description: Re-measuring rack protrusion from housing after pinion insertion to verify equal 87.4 mm (3.441 in) extension.
mechanic_notes: Make sure again of the length protruding from both the left and right sides of housing.

caption: Fig. ST-33 Fitting oil seal
description: Fitting the pinion shaft oil seal into the upper pinion bore of the gear housing.
mechanic_notes: Fit oil seal and make sure pinion rotates smoothly.

caption: Fig. ST-34 Locking retainer lock nut
description: Locking the retainer adjusting screw lock nut while holding the adjusting screw at the backed-off position.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 4 to 6 kg-m (29 to 43 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Fully tighten adjusting screw and then back it off 20 to 25 degrees. Tighten retainer lock nut to 4 to 6 kg-m.

caption: Fig. ST-35 Area to which liquid sealant is applied
description: Sectional view of the steering gear housing showing retainer float play (0.09 mm / 0.0035 in), callouts 1-12, and liquid sealant application area 'A'.
mechanic_notes: Apply suitable liquid sealant around lock nut at 'A'.

caption: Fig. ST-36 Measuring pinion rotary torque
description: Measuring pinion rotary torque using a torque gauge on the pinion serration shaft.
measurements_and_specs: Pinion rotary torque: Less than 20 kg-cm (17 in-lb)
mechanic_notes: Measure torque required to keep pinion and rack in motion.

caption: Fig. ST-37 Measuring rack force to pull
description: Measuring force required to pull rack at neutral position using a spring scale.
measurements_and_specs: Rack force to pull at neutral position: 14 to 17 kg (31 to 37 lb)
mechanic_notes: Re-adjust retainer adjusting screw as necessary to obtain proper torque.

caption: Fig. ST-38 Fitting side rod assembly to rack
description: Fitting side rod inner socket onto rack end with inner spring and spring seat.
mechanic_notes: Apply recommended grease to sliding surfaces of side rod inner socket and spring seat. Boot must be positioned toward ball stud end.

caption: Fig. ST-39 L-mark
description: Identification L-mark stamped on the left side rod assembly.
mechanic_notes: Side rod assembly for the left side has an L-mark. No mark is used for the right side.

caption: Fig. ST-40 Tightening lock nut
description: Tightening the inner socket lock nut against the rack end using two wrenches.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Screw inner socket portion until ball seat reaches rack end, then tighten lock nut securely.

caption: Fig. ST-41 Measuring swinging torque
description: Measuring swinging torque of the inner side rod ball joint with a spring scale.
measurements_and_specs: Swinging torque: 0 to 0.5 kg-m (0 to 3.6 ft-lb)
Axial play: 0 to 0.05 mm (0 to 0.0020 in)
mechanic_notes: Measure swinging torque and axial play upon completion of side rod assembly.

caption: Fig. ST-42 Measuring rack stroke
description: Measuring rack stroke from lock to lock using vernier calipers: 60.7 mm (2.390 in).
mechanic_notes: Verify full stroke of 60.7 mm (2.390 in) without interference.

caption: Fig. ST-43 Tightening boot clamp
description: Tightening boot clamp screw until the specified lug gap clearance of 2 mm (0.08 in) is reached.
mechanic_notes: Tighten inside boot clamp securely. Boot should be neither too inflated nor too elongated.

caption: Fig. ST-44 Adjusting side rod length
description: Sectional view of side rod length adjustment showing 37.9 mm (1.492 in) setting from stopper nut to ball stud center.
measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Adjust side rod length both left and right, and tighten steering stopper nuts to specified torque.

caption: Steering wheel puller (ST27180001 / J 25726)
description: Steering wheel puller tool ST27180001 (Kent-Moore J 25726) featuring puller yoke, center bolt, and two side anchor bolts.
mechanic_notes: Use to pull steering wheel hub off splined shaft without hammer impact.

caption: Ball joint remover (HT72520000)
description: Ball joint remover HT72520000 lever type tool with forcing screw and pivot pin marked PAT. P.
mechanic_notes: Insert between side rod ball stud and knuckle arm, tighten bolt to separate ball stud.

caption: Fig. WT-1 Tread wear indicator
description: Illustration of tire tread pattern and tread wear indicator bars located across tread grooves.

callouts.Tread wear indicator: Tread wear indicator bar across grooves

measurements_and_specs: Located at six places around tire circumference
mechanic_notes: When tread wears down to 1.6 mm (1/16 in) and wear indicator marks appear across the grooves, replace tires with new ones.

caption: Fig. WT-2 Abnormal tire wear
description: Four cross-sectional illustrations demonstrating abnormal tire tread wear patterns: toe-in/toe-out wear (feathered edge), overinflation wear (center), underinflation wear (both shoulders), and uneven wear (one side or irregular).

callouts.Toe-in or toe-out wear: Feathered edge wear pattern caused by excessive toe-in or toe-out
callouts.Overinflation wear: Center tread wear pattern caused by tire overinflation
callouts.Underinflation wear: Shoulder wear on both edges caused by tire underinflation or hard cornering
callouts.Uneven wear: One-sided or irregular wear caused by incorrect camber/caster, out-of-round drum, or unbalanced wheel

mechanic_notes: Inspect tread wear patterns to diagnose underlying wheel alignment, tire pressure, or suspension faults.

caption: Fig. WT-3 Tire rotation
description: Five-tire rotation pattern schematic diagram showing repositioning sequence for all four road wheels and the full-size spare tire.
mechanic_notes: Rotate tires periodically to equalize wear. Never include the foldable emergency spare tire in rotation.

caption: Fig. WT-4 Tire rotation
description: Four-tire rotation pattern schematic diagram showing rotation paths between front and rear wheels without spare tire.
mechanic_notes: Cross rear tires to opposite front positions; move front tires directly to rear positions. Do not include foldable spare.

caption: Fig. WT-5 Wheel nut
description: Comparison illustration showing two distinct wheel nut designs: sleeve-shank nut with washer for aluminum wheels only, and tapered acorn nut for steel wheels only.

callouts.For aluminum wheels only: Sleeve-type wheel nut with integral washer for aluminum wheels
callouts.For steel wheels only: Tapered acorn-seat wheel nut for steel wheels

mechanic_notes: Always use exclusive sleeve wheel nuts on aluminum wheels. Never interchange aluminum wheel nuts and steel wheel nuts. Never use aluminum wheel nuts on the foldable spare tire wheel.

caption: Fig. WT-6 Installing aluminum wheel
description: Two-step procedure diagram illustrating correct installation and shank alignment of aluminum wheels: loosely threading sleeve nuts onto hub bolts, then pulling the wheel back to center the shank into wheel bolt counterbores before progressively tightening in criss-cross order.

callouts.Screw nut onto hub bolt: Initial loose finger threading of sleeve nut onto hub bolt
callouts.Align nuts with bolt holes in wheel and: Pull wheel back to align sleeve nut shank into counterbored wheel hole, then tighten progressively

measurements_and_specs: Tightening torque: 8 to 10 kg-m (58 to 72 ft-lb)
mechanic_notes: Snugly tighten four nuts after wheel is positioned, pull wheel back slightly to align sleeve nuts into bolt hole counterbores, tighten finger-tight, then torque evenly with wrench in criss-cross pattern.

caption: Fig. WT-7 Wheel rim run-out check points
description: Cross-sectional illustration of wheel rim profile indicating balance weight clipping location and dial indicator checking points for measuring lateral and diametral rim runout.

callouts.Balance weight: Balance weight clipped to inner/outer rim flange edge
callouts.Checking points: Dial indicator stylus contact points on rim flange and bead seat for lateral and diametral runout measurement

measurements_and_specs: Lateral runout limit: Less than 1.0 mm (0.039 in) total indicator reading
Rim flange unbalance limit: 10 gr (0.35 oz)
mechanic_notes: Use dial gauge to inspect rim runout. Remove rubber/dust/sand with cloth on aluminum wheels (do not use sandpaper or wire brush). Place correct balance weights on inner edge of rim, not more than two per side.

caption: Wiring Diagram Sheet 1: Rear Combination Lamps, Cargo Area, Fuel Delivery, Defogger, and Center Console Harness
description: Full high-resolution electrical schematic of the 1978 Datsun 280Z rear body, tail lighting, fuel pump, fuel gauge sending unit, rear window defogger grid, auto antenna, audio speakers, center console switches, and harness connectors C-1 through C-10.
measurements_and_specs: Fuel tank sender resistance: approx. 10 to 80 ohms (Empty ~80Ω, Full ~10Ω)
Rear window defogger current draw: 12-15A (approx. 1 ohm total grid resistance)
mechanic_notes: All rear exterior lamps share the common body ground point in the rear hatch quarter panel; corroded or loose ground lugs cause dim lamps or cross-backfeeding into turn signal circuits.

caption: Rear Exterior Lighting, Fuel Pump, and Tank Sending Unit Sub-Circuit
description: Close-up detail of the rear lighting harness, license lamps, fuel pump power feed, and fuel level sender connections.
measurements_and_specs: Fuel level gauge resistance: 10 ohms (full) to 80 ohms (empty)
wiring_and_connections: G: Turn Signal RH & Fuel Pump feed
mechanic_notes: Verify fuel pump dedicated ground lug bolted to inner wheel arch frame to avoid intermittent engine stall under vibration.

caption: Wiring Diagram Sheet 2: Combination Meter, Steering Column Switches, Under-Dash Fuse Box, Relay Bracket, and HVAC System
description: Comprehensive schematic of the 1978 Datsun 280Z dashboard electrical wiring including the combination meter cluster (volts, fuel, temp, oil, tach, speedo, clock), steering column combination switch contact matrices, ignition switch, 12-circuit fuse block, relay bracket, and heater/AC controls.
measurements_and_specs: Seat belt warning timer interval: 4-8 seconds
Water temperature sender resistance: approx. 70-90Ω at 60°C (140°F), 20-30Ω at 100°C (212°F)
Oil pressure sender resistance: approx. 10-15Ω at 0 psi, 80-90Ω at 60 psi
mechanic_notes: When troubleshooting no-start or dead instrument clusters, inspect the ignition switch solder joints and the multi-pin connector C-6 for burnt pins caused by high current draw.

caption: Under-Dash Fuse Box, Ignition Switch, and Relay Bracket Sub-Circuit
description: Focused schematic showing the under-dash 12-circuit fuse box power distribution, ignition switch contact assignments, and relay bracket module pinouts.
measurements_and_specs: Fuse box continuous rating: 12V 10A-20A glass barrel fuses (SFE/AGC type)
mechanic_notes: Glass fuse clips in the 280Z fuse box are prone to corrosion and tension loss, causing voltage drop to EFI and ignition circuits.

caption: Wiring Diagram Sheet 3: Electronic Fuel Injection (EFI) ECU, Injector Harness, Dropping Resistor Bank, Air Flow Meter, and Power Distribution
description: Complete schematic of the 1978 Datsun 280Z Electronic Fuel Injection (EFI) circuitry showing the 35-pin ECU connector pinout, dropping resistor bank, 6 fuel injectors, cold start valve, thermotime switch, air regulator, throttle valve switch, air flow meter, battery, and fusible links.
measurements_and_specs: Dropping resistor individual branch resistance: 5.6 to 6.4 ohms
Fuel injector coil resistance: 2.0 to 3.0 ohms (low impedance)
Water temperature sensor resistance: 2.1 to 2.9 kΩ at 20°C (68°F); 0.27 to 0.38 kΩ at 80°C (176°F)
Air regulator heater coil resistance: approx. 70 to 80 ohms
Thermotime switch opening temperature: approx. 35°C (95°F); max cranking duration: 8-12 seconds
Air flow meter potentiometer resistance (pins 8-9): approx. 180 to 220 ohms
Fusible link capacities: Brown (0.3mm² / approx. 30A), Green (0.5mm² / approx. 40A), Black (1.25mm² / approx. 80A)
wiring_and_connections: BY (Starter cranking trigger: Pin 4 & cold start)
G (AFM fuel pump safety switch / injector power)
mechanic_notes: A poor ground connection at the intake manifold engine earth cluster is the #1 cause of bizarre EFI malfunctions, rich surging, or injector failure to fire.

caption: EFI Control Unit, Dropping Resistor, and Injector Bank Sub-Circuit
description: High-density detail of the 35-pin Bosch L-Jetronic ECU pin connections, dropping resistor connections, and 6-cylinder injector firing lines.
measurements_and_specs: Total injector resistance per cylinder: approx. 8.5Ω (2.5Ω injector + 6.0Ω resistor)
Injector pulse width: 2.0 to 9.0 milliseconds depending on load/temperature
mechanic_notes: Never connect 12V directly across the fuel injectors without the dropping resistor in series; doing so will immediately fry the delicate low-impedance injector solenoid windings.

caption: Wiring Diagram Sheet 4: Alternator, IC Regulator, Starter Motor, Electronic Distributor, Ignition Coil, Front Lighting, and Relay Bracket
description: Comprehensive schematic of the 1978 Datsun 280Z front engine compartment electrical system including alternator charging circuit, solid-state IC regulator, starter motor cranking circuit, ballast resistor, high-energy ignition coil, electronic distributor, front lighting, and under-hood diagnostic check connector.
components: Relay Bracket (EFI Main, Fuel Pump, A/C, Inhibitor)
measurements_and_specs: Alternator regulated voltage: 14.0 to 14.7V at 2,500 RPM
Starter motor no-load current: less than 90A at 11V (over 4,000 RPM)
Ballast resistor total resistance: approx. 1.5 to 1.7 ohms
Ignition coil primary winding resistance: approx. 1.0 to 1.3 ohms
Ignition coil secondary winding resistance: approx. 8.0 to 12.0 kΩ
Distributor magnetic pickup stator resistance: approx. 600 to 800 ohms
Spark plug gap: 0.8 to 0.9 mm (0.031 to 0.035 in)
wiring_and_connections: WR: Alternator BAT output / Battery feed
WB: Alternator field coil / IC regulator F
Y: Alternator neutral stator tap / IC regulator N
YW: IC regulator L terminal / Charge lamp
W: IC regulator S terminal (battery sense)
BR: Starter terminal R ballast bypass line
BW: Switched ignition 12V to ballast resistor
L: Ignition coil negative / TIU switching / Tach
G / R: Distributor magnetic pickup stator twisted pair
GB: Horn relay output to dual horns
YL: Oil pressure sending unit signal
YW: Water temperature sending unit signal
mechanic_notes: The ballast bypass line (Black/Red wire from starter terminal R to coil positive) is essential for cold starting; if disconnected, the engine will crank vigorously but will only catch or fire as the key is released back to the ON position.

caption: Alternator, IC Regulator, Starter, and Ignition Sub-Circuit
description: High-density detail of the alternator charging circuit with solid-state IC regulator, starter motor solenoid wiring, ballast resistor, high-tension ignition coil, and distributor.
mechanic_notes: Use the 6-pin Check Connector to test charging and ignition signals directly with a multimeter without puncturing harness insulation.

page_label: Zone 1: Front/Left — Headlights, Alternator, Starter & Ignition
caption: 1978 Datsun 280Z Factory Color Wiring Diagram — Zone 1: Front Chassis, Lighting, Alternator, Starter & Ignition
description: High-resolution schematic segment of the forward vehicle harness for 1978 Datsun 280Z. Shows complete wiring paths and color codes for dual sealed-beam headlamps, front combination turn/clearance lamps, horn circuits, alternator with integrated IC regulator, starter motor and solenoid, check connector, ignition distributor and coil, thermal transmitter, oil pressure sender, and transmission inhibitor/reverse switches.

callouts.A: Alternator Output Terminal (BAT)
callouts.S: Alternator Battery Voltage Sense Terminal / Starter Solenoid Terminal
callouts.L: Alternator Charge Lamp Terminal / Ignition Coil (-) Lead
callouts.R: Reverse Position Contact (Inhibitor Switch / Backup Lamp)

measurements_and_specs: Alternator Output: 12V 60A (Mitsubishi or Hitachi with integral IC regulator)
Starter Motor: 12V 1.4 kW reduction gear drive
Headlamps: Dual round sealed beams (12V 50W Low / 60W High)
Front Turn Signal Bulbs: 12V 27W (Single filament amber/clear)
Ignition Coil Primary Resistance: 0.84 to 1.02 Ω
Ignition Coil Secondary Resistance: 8.2 to 12.4 kΩ
Check Connector: 6-pin circular automotive test socket
wiring_and_connections: RW: Headlamp R.H. Low Beam feed
RB: Headlamp R.H. High Beam feed
RL: Headlamp L.H. Low Beam & clearance lamp bus
RY: Headlamp L.H. High Beam feed
R: Protected 12V headlamp power bus from fuses 4 & 5
GY: Right front turn signal wire
GB: Left front turn signal wire & Horn power feed
WR: Alternator main BAT charging output to fusible link
Y: Alternator voltage sense lead to fusible link
WB: Alternator L terminal to charge lamp & check connector
BY: Starter solenoid S trigger (12V START bus)
L: Ignition coil negative trigger pulse / tachometer signal
YB: Oil pressure sender variable resistance wire
YW: Thermal transmitter coolant temperature wire
LR: Air conditioning compressor clutch power feed
mechanic_notes: Ensure clean metal-to-metal contact at the front body ground lugs adjacent to each headlamp bucket. When installing replacement alternators, verify that the 'S' (Sense) and 'L' (Lamp) spade terminals are not reversed; reversing these terminals will prevent charging and cause continuous battery discharge through the regulator.

page_label: Zone 2: Engine Compartment, Relays, Fusible Links & EFI System
caption: 1978 Datsun 280Z Factory Color Wiring Diagram — Zone 2: Engine Compartment, Relays, Fusible Links & EFI System
description: Detailed schematic segment showing the complete L28E engine electrical management system. Includes Battery, fusible links (Green EFI link and Main fusible link block), Transistor Ignition Unit, Relay Bracket (Inhibitor, A/C, Fuel Pump Control, Fuel Pump, and EFI Main relays), 35-pin ECU harness, Dropping Resistor packs, Injectors 1 through 6, Air Flow Meter, Cold Start Valve, Thermotime Switch, Water Temperature Sensor, Air Regulator, Throttle Valve Switch, Wiper/Washer motors, and harness disconnects C-1 through C-9.
components: Harness Connectors C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-9

callouts.71 L: Switched 12V EFI power from main relay to ECU
callouts.72 R: Unswitched 12V battery standby from green fusible link
callouts.43/2: Common 12V power rail to dropping resistors

measurements_and_specs: EFI Fusible Link: Green (approx. 40A equivalent capacity)
Main Fusible Links: Brown (30A) and Black/Green (40A)
Dropping Resistor Resistance: 6.0 Ω ± 0.3 Ω per resistor section
Fuel Injector Coil Resistance: 2.5 to 3.0 Ω (low impedance EV1)
Water Temperature Sensor Resistance: 2.1 to 2.9 kΩ @ 20°C (68°F); 270 to 380 Ω @ 80°C (176°F)
Thermotime Switch Resistance: Below 14°C (57°F): 0 Ω (closed); Above 35°C (95°F): ∞ (open)
Air Regulator Resistance: Approx. 70 to 80 Ω heater element
wiring_and_connections: 72 R: Heavy Red wire from EFI fusible link to relay contact
71 L: Heavy Blue wire from EFI main relay to ECU pins
BW: Switched 12V ignition power to relay coils and transistor unit
L: Switched spark trigger wire from transistor unit to coil (-)
B: Engine ground returns for ECU, sensors, and relays
BY: Starter 50 cranking signal to ECU pin 4 and fuel pump control relay
G 21 / G 47: Cold start valve trigger leads
B 45 / B 46: Thermotime switch heater and contact leads
34 G / 48 G: Air regulator warmup heater power and ground
6, 7, 8, 9, 27 (Black): AFM potentiometer and intake air temp leads
GY / BW: High-current power feed to electric fuel pump
mechanic_notes: Never connect 12V directly to the fuel injector terminals without the 6-ohm dropping resistors in series; direct 12V will burn out the low-impedance injector coils in seconds. Check the heavy engine ground cluster on the intake manifold whenever intermittent EFI or misfire issues occur.

caption: Cutaway schematic of Bosch L-Jetronic Air Flow Meter (AFM) showing internal air bypass, damper chamber, flap, helical spring, and potentiometer housing
description: Schematic isometric cutaway diagram illustrating the complete internal air path and electro-mechanical mechanisms of the 280Z AFM. Incoming air from the air cleaner pushes against the pivoted measuring flap, which is counter-balanced by a damper plate moving within a closed damper chamber. An idle air bypass passage runs underneath the main measuring bore, regulated by an adjustable idle bypass needle screw. The intake air temperature sensor probe extends directly into the incoming airstream. The flap pivot shaft connects to the external electrical housing containing the helical return spring and potentiometer.

callouts.Helical spring: Helical return spring controlling flap resistance
callouts.Damper chamber: Sealed chamber damping intake air pulses
callouts.By-pass port: Idle air bypass channel beneath main air passage
callouts.To intake manifold: Air outlet to throttle body and intake manifold
callouts.Potentiometer: Potentiometer resistive board and wiper assembly
callouts.To EFI harness: Electrical connector socket to engine wiring harness

wiring_and_connections: To EFI harness connector (7-pin terminal block)
mechanic_notes: Bypass channel allows idle airflow to bypass the measuring flap. If the bypass screw is closed completely, backfire ('front fire') shock waves cannot vent through the passage and will bend or destroy the measuring flap.

caption: Characteristic curve of Air-Fuel Ratio (AFR) vs. Zirconia Oxygen Sensor output voltage showing steep transition at stoichiometric (14.7:1)
description: Graph plotting narrow-band zirconia O2 sensor output voltage (0 to 1.0 V) as a function of air-fuel ratio (11:1 to 18:1). Rich mixtures (12:1 - 14.5:1) produce a high sensor output of 0.90 - 0.95 V. At the stoichiometric ratio (~14.7:1), the voltage drops sharply from 0.9 V to ~0.15 V. Lean mixtures (15:1 - 18:1) produce a low output of 0.12 - 0.15 V.
mechanic_notes: Narrow-band O2 sensors exhibit extreme sensitivity right at 14.7:1 AFR but provide little resolution deep in rich or lean zones. Tuning the AFM without a wideband AFR meter relies on spark plug color reading, fingering responsiveness, and fuel economy measurement.

caption: Picture 1: AFM mechanical chamber showing locking screw for black wheel, factory glue blob, reference mark, counterweight, return-to-zero shock absorber, and fuel pump shut-off switch
description: Top view of the AFM mechanical and electrical compartment with black plastic dust cover removed. Shows the black notched adjustment wheel under tension of the clock spring, the upper-left locking screw with clamp washer, the factory glue blob, user-scribed reference marks on the gear teeth and aluminum casting, the cast zinc counterweight, the return-to-zero spring steel shock absorber, the fuel pump safety shut-off switch contacts, and the internal idle flow bypass adjuster passage.
components: Locking screw with clamp tab for black wheel
Return to zero shock absorber spring
Fuel pump shut-off switch leaf contacts

callouts.Locking Screw for Black Wheel: Upper left screw securing the toothed black spring tension wheel
callouts.Reference Mark: Red paint / scribe line marking original factory tooth position against casting
callouts.Glue Blob: Original factory silicone / glue seal locking black wheel; broken blob indicates prior tampering
callouts.Return to Zero shock absorber: Curved spring steel strip absorbing rotational inertia when flap snaps shut
callouts.Fuel Pump Shut Off Switch: Dual contact leaf switch actuated by wiper arm to cut fuel pump when engine stalls
callouts.Idle \"flow\" adjuster: Access port for internal idle bypass needle valve

measurements_and_specs: Return-to-zero shock absorber clearance: contacts ~5 mm (1/2 cm) before physical stop
Pin 36-39 fuel pump switch: Flap closed = infinite Ω (open), Flap cracked = 0 Ω (closed)
wiring_and_connections: Black wire leads from fuel pump safety switch to connector terminals (Pins 36 and 39)
mechanic_notes: WARNING: The black toothed wheel is under spring tension! Loosening the locking screw without holding firm finger pressure on the wheel will cause it to violently recoil ('sprong') and lose all factory calibration. ALWAYS scribe a reference mark on the tooth and case before loosening!

caption: Picture 2: AFM potentiometer board, wiper contacts, second glue blob locking screw, and carbon resistance trace
description: Detailed close-up of the ceramic potentiometer printed circuit board, dual-finger beryllium copper wiper arm, center pivot locking screw with glue blob #2, fuel pump switch actuator arm (silver nail-like pin), and curved carbon resistor trace. The wiper picks up an analog voltage signal ranging from approximately 2V (idle/closed) to 7V (wide-open throttle) and routes it to the ECU.
components: Silver nail-like actuator pin for fuel switch
Lead wires with spade push-on terminals

callouts.Potentiometer Carbon Trace: Curved resistive carbon track dividing voltage from ~2.0V to 7.0V
callouts.Wiper Contact: Dual flexible copper wiper fingers sweeping along the carbon track
callouts.Glue Blob: Glue blob #2 securing the center wiper pivot locking screw (adjusts 0V rest position and fuel pump switch arm)

measurements_and_specs: Wiper sweep voltage range: ~2.0 V to ~7.0 V
Wiper rest limit: Stops 2 to 4 mm before the end of the carbon trace (must not fall off trace)
wiring_and_connections: Spade terminals connected to internal base pins
mechanic_notes: Ensure the wiper does not overshoot the clockwise end of the carbon trace when the flap is closed; it must stop 2-4 mm before the edge. If the wiper shoots off the trace, it registers an open circuit (infinite resistance) and causes severe lean stumble or engine stall. Loosen the center pivot screw to recalibrate wiper rest position.

caption: Picture 3: Fingering check technique demonstrating manual deflection of the wiper counterweight towards 'More Fuel' (CCW) and 'Less Fuel' (CW)
description: Illustration of the live engine 'fingering' diagnostic check. With the AFM cover removed and engine running, a finger gently rotates the counterweight/wiper assembly clockwise (CW, toward 'Less Fuel' / lean) or counter-clockwise (CCW, toward 'More Fuel' / rich). Listening to engine RPM and smoothness at idle and at 3,000 RPM reveals whether the engine is starved for fuel (lean) or drowning in fuel (rich) before altering the black gear setting.

callouts.More Fuel: Counter-clockwise (CCW) rotation opens flap further, increasing output voltage and enriching mixture
callouts.Less Fuel: Clockwise (CW) rotation moves flap towards closed position, lowering output voltage and leaning mixture

measurements_and_specs: Idle wiper displacement: ~10 mm (1 cm) from rest
Stock calibrated AFM optimal fingering deflection: ~4 mm to rich (CCW) for maximum RPM
Test RPM levels: Idle (~750-800 RPM) and steady 3,000 RPM
Adjustment step increment: ~4 teeth per adjustment
mechanic_notes: Always verify ignition timing, mechanical cam timing, valve lash, vacuum leaks, and EFI coolant temperature sensor integrity BEFORE modifying AFM spring tension. False lean symptoms caused by vacuum leaks or over-advanced timing will lead to improper over-enrichment of the AFM.

caption: AFM idle air bypass adjustment screw removed from housing, showing adjustment slot, O-ring seal, and bypass port
description: View of the complete AFM cast aluminum body with the idle air bypass adjustment screw backed out of its threaded bore in the casting (highlighted with yellow circle). The screw features a slotted drive head, threaded shank, and rubber O-ring seal. Turning this screw CW restricts unmetered bypass airflow beneath the flap, enriching idle mixture; turning CCW increases bypass airflow, leaning idle mixture.
components: Threaded bypass adjustment bore in AFM body

callouts.Yellow circle: Slotted idle air bypass needle adjustment screw and threaded passage bore

measurements_and_specs: Turn Clockwise (CW): Restricts bypass passage -> Forces more air past flap -> Enriches idle mixture
Turn Counter-Clockwise (CCW): Opens bypass passage -> Bypasses more air around flap -> Leans idle mixture
wiring_and_connections: 7-pin female electrical socket integrated into side casting
mechanic_notes: CAUTION: Do not bottom out or completely seal the idle bypass screw. When an intake backfire ('front fire') occurs due to lean mixture, explosive pressure waves vent harmlessly through the bypass passage. If the screw is closed shut, the pressure wave has nowhere to go and will bend or fracture the delicate aluminum measuring flap.
